\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides scalable analysis and visualization of multilayer and multiplex networks in Python.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key features at a glance:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplex and multilayer network structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL for network queries} — first\sphinxhyphen{}class feature

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
17+ multilayer statistics and centrality measures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection (Louvain, Infomap, multilayer modularity)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk algorithms (Node2Vec, DeepWalk) for embeddings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Publication\sphinxhyphen{}ready visualizations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O with Arrow/Parquet support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Full NetworkX compatibility

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL: Query Networks Like SQL}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex DSL lets you query networks using intuitive SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like syntax or a type\sphinxhyphen{}safe Python builder API. Both return the same results; pick the style that fits your workflow.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} String DSL: Simple and readable}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ AND degree \PYGZgt{} 5 }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Builder API: Type\PYGZhy{}safe with autocompletion}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL is \sphinxstylestrong{perfect for}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interactive network exploration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rapid prototyping

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Educational purposes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Production pipelines

\chapter{Quickstart}
\label{\detokenize{index:quickstart}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get started in three steps: install, build a tiny multilayer network, and inspect it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Step 1 — Install

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Step 2 — Create a multilayer network

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{visualize\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Expected output

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Number of nodes: 6
Number of edges: 3
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts reflect per\sphinxhyphen{}layer node identities (Alice/Bob/Carol each appear in two layers). Your totals will differ if you change the edge list. The visualization opens in a Matplotlib window and colors nodes by layer.

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{overview/part_intro:overview}}\label{\detokenize{overview/part_intro::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Welcome to py3plex! This section provides a high\sphinxhyphen{}level introduction to the library and its capabilities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is py3plex?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is a Python library for analyzing and visualizing multilayer and multiplex networks. Unlike traditional network analysis tools that treat all relationships uniformly, py3plex preserves the distinct types of connections between entities—whether they’re social ties, biological interactions, or transportation links.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why py3plex?}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Native multilayer support:} Built for networks with multiple relationship types from the start.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL:} Query networks intuitively with SQL\sphinxhyphen{}inspired syntax.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Production\sphinxhyphen{}ready:} High\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O, sklearn\sphinxhyphen{}style pipelines, and comprehensive testing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Research\sphinxhyphen{}proven:} Used in peer\sphinxhyphen{}reviewed publications.

\end{itemize}

\subsection{What is py3plex?}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:what-is-py3plex}}\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is a Python library for scalable analysis and visualization of multilayer and multiplex networks.


\subsubsection{Key Features}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:key-features}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use py3plex when you need to keep relationship types distinct while still running end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end analysis and visualization.


\paragraph{Multilayer Network Structures}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:multilayer-network-structures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides native support for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex networks} — Same nodes across multiple layers (e.g., social networks with friendship, collaboration, and family ties).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Heterogeneous networks} — Different node types across layers (e.g., author\sphinxhyphen{}paper\sphinxhyphen{}venue networks).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal networks} — Networks that evolve over time; edges and nodes can carry timestamps or time windows.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All network types are first\sphinxhyphen{}class citizens with consistent APIs.


\paragraph{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL for Network Queries}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:sql-like-dsl-for-network-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query networks using SQL\sphinxhyphen{}inspired syntax that stays close to plain language:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} String DSL: readable and concise}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ AND degree \PYGZgt{} 5 }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Or use the type\sphinxhyphen{}safe builder API for IDE autocompletion and refactoring support:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Builder API: with IDE autocompletion}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL makes complex network analyses readable and maintainable.


\paragraph{Comprehensive Algorithm Suite}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:comprehensive-algorithm-suite}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex includes multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific algorithms such as:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community detection:} Louvain, Infomap, multilayer modularity.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Centrality measures:} Multilayer PageRank, betweenness, versatility.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Random walks:} Node2Vec, DeepWalk for network embeddings.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dynamics:} SIR/SIS epidemic models, diffusion processes.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All algorithms handle multilayer structure natively without flattening.


\paragraph{Publication\sphinxhyphen{}Ready Visualizations}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:publication-ready-visualizations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create professional network diagrams with:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatic multilayer layouts that preserve layer separation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Customizable styling and colors.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Support for large networks (1000+ nodes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Export to multiple formats (PNG, PDF, SVG).

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{High\sphinxhyphen{}Performance I/O}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:high-performance-i-o}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apache Arrow/Parquet support for large datasets.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NetworkX compatibility for easy integration.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple input formats (edge lists, adjacency matrices, JSON) without forcing layer flattening.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{What Makes py3plex Unique?}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:what-makes-py3plex-unique}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Native Multilayer Representation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike tools that flatten multilayer networks into single\sphinxhyphen{}layer graphs, py3plex preserves the multilayer structure throughout the analysis pipeline. This leads to more accurate results for multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific properties.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Pair Abstraction}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex represents multilayer networks using node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs: a node in layer A is distinct from the same node in layer B. This clean abstraction enables:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific queries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer and intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edge differentiation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

py3plex is designed for both research and production:

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{When to Use py3plex?}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:when-to-use-py3plex}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is ideal when you have:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple relationship types} between entities (e.g., email + phone + in\sphinxhyphen{}person contacts)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Heterogeneous networks} with different node types (e.g., users, posts, hashtags)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal networks} where relationships change over time

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Need for layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific analysis} (e.g., comparing community structure across layers)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you only need single\sphinxhyphen{}layer network analysis, NetworkX or igraph might be simpler choices.


\subsubsection{Related Projects}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:related-projects}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX:} py3plex builds on NetworkX for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{igraph:} Faster for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks, but limited multilayer support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pymnet:} Pure Python multilayer library, different API design

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{graph\sphinxhyphen{}tool:} High performance, but steeper learning curve

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex balances ease of use with multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific functionality.

\subsection{Key Use Cases}
\label{\detokenize{overview/key_use_cases:key-use-cases}}\label{\detokenize{overview/key_use_cases::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex models systems where the same entities interact through many
relationship types (layers). Each node may appear in multiple layers, and
interlayer edges let you model transfers or couplings between contexts. Below
are common domains, what the layers represent, and the kinds of questions you
can answer.


\subsubsection{Social Networks}
\label{\detokenize{overview/key_use_cases:social-networks}}

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\subsection{Multilayer Networks in 2 Minutes}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:multilayer-networks-in-2-minutes}}\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer network} represents systems where entities can be connected through multiple types of relationships simultaneously.


\subsubsection{The Core Idea}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:the-core-idea}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the real world, relationships are rarely uniform. Consider a group of researchers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They \sphinxstylestrong{co\sphinxhyphen{}author papers} (collaboration network)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They \sphinxstylestrong{cite each other} (citation network)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They \sphinxstylestrong{attend conferences} together (social network)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They may \sphinxstylestrong{share funding} (grant network)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A single\sphinxhyphen{}layer network captures only one of these relationships. A multilayer network keeps every relationship type separate while linking the same entity across layers.


\subsubsection{Visual Intuition}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:visual-intuition}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Single\PYGZhy{}layer network (e.g., only co\PYGZhy{}authorship):

Alice \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} Bob \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} Carol
          |
        David

Multilayer network (co\PYGZhy{}authorship + citations):

Layer 1 (Co\PYGZhy{}authorship):
Alice \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} Bob \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} Carol
          |
        David

Layer 2 (Citations):
Alice \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Bob \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Carol
          ↓
        David

Inter\PYGZhy{}layer connections:
Alice in Layer 1 ↔ Alice in Layer 2 (same person)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Key Concepts}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:key-concepts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep these quick definitions in mind while you read the rest.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers}
Each layer represents one relationship type (e.g., friendship, collaboration, family).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs}
Every node is represented per layer. In py3plex, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(\textquotesingle{}Alice\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}friends\textquotesingle{})}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(\textquotesingle{}Alice\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}work\textquotesingle{})}} are distinct node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs that can be linked. Counts in py3plex statistics refer to these pairs, not just the unique entity names.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges}
Connections within a single layer (e.g., Alice friends with Bob).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges}
Connections between layers, typically tying the same entity across layers (e.g., Alice in the friendship layer ↔ Alice in the collaboration layer). They can also connect different entity types when modeling interactions between layers.


\subsubsection{Types of Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:types-of-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex networks}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same nodes across all layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different edge types per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example: Social media (same users, different platforms)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Heterogeneous networks}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different node types in different layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example: Author\sphinxhyphen{}Paper\sphinxhyphen{}Venue networks

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal networks}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layers represent time slices

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same nodes and edge types, but edges appear/disappear over time

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example: Communication networks over days/weeks

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Why Multilayer Matters}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:why-multilayer-matters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Information is lost when flattening}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you merge all layers into a single network, you lose critical information:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Which type of relationship connects two nodes?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Are communities consistent across layers or layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
How do different relationship types interact?

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{New properties emerge}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer networks have properties that don’t exist in single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node versatility:} How many layers a node participates in, and whether its role shifts by layer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer correlation:} Whether connections in layer A are predictive of connections in layer B.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer communities:} Groups that span multiple relationship types.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplexity:} Number of different relationship types between two nodes.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Real\sphinxhyphen{}World Impact}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:real-world-impact}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example: Disease spread}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In epidemic modeling, people interact through:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Household contacts (high transmission rate)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Workplace contacts (medium rate, large reach)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Social gatherings (variable)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A single\sphinxhyphen{}layer model that averages these interactions will give incorrect predictions. A multilayer model preserves the structure and transmission dynamics of each contact type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example: Social influence}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A person might be influential on Twitter (many followers) but not on LinkedIn (few connections). Flattening these into a single “social network” loses this nuance.


\subsubsection{Quick Example in Code}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:quick-example-in-code}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create multilayer network}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges in different layers}

    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Collaboration layer}

\subsubsection{When to Use Multilayer Analysis?}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:when-to-use-multilayer-analysis}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use multilayer networks when:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✅ You have \sphinxstylestrong{multiple relationship types} between entities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✅ The \sphinxstylestrong{type of relationship matters} for your analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✅ You want to \sphinxstylestrong{preserve layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific structure}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✅ You’re studying \sphinxstylestrong{cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer effects} (e.g., how Twitter activity affects LinkedIn connections)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Stick with single\sphinxhyphen{}layer when:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
❌ All relationships are of the same type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
❌ Relationship type doesn’t affect your analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
❌ You only care about aggregate connectivity

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Basic Installation}

\paragraph{Install from PyPI (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:install-from-pypi-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We recommend using \sphinxhref{https://docs.astral.sh/uv/}{uv}%
\begin{footnote}[4]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
\sphinxnolinkurl{https://docs.astral.sh/uv/}
%
\end{footnote} for fast, reliable Python environment management:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install uv (if not already installed)}
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}LsSf\PYG{+w}{ }https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }sh

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create and activate virtual environment}
uv\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }.venv
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }.venv/bin/activate\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} On Windows: .venv\PYGZbs{}Scripts\PYGZbs{}activate}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install py3plex}
uv\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative (traditional pip):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }pip
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This installs the core py3plex library with all required dependencies.


\paragraph{Install from Source}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:install-from-source}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For development or to access the latest features:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Using uv (recommended):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
uv\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }.venv
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }.venv/bin/activate
uv\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Using pip:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }pip
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}e}} flag installs in editable mode, so changes to the source code are immediately available.

For a containerized environment with all dependencies pre\sphinxhyphen{}installed, use Docker:

docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}v\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{PWD}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}:/data\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }selftest

\subsubsection{Optional Dependencies}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:optional-dependencies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex offers several optional feature sets that can be installed separately. Quote extras (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"py3plex{[}extra{]}"}}) to avoid shell globbing on some terminals.


\paragraph{Advanced Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:advanced-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install Infomap for advanced overlapping community detection:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}py3plex[infomap]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Additional Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:additional-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install extra community detection algorithms (Louvain, cdlib):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}py3plex[algos]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Advanced Visualization}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:advanced-visualization}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install Plotly and igraph for interactive and advanced visualizations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}py3plex[viz]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Apache Arrow Support}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:apache-arrow-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install pyarrow for high\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O with Arrow/Parquet formats:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}py3plex[arrow]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Arrow format typically provides faster read/write operations and better compression than JSON/CSV for large graphs.
See \DUrole{xref}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{../user\_guide/io\_and\_formats}}} for details on using Arrow format.


\paragraph{Multiple Extras}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:multiple-extras}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install multiple feature sets at once:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}py3plex[infomap,viz,algos,arrow]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Workflow Configuration Support}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:workflow-configuration-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install YAML support for config\sphinxhyphen{}driven workflows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}py3plex[workflows]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Development Installation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For contributors, install with development tools (testing, linting):

\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create environment and install}

\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }.venv/bin/activate
uv\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}.[dev]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Using Makefile:}

\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }pip

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{System Requirements}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:system-requirements}}

\paragraph{Python Version}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:python-version}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex requires Python 3.8 or higher. We test on:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.8

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.9

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.10

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.11

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.12

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Platform Support}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:platform-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform and tested on:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Linux} (Ubuntu 20.04, 22.04)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{macOS} (macOS 11, 12, 13)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Windows} (Windows Server 2019, 2022)

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:core-dependencies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These are automatically installed with py3plex:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{networkx\textgreater{}=2.5}} \sphinxhyphen{} Graph data structures and algorithms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{numpy\textgreater{}=1.19.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Numerical computing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scipy\textgreater{}=1.5.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Scientific computing and sparse matrices

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pandas}} \sphinxhyphen{} Data manipulation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matplotlib\textgreater{}=3.3.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Static visualization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scikit\sphinxhyphen{}learn\textgreater{}=0.24.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Machine learning utilities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tqdm\textgreater{}=4.40.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Progress bars

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdflib\textgreater{}=6.0.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Semantic web support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bitarray\textgreater{}=2.0.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Efficient boolean arrays

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gensim\textgreater{}=4.0.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Topic modeling utilities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seaborn\textgreater{}=0.11.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Statistical plotting

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cython\textgreater{}=0.29.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Extension compilation support

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{External Binaries (Optional)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:external-binaries-optional}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex no longer bundles external binaries; install them separately when needed to keep the base package lightweight and licensing clear.


\paragraph{Infomap Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:infomap-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For advanced community detection using Infomap:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 1:} Use the bundled Python implementation (recommended):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}py3plex[infomap]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 2:} Download the C++ binary from the official source:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Website: \sphinxurl{https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Follow platform\sphinxhyphen{}specific installation instructions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative:} Use the built\sphinxhyphen{}in Louvain algorithm (no binary needed):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{best\PYGZus{}partition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Node2Vec Embeddings}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:node2vec-embeddings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For Node2Vec node embeddings, use pure Python alternatives:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 1:} Use pecanpy (fast parallel implementation):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }pecanpy
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 2:} Use node2vec package:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }node2vec
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 3:} Use py3plex’s built\sphinxhyphen{}in random walk implementation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{general}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{walkers}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{node2vec\PYGZus{}walk}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{generate\PYGZus{}walks}
\PYG{n}{walks} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{generate\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{80}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Virtual Environment Setup}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:virtual-environment-setup}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We strongly recommend using a virtual environment to prevent dependency conflicts:


\paragraph{Using uv (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:using-uv-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://docs.astral.sh/uv/}{uv}%
\begin{footnote}[5]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
\sphinxnolinkurl{https://docs.astral.sh/uv/}
%
\end{footnote} is a fast Python package installer and resolver:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install uv}
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}LsSf\PYG{+w}{ }https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }sh

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create virtual environment}
uv\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }.venv

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Activate (Linux/macOS)}
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }.venv/bin/activate

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Activate (Windows)}
.venv\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}S}cripts\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}a}ctivate

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install py3plex inside the environment}
uv\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Using venv}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:using-venv}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create virtual environment}
python3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Activate (Linux/macOS)}
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env/bin/activate

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Activate (Windows)}
py3plex\PYGZhy{}env\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}S}cripts\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}a}ctivate

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install py3plex inside the environment}
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }pip
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Using conda}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:using-conda}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create conda environment}
conda\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}n\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{python}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{3}.10

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Activate}
conda\PYG{+w}{ }activate\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install py3plex}
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Common Installation Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:common-installation-issues}}

\paragraph{Issue: “No module named ‘numpy’”}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-no-module-named-numpy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install numpy first (preferably in a virtual environment):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Issue: Compilation errors on Windows}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-compilation-errors-on-windows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install Visual C++ Build Tools:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download from: \sphinxurl{https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install “Desktop development with C++”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restart your shell, then retry installation

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Issue: “Permission denied” on Linux/macOS}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-permission-denied-on-linux-macos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 1:} Use a virtual environment:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env/bin/activate\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} On Windows: py3plex\PYGZhy{}env\PYGZbs{}Scripts\PYGZbs{}activate}
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }pip
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} Use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}user}} flag if you cannot use venv:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Issue: Old version installed}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-old-version-installed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Check the installed version and upgrade if needed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\subsection{Quick Start Tutorial}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min:quick-start-tutorial}}\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get started with py3plex in just a few minutes. This tutorial shows you the essential concepts through three focused examples.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{📓 Executable Examples}

\subsubsection{Example 1: Load and Query (1 min)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min:example-1-load-and-query-1-min}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load a built\sphinxhyphen{}in dataset and run a simple query:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{datasets}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}aarhus\PYGZus{}cs}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1. Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}aarhus\PYGZus{}cs}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2. Run query \PYGZhy{} find nodes with degree \PYGZgt{} 5}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 3. Inspect result}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filters nodes with more than 5 connections

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes degree centrality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Common Issues and Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:common-issues-and-troubleshooting}}\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Quick fixes for frequent issues when getting started with py3plex. Work through the sections in order (installation \(\rightarrow\) data loading \(\rightarrow\) visualization \(\rightarrow\) performance \(\rightarrow\) algorithms). Apply one fix at a time, then rerun your script before trying the next so you know which change helped.


\subsubsection{Installation Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:installation-issues}}

\paragraph{“No module named ‘numpy’”}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:no-module-named-numpy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Import error when trying to use py3plex (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ModuleNotFoundError}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install numpy first (preferably in a virtual environment to avoid system\sphinxhyphen{}wide changes). Upgrading pip often avoids build warnings:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }pip
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }numpy

\paragraph{File Not Found Errors}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:file-not-found-errors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FileNotFoundError}} when loading networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 1:} Confirm the file exists and your working directory is correct (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{os.getcwd()}} often differs from the script directory):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Current directory:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{getcwd}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{File exists:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exists}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} Use an absolute path to avoid ambiguity:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}path} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/absolute/path/to/data.edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 3:} Build a path relative to the script location (avoids brittle working\sphinxhyphen{}directory assumptions):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}

\PYG{n}{script\PYGZus{}dir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dirname}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{abspath}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nv+vm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}file\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{data\PYGZus{}path} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{join}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{script\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{network.edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{data\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Empty or Malformed Networks}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:empty-or-malformed-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Network loads but has no nodes or edges (zero counts).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Confirm the file contents and chosen \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} match. Pick the loader that matches your columns and delimiter:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For simple edge lists (source target)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For multilayer edge lists (source target layer)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Always verify after loading}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If counts are still zero:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inspect the first few lines for the expected number of columns and delimiters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ensure header rows are skipped or removed before loading.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check that the file is not empty (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{os.path.getsize}}).

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{network.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dpi}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{150}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{bbox\PYGZus{}inches}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{tight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install Arrow support}
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}py3plex[arrow]\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Quotes required on some shells}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{io}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{read}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{write}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load faster from Arrow}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} Process in chunks or use subnetworks for testing:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\paragraph{Community Detection Returns Trivial Results}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:community-detection-returns-trivial-results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Each node in its own community or all nodes in one community (degenerate partition).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Adjust algorithm parameters and randomness, then compare partitions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Try different resolution parameters}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,}    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Lower = fewer, larger communities}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{,}    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Higher = more layer consistency}
    \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Random Walk or Embedding Errors}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:random-walk-or-embedding-errors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Random walk or Node2Vec functions fail.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Ensure the graph is connected before running walks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check connectivity}
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{o+ow}{not} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}connected}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}undirected}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Warning: Network is not connected}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get largest component}
    \PYG{n}{largest} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{connected\PYGZus{}components}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}undirected}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{key}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create subgraph}
    \PYG{n}{subgraph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{largest}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the subgraph for embedding or random walk routines if the full network is disconnected. Re\sphinxhyphen{}attach results to the full graph only after inspecting coverage.


\subsubsection{Docker Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:docker-issues}}

\paragraph{Docker Build Fails}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:docker-build-fails}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Docker build fails or takes very long.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Clear Docker cache (removes all unused images and build layers) and rebuild:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }system\PYG{+w}{ }prune\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}a
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}cache\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Cannot Access Files in Docker}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:cannot-access-files-in-docker}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Docker container can’t see your data files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Mount volumes correctly so container paths resolve:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Mount current directory}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}v\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nb}{pwd}\PYG{k}{)}:/data\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }/data/network.edgelist

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} On Windows (PowerShell)}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}v\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{PWD}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}:/data\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }/data/network.edgelist
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Adjust the command after the image name to match your workflow (for example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex load /data/network.edgelist \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}info}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Docker Usage Guide}}}} for complete Docker documentation.

\subsection{How to Load and Build Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:how-to-load-and-build-networks}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Create multilayer networks from scratch or load them from files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} Basic Python knowledge. For conceptual background, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{The py3plex Core Model}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Start from the format you already have: add edges directly if you are prototyping, or load from files/dataframes when your data is already tabular. The examples below always build a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network}} object you can reuse in later steps.


\subsubsection{Creating Networks from Scratch}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:creating-networks-from-scratch}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use these options when you want to assemble a small network interactively or generate synthetic structures.


\paragraph{Method 1: Add Edges Directly (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:method-1-add-edges-directly-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The simplest approach—nodes are created automatically when you add edges.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create empty network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges in list format}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Format: [source\PYGZus{}node, source\PYGZus{}layer, target\PYGZus{}node, target\PYGZus{}layer, weight]}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Verify}
\PYG{n}{stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Number of nodes: 6
Number of edges: 4
Number of unique node IDs (across all layers): 4
Nodes per layer:
  Layer \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}: 3 nodes
  Layer \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}: 3 nodes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Method 2: Add Nodes First}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:method-2-add-nodes-first}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For more control over node attributes and to ensure edges only connect existing nodes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add nodes explicitly (as node\PYGZhy{}layer tuples)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges between existing nodes}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Method 3: Use Dictionary Format}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:method-3-use-dictionary-format}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For networks with edge attributes and mixed field names (timestamps, types, etc.):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges with custom attributes}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{timestamp}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}15}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{interaction\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{message}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.5}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{timestamp}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}16}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{dict}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Loading Networks from Files}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:loading-networks-from-files}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use file\sphinxhyphen{}based loading when your data already lives on disk. Edge lists remain the most compact choice; JSON is convenient for richer metadata. Each snippet builds the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network}} interface shown above.


\paragraph{Load Edge Lists}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:load-edge-lists}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most common format: one edge per line. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multiedgelist}} loader expects
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source source\_layer target target\_layer weight}} (weight defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} if omitted).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{File format (stored as datasets/simple\_multiplex.txt in the repository):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Alice friends Bob friends 1.0
Bob friends Carol friends 1.0
Alice colleagues Bob colleagues 1.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Load it:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Option 1: Load from repository file}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/simple\PYGZus{}multiplex.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Option 2: Create from data directly (recommended for examples)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Load from Pandas DataFrame}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:load-from-pandas-dataframe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert tabular data to networks (each row becomes an edge). Use separate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer}} columns if endpoints belong to different layers.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pandas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pd}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Your data}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{row} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{iterrows}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{weight}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} If your dataframe has ``source\PYGZus{}layer`` and ``target\PYGZus{}layer`` columns,}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pass those instead of a single ``layer`` column:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} network.add\PYGZus{}edge(}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}     row[\PYGZsq{}source\PYGZsq{}], row[\PYGZsq{}source\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZsq{}],}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}     row[\PYGZsq{}target\PYGZsq{}], row[\PYGZsq{}target\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZsq{}],}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}     weight=row[\PYGZsq{}weight\PYGZsq{}]}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} )}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Load from JSON}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:load-from-json}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For complex networks with metadata (define both nodes and edges explicitly). Keep
edge dictionaries consistent: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_layer}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_layer}}, plus any other attributes you want to preserve.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{json}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load JSON}
\PYG{k}{with} \PYG{n+nb}{open}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.json}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{r}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{json}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Assuming JSON structure: \PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}edges\PYGZdq{}: [...], \PYGZdq{}nodes\PYGZdq{}: [...]\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attributes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Optionally, add nodes first if your JSON includes node attributes}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} for node in data.get(\PYGZsq{}nodes\PYGZsq{}, []):}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}     network.add\PYGZus{}nodes([(node[\PYGZsq{}id\PYGZsq{}], node[\PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZsq{}])])}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Load from NetworkX}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:load-from-networkx}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert existing single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks by assigning a default layer name. If the
original graph has edge attributes, pass them through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_edge}} as keyword
arguments.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Existing NetworkX graph}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{karate\PYGZus{}club\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to multilayer (single layer)}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{v} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Loading with Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer Edges}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:loading-with-inter-layer-edges}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To represent the same entity across layers, connect node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuples that share the same node identifier:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Intra\PYGZhy{}layer edges}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Inter\PYGZhy{}layer edges (same person across layers)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{interlayer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{interlayer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Common Patterns}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:common-patterns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pick a template that matches your data model, then extend it with attributes as needed.


\paragraph{Pattern 1: Social Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:pattern-1-social-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple relationship types between same people:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}

    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{linkedin}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{linkedin}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{twitter}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{twitter}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{authors}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Paper1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{papers}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{authors}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Paper2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{papers}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
