        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{t}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}15T10:00:00}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Point in time}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{t\PYGZus{}start}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}15}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}     \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Time range}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{t\PYGZus{}end}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}20}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{dict}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Verifying Your Network}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:verifying-your-network}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After loading, verify the structure to catch layer/weight mistakes early:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Basic stats}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Layers: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Total nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check a specific layer}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}
\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Friends layer: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Query Zoo is organized around common multilayer analysis tasks:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic Multilayer Exploration} — Understand layer statistics and structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Hubs} — Find nodes that are important across multiple layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer Similarity} — Measure structural alignment between layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community Structure} — Detect and analyze multilayer communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex PageRank} — Compute multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}aware centrality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Robustness Analysis} — Assess network resilience to layer failures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Advanced Centrality Comparison} — Identify versatile vs specialized hubs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Edge Grouping and Coverage} — Analyze edges across layer pairs with top\sphinxhyphen{}k and coverage

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer Algebra Filtering} — Use layer set algebra for flexible layer selection

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Paths with Algebra} — Find paths while excluding certain layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Null Model Comparison} — Statistical significance testing against null models

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Bootstrap Confidence Intervals} — Estimate uncertainty in centrality measures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}Aware Ranking} — Rank nodes considering variability across layers

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All examples use small, reproducible multilayer networks from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/dsl\_query\_zoo/datasets.py}} module with fixed seeds so you can match the outputs shown here.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Running the Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All query functions are available in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/dsl\_query\_zoo/queries.py}}.
To run all queries and generate outputs:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{python} \PYG{n}{examples}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{dsl\PYGZus{}query\PYGZus{}zoo}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{run\PYGZus{}all}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{py}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Test the queries with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pytest} \PYG{n}{tests}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{test\PYGZus{}dsl\PYGZus{}query\PYGZus{}zoo}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{py}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{1. Basic Multilayer Exploration}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:basic-multilayer-exploration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} You’ve loaded a multilayer network and want to quickly understand its structure. Which layers are densest? How many nodes and edges does each layer have?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Compute basic statistics per layer using the DSL.


\paragraph{Query Code}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:query-code}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{query\PYGZus{}basic\PYGZus{}exploration}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{Network}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Summarize layers: node counts, edge counts, and average degree per layer.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Refactored: single DSL query over all layers + pandas groupby, no explicit}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    for\PYGZhy{}loop over layers.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    This query demonstrates basic multilayer exploration by computing}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    fundamental statistics for each layer independently. This is typically}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    the first step in multilayer analysis to understand the structure}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    and identify layers with different connectivity patterns.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Why it\PYGZsq{}s interesting:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Reveals which layers are denser or sparser}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Identifies layers that might be hubs of activity}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Shows structural diversity across the multilayer network}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    DSL concepts demonstrated:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} SELECT nodes from all layers in one shot}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Computing degree per layer}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Vectorized aggregation by layer}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Args:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        network: A multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network instance}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Returns:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        pd.DataFrame with columns: layer, n\PYGZus{}nodes, n\PYGZus{}edges, avg\PYGZus{}degree}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}       \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} all layers in one shot}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{columns}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{n\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{n\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{avg\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} One row per (node, layer), so size() is node count}
    \PYG{n}{stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{groupby}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
          \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{agg}\PYG{p}{(}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Find top\sphinxhyphen{}k central nodes per layer, then identify which nodes appear in multiple layers’ top lists.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Find nodes that are consistently central across multiple layers.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Refactored: one DSL query across all layers + pandas grouping, no explicit}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    per\PYGZhy{}layer for loop.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    This query identifies \PYGZdq{}super hubs\PYGZdq{} \PYGZhy{} nodes that maintain high centrality}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    across different layers. These nodes are particularly important because}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    they serve as connectors across different contexts or domains.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Why it\PYGZsq{}s interesting:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Reveals nodes with consistent importance across contexts}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Useful for identifying key actors in multiplex social networks}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Helps understand cross\PYGZhy{}layer influence and information flow}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    DSL concepts demonstrated:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Single query across all layers}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Computing betweenness centrality}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Vectorized top\PYGZhy{}k selection per layer using groupby}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Coverage analysis (nodes appearing in multiple layers)}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Args:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        network: A multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network instance}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        k: Number of top nodes to select per layer}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Returns:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        pd.DataFrame with nodes and their centrality scores per layer}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rename}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{columns}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{node}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Top\PYGZhy{}k by betweenness within each layer (vectorized)}
    \PYG{n}{df\PYGZus{}sorted} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
                               \PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{topk} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df\PYGZus{}sorted}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{groupby}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{k}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Count how many layers each node appears in as a top\PYGZhy{}k hub}
    \PYG{n}{coverage} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{topk}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{groupby}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{node}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
            \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nunique}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
            \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{reset\PYGZus{}index}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{topk}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{merge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{coverage}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{on}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{node}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
            \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
                         \PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{node}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
                      \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}

\subsubsection{3. Layer Similarity}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:layer-similarity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} How similar are different layers structurally? Do they serve redundant or complementary roles?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Compute degree distributions per layer and measure pairwise correlations.


\paragraph{Query Code}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id5}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{query\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}similarity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{Network}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Compute structural similarity between layers based on degree distributions.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Refactored: single DSL query + pivot, no explicit loops over layers/nodes.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    This query measures how similar different layers are in terms of their}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    connectivity patterns. Layers with similar degree distributions likely}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    serve similar structural roles in the multilayer network.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Why it\PYGZsq{}s interesting:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Identifies redundant or complementary layers}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Helps understand layer specialization}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Can inform layer aggregation or simplification decisions}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    DSL concepts demonstrated:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Single query across all layers}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Pivot table to create node × layer matrix}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Correlation between layers via .corr()}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Args:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        network: A multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network instance}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Returns:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        pd.DataFrame: Pairwise correlation matrix of layer degree distributions}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build node × layer degree matrix: rows = nodes, cols = layers}
    \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}matrix} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pivot\PYGZus{}table}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{columns}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{values}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{fill\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}

         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{communities}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{reset\PYGZus{}index}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{columns} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{size}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{avg\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

    \PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rename}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{columns}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{dominant\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{size}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{avg\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{dominant\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}

\subsubsection{5. Multiplex PageRank}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:multiplex-pagerank}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Standard PageRank treats each layer independently. How do we compute importance considering the full multiplex structure?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Compute PageRank per layer, then take the average across layers as a simplified multiplex score. (True multiplex PageRank uses supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrices.)


\paragraph{Query Code}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id13}}

\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{query\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}pagerank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{Network}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Approximate multiplex PageRank by aggregating layer\PYGZhy{}specific scores.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    NOTE: This is still a *simplified* multiplex PageRank approximation}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    (average of layer\PYGZhy{}specific PageRank). For true Multiplex PageRank, wrap}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    the dedicated algorithm from the algorithms module (see query\PYGZus{}true\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}pagerank).}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Refactored: single DSL query over all layers + vectorized pandas aggregation,}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    no explicit for\PYGZhy{}loop over layers.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Why it\PYGZsq{}s interesting:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Approximates node importance across the entire multiplex}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} More informative than single\PYGZhy{}layer centralities}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Efficient computation via aggregation}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Good starting point before using full multiplex algorithms}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    DSL concepts demonstrated:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Single query across all layers}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Computing PageRank}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Vectorized aggregation and pivot tables}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Ranking nodes by multilayer importance}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Args:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        network: A multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network instance}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Returns:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        pd.DataFrame with nodes ranked by multiplex PageRank scores}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pagerank}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rename}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{columns}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{node}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Aggregate across layers: average PR, total degree}
    \PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}pr} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}

    \PYG{n}{baseline\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{baseline\PYGZus{}df}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation:} Removing the bus layer causes 46.67\% connectivity loss — it’s the most critical layer. Walking is least critical (only 6.67\% loss), indicating good redundancy from other transport modes. Connectivity loss is computed from total degree (divided by 2 for undirected edges), so it assumes undirected layers.
The reported loss compares baseline total degree to the degree after removing a layer; for undirected networks total degree is twice the number of edges.

\subsubsection{7. Advanced Centrality Comparison}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:advanced-centrality-comparison}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Different centralities capture different notions of importance. Which nodes are “versatile hubs” (high in many centralities relative to the best scorer) vs “specialized hubs” (high in only one)?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Compute multiple centralities, normalize them, and classify nodes by how many centralities place them in the top tier.

\subsubsection{8. Edge Grouping and Coverage}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:edge-grouping-and-coverage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} You want to analyze which edges (connections) are important within and between layers. Which edges consistently appear in the top\sphinxhyphen{}k across different layer\sphinxhyphen{}pair contexts?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Use the new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.per\_layer\_pair()}} method to group edges by (src\_layer, dst\_layer) pairs, then keep the top\sphinxhyphen{}k edges per pair. (Add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.coverage(...)}} if you later need to filter across groups.)

\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id25}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Analyze edges across layer pairs with grouping and coverage.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    This query demonstrates the powerful new edge grouping capabilities}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    introduced in DSL v2. It groups edges by (src\PYGZus{}layer, dst\PYGZus{}layer) pairs}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    and analyzes edge distribution across layer pairs.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Why it\PYGZsq{}s interesting:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Reveals how connections are distributed within and between layers}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Shows which layer pairs have more connectivity}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Identifies edges that appear across multiple layer contexts}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Essential for understanding cross\PYGZhy{}layer edge patterns}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    DSL concepts demonstrated:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} .per\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}pair() for edge grouping}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} .coverage() for cross\PYGZhy{}group filtering}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Edge\PYGZhy{}specific grouping metadata}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Query: Get edges grouped by layer pair}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Why It’s Interesting}

\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation:} The query reveals edge distribution across layer pairs. Each intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (e.g., social\sphinxhyphen{}social, work\sphinxhyphen{}work) contains up to k=3 edges. The sample dataset has only intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges; inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs would appear if your network contains cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections. The family layer has sparser connectivity overall, so only three family edges remain after limiting.
When no sort key is provided, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_k}} keeps edges by their existing order; specify a weight to make the selection explicitly score\sphinxhyphen{}based.


\paragraph{DSL Concepts Demonstrated}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id28}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.per\_layer\_pair()}} — Group edges by (src\_layer, dst\_layer) pairs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.top\_k(k, "weight")}} — Select top\sphinxhyphen{}k items per group

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.coverage(mode="at\_least", k=2)}} — Optional cross\sphinxhyphen{}group filtering

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.group\_summary()}} — Get aggregate statistics per group

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge\sphinxhyphen{}specific grouping metadata in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QueryResult.meta{[}"grouping"{]}}}

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{New in DSL v2}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge grouping and coverage are new features that parallel the existing node
grouping capabilities. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.per\_layer\_pair()}} for edges and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.per\_layer()}}
for nodes. Both support the same coverage modes and grouping operations.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subsubsection{9. Layer Algebra Filtering}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:layer-algebra-filtering}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} You want to query specific subsets of layers using set operations. For instance, you might want to analyze “all layers except coupling layers” or “the union of biological layers.”

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Use the LayerSet algebra with set operations (union, intersection, difference, complement) for expressive layer filtering.

\paragraph{Why It’s Interesting}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id30}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expressive layer selection} — Combine layers using set operations rather than listing them individually

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reusable layer groups} — Define named layer groups for consistent reuse across queries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exclude infrastructure layers} — Easily filter out meta\sphinxhyphen{}layers like coupling layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complex filter expressions} — Build sophisticated layer filters with union, intersection, difference

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Example Output}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id31}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The query returns a dictionary with multiple DataFrames showing different layer selection strategies:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No Coupling Layers:} All layers except the coupling layer (useful for excluding meta\sphinxhyphen{}layers)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Bio Layers:} Named group containing biological layers (ppi | gene | disease)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Intersection:} Nodes appearing in both social AND work layers

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complement:} Complement of coupling layer (equivalent to * \sphinxhyphen{} coupling)


\paragraph{DSL Concepts Demonstrated}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id32}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"* \sphinxhyphen{} coupling"{]}}} — Layer difference: all layers except coupling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"social \& work"{]}}} — Layer intersection: nodes in both layers

\subsubsection{12. Bootstrap Confidence Intervals}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:bootstrap-confidence-intervals}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} When analyzing centrality in multilayer networks, how stable are the measurements? Do nodes maintain consistent importance across layers, or is their centrality highly variable?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Analyze cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer variability to estimate uncertainty in centrality measures, identifying nodes with stable vs fragile importance.

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get base centrality values from multiple layers}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{metric}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{groupby}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{metric}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{agg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{std}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{count}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{reset\PYGZus{}index}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute relative variability (coefficient of variation)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} This shows which nodes have stable vs variable centrality across layers}
    \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{relative\PYGZus{}variability}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{std}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1e\PYGZhy{}10}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Identify nodes present in multiple layers}

        \PYG{n}{on}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{how}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{left}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{suffixes}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZus{}across\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Sort by mean centrality across layers}
    \PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{[}
        \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{metric}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{std}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{relative\PYGZus{}variability}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer\PYGZus{}coverage}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{drop\PYGZus{}duplicates}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{13. Uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}Aware Ranking}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:uncertainty-aware-ranking}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Traditional rankings order nodes by a single metric (e.g., max centrality). But what if a node has high centrality in one layer but low in others? How do you account for consistency vs peak performance?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Compare multiple ranking strategies—by maximum value, by mean across layers, and by consistency (low variability)—to make uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}aware decisions.


\paragraph{Query Code}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id45}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{query\PYGZus{}uncertainty\PYGZus{}aware\PYGZus{}ranking}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{Network}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Rank nodes considering variability across layers.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Traditional rankings use single\PYGZhy{}layer metrics. This demonstrates}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    uncertainty\PYGZhy{}aware ranking by considering how node importance varies}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    across different layers in a multilayer network.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Why it\PYGZsq{}s interesting:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Avoids over\PYGZhy{}confident conclusions from single\PYGZhy{}layer analysis}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Identifies nodes with consistent vs inconsistent importance}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Useful for decision\PYGZhy{}making in multilayer contexts}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Shows how cross\PYGZhy{}layer analysis changes conclusions}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    DSL concepts demonstrated:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Cross\PYGZhy{}layer metric aggregation}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Variability\PYGZhy{}aware node ranking}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{} Comparing consistency vs peak performance}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Args:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        network: A multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network instance}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Returns:}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        pd.DataFrame comparing different ranking strategies}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get betweenness with cross\PYGZhy{}layer variability}
    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{query\PYGZus{}bootstrap\PYGZus{}confidence\PYGZus{}intervals}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{metric}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Traditional ranking: order by max value across layers}

    \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{rank\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}max}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{map}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}per\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{method}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{min}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{rank\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}consistency}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{consistency\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{method}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{min}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{relative\PYGZus{}variability}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
         \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{rank\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}max}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{rank\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{rank\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}consistency}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{rank\PYGZus{}change}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{drop\PYGZus{}duplicates}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Why It’s Interesting}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:id46}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Beyond single\sphinxhyphen{}layer analysis} — Consider multilayer context in rankings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Consistent vs peak performers} — Identify nodes with stable vs specialized importance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Decision\sphinxhyphen{}making under uncertainty} — Choose ranking strategy based on use case

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reveals ranking sensitivity} — See how rankings change with different strategies

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Practical implications} — Different strategies matter for different applications

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Choosing a Ranking Strategy}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{High\sphinxhyphen{}stakes decisions:} Use consistency ranking to avoid nodes with variable performance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exploratory analysis:} Use max ranking to find peak performers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{General purpose:} Use mean ranking for balanced assessment

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Large rank changes:} Investigate why nodes rank differently across strategies

\end{itemize}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{examples}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl\PYGZus{}query\PYGZus{}zoo}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{queries}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{query\PYGZus{}basic\PYGZus{}exploration}

\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}social\PYGZus{}work\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Adapting Queries to Your Data}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:adapting-queries-to-your-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All queries are designed to work with any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} object. To adapt:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Replace the dataset}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load your own network}
\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{mydata.edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edgelist\PYGZus{}mx}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run any query}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{query\PYGZus{}cross\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}hubs}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Adjust parameters}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query\_cross\_layer\_hubs}} — Number of top nodes per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_zoo:datasets}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Three multilayer networks are provided:

\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%

\sphinxstylestrong{social\_work\_network}
\begin{itemize}

\sphinxstylestrong{communication\_network}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Nodes:} 10 people (Manager, Dev team, Marketing, Support, HR)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Structure:} Star topology in email, distributed in chat/phone

\sphinxstylestrong{transport\_network}
\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Nodes:} 8 locations (CentralStation, ShoppingMall, Park, etc.)

\subsection{How to Compute Network Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:how-to-compute-network-statistics}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Calculate metrics that describe the structure of your multilayer network—quick counts, per\sphinxhyphen{}layer comparisons, node\sphinxhyphen{}level rankings, and multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific measures.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} A loaded network (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}). Examples reuse the same small network unless noted.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Imports used below

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most snippets rely on the DSL helpers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where to find this data

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples in this guide use:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Programmatically created networks} (recommended for self\sphinxhyphen{}contained examples)

\subsubsection{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:layer-specific-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understand how structure varies per layer before aggregating the network.


\paragraph{Compute Per\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Density}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:compute-per-layer-density}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Density compares observed edges \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}} to the maximum possible edges among \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} nodes in one layer.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes and edges in this layer}
    \PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Density = actual edges / possible edges}
    \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} undirected}
    \PYG{n}{density} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Layer }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: density = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{density}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For directed layers, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_edges = n * (n \sphinxhyphen{} 1)}} instead (ordered pairs).

    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: avg degree = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{active\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{p}{)}

\subsection{How to Run Community Detection on Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:how-to-run-community-detection-on-multilayer-networks}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} This guide demonstrates how to apply community detection algorithms to multilayer networks and interpret their results. Community detection identifies \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesoscale structure}—groups of nodes that are more densely connected internally than to the rest of the network. In multilayer networks, communities can exist within single layers, span multiple layers, or emerge from inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling patterns. This analysis is essential for understanding functional modules, organizational structure, and hierarchical clustering in complex systems.

\subsubsection{Quick Start: Louvain Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:quick-start-louvain-algorithm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Louvain?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Louvain algorithm (Blondel et al., 2008) is a fast, greedy method that optimizes \sphinxstyleemphasis{modularity}, defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q = \frac{1}{2m} \sum_{ij} \left[ A_{ij} - \frac{k_i k_j}{2m} \right] \delta(c_i, c_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(A_{ij}\) is the adjacency matrix, \(k_i\) is node degree, \(m\) is total edges, and \(\delta(c_i, c_j)=1\) if nodes \(i,j\) are in the same community. Higher \(Q\) indicates stronger community structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{How it works:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize: each node starts in its own community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node, compute \(\Delta Q\) from moving to each neighbor’s community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Move the node to the community with maximum positive \(\Delta Q\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregate: collapse communities into super\sphinxhyphen{}nodes and repeat

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stop when no further improvement is possible

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Time complexity:} \(O(n \log n)\) for sparse networks

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load multilayer network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run Louvain (operates on flattened network by default)}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyze results}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{collections}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Counter}
\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Counter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific: Multilayer Louvain}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:multilayer-specific-multilayer-louvain}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What makes multilayer community detection different?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Standard Louvain treats a multilayer network as a single flattened graph, losing layer identity. \sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Louvain} (Mucha et al., 2010) optimizes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{multilayer modularity}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q_{\text{multi}} = \frac{1}{2\mu} \sum_{ij\alpha\beta} \left[ \left(A^\alpha_{ij} - \gamma^\alpha \frac{k_i^\alpha k_j^\alpha}{2m_\alpha}\right)\delta_{\alpha\beta} + \delta_{ij}\omega_{\alpha\beta} \right] \delta(g_{i\alpha}, g_{j\beta})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A^\alpha_{ij}\): adjacency in layer \(\alpha\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k_i^\alpha\): degree (or strength) of node \(i\) in layer \(\alpha\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(m_\alpha\): total edge weight in layer \(\alpha\) (\(2m_\alpha = \sum_{ij} A_{ij}^\alpha\))

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma^\alpha\): resolution parameter for layer \(\alpha\) (default 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\omega_{\alpha\beta}\): inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength (default 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta_{ij}=1\) if \(i=j\) (inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges connect same node across layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta_{\alpha\beta}=1\) if \(\alpha=\beta\) (restricts intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer term)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta(g_{i\alpha}, g_{j\beta})=1\) if node \(i\) in layer \(\alpha\) and node \(j\) in layer \(\beta\) are in the same community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\mu\): total weight in the supra\sphinxhyphen{}network (\(2\mu = \sum_\alpha 2 m_\alpha + \sum_{\alpha\neq\beta}\omega_{\alpha\beta}\))

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key insight:} The coupling term \(\omega_{\alpha\beta}\) controls whether communities span layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω = 0:} Layers are independent \(\rightarrow\) separate communities per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω \(\rightarrow\) \(\infty\):} Strong coupling \(\rightarrow\) communities span all layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{0 \textless{} ω \textless{} \(\infty\):} Partial coupling \(\rightarrow\) communities can span some layers

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Infomap Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:infomap-algorithm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Infomap?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Infomap (Rosvall \& Bergstrom, 2008) uses information theory to find communities by minimizing the \sphinxstyleemphasis{map equation}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}L(M) = q_\curvearrowright H(Q) + \sum_{i=1}^m p_{\circlearrowright}^i H(P^i)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(q_\curvearrowright\): probability of switching between modules (inter\sphinxhyphen{}module flow)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(H(Q)\): entropy of module codebook

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(p_{\circlearrowright}^i\): probability of staying within module \(i\) (intra\sphinxhyphen{}module flow)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(H(P^i)\): entropy of nodes within module \(i\)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key insight:} Infomap simulates a random walker and finds communities that compress the \sphinxstyleemphasis{description length} of the walker’s trajectory. Communities are regions where the walker gets “trapped” for extended periods.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros/cons vs. Louvain:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros:} Often finds better communities for flow\sphinxhyphen{}based systems (e.g., citation networks, web graphs)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cons:} Requires external binary (not pure Python), slower than Louvain, harder to interpret parameters

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Installation:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Infomap requires the standalone binary from \sphinxurl{https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Download and install}
wget\PYG{+w}{ }https://www.mapequation.org/downloads/Infomap.zip
unzip\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap.zip
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap
make
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }cp\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap\PYG{+w}{ }/usr/local/bin/infomap

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Or install Python wrapper (alternative)}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }infomap
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic usage:}

\subsubsection{Label Propagation}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:label-propagation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Label Propagation?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Label propagation (Raghavan et al., 2007) is an extremely fast, near\sphinxhyphen{}linear time algorithm that works by iteratively assigning each node to the most common community among its neighbors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Algorithm:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize: each node gets a unique label (community ID)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{For t=1 to T iterations:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\alph}{enumii}{enumiii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Randomize node order

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node \(i\):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Count neighbor labels: \(n_c = |\{j \in N(i) : c_j = c\}|\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assign \(c_i = \arg\max_c n_c\) (ties broken randomly)

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stop when labels stabilize or max iterations reached

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Time complexity:} \(O(m)\) per iteration (linear in edges)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros/cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros:} Very fast, scales to millions of nodes, no parameters to tune

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cons:} Non\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic (order\sphinxhyphen{}dependent), lower quality than Louvain/Infomap, may not converge

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Query Communities with DSL}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:query-communities-with-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL) to query and analyze community\sphinxhyphen{}detected networks efficiently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL provides a declarative, SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like interface for querying multilayer networks. After detecting communities, you can use DSL queries to filter nodes by community membership, compute community\sphinxhyphen{}level statistics, and extract subnetworks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection results (e.g., from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{louvain\_communities()}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Familiarity with DSL basics (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Query Multilayer Graphs with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL}}}} for full tutorial)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{DSL Basics for Communities}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:dsl-basics-for-communities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{String Syntax \sphinxhyphen{} SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like queries:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network and detect communities}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{py3plex/datasets/\PYGZus{}data/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Attach community labels as node attributes}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} DSL Query: Find nodes in community 0}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE community=0}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{nodes\PYGZus{}in\PYGZus{}comm0} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in community 0: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes\PYGZus{}in\PYGZus{}comm0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{nodes\PYGZus{}in\PYGZus{}comm0}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Calculate averages}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Community\PYGZhy{}level statistics:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Community}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZlt{}12}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Nodes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZlt{}8}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Avg Degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZlt{}12}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Avg Betweenness}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZlt{}18}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{sorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

\paragraph{Complex DSL Workflows}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:complex-dsl-workflows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multi\sphinxhyphen{}step analysis: Find bridge nodes between communities:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Bridge nodes: high betweenness + connect multiple communities}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} First, compute betweenness}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Identify potential bridges (high betweenness)}
\PYG{n}{bridges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.01}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Threshold}
\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Potential bridge nodes (betweenness \PYGZgt{} 0.01): }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{bridges}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For each bridge, check which communities its neighbors belong to}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{betw} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{sorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{bridges}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{key}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get neighbors}
    \PYG{n}{neighbors} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{neighbors}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{neighbor\PYGZus{}comms} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{neighbors}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: betweenness=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{betw}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.6f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{, connects }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{neighbor\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ communities}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Compare Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:compare-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different algorithms optimize different objective functions and may produce different community structures. \sphinxstylestrong{Comparing multiple algorithms} helps validate findings and understand algorithm\sphinxhyphen{}specific biases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Metrics for comparing partitions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)}: Measures similarity adjusted for chance
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}, where 1 = perfect agreement, 0 = random

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adjusted for cluster size imbalance

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Normalized Mutual Information (NMI)}: Information\sphinxhyphen{}theoretic similarity
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}0, 1{]}, where 1 = perfect agreement

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Symmetric, handles different number of communities well

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Variation of Information (VI)}: Distance metric (lower = more similar)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}0, \(\infty\){]}, where 0 = identical partitions

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Quality Metrics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:quality-metrics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why quality metrics matter:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quality metrics help you:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compare algorithms} objectively

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tune parameters} (e.g., choosing optimal \(\omega\) in multilayer Louvain)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Validate results} (high Q suggests real structure, not random fluctuations)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Detect overfitting} (too many tiny communities = over\sphinxhyphen{}segmentation)

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Compute Modularity}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:compute-modularity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Single\sphinxhyphen{}layer modularity:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For flattened networks, use the Newman\sphinxhyphen{}Girvan modularity:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q = \frac{1}{2m} \sum_{ij} \left[ A_{ij} - \frac{k_i k_j}{2m} \right] \delta(c_i, c_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{modularity}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Detect communities}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to NetworkX for modularity calculation}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Calculate modularity}
\PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{modularity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{weight}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Modularity Q: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Interpretation}
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.7}\PYG{p}{:}

\PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.4}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Interpretation: Strong community structure}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Interpretation: Moderate community structure}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Interpretation: Weak or no community structure}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

For multilayer networks, use the generalized modularity that accounts for inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run multilayer Louvain}

    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Calculate multilayer modularity}
\PYG{n}{Q\PYGZus{}multi} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Multilayer modularity Q: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{Q\PYGZus{}multi}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modularity resolution:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Modularity has a \sphinxstylestrong{resolution limit}: in undirected graphs it struggles to detect communities much smaller than roughly \(\sqrt{2m}\) (with \(m\) edges). The resolution parameter \(\gamma\) can help:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Modularity vs. resolution:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Multilayer Quality Metrics (Guardrails)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:multilayer-quality-metrics-guardrails}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For multilayer community detection, two specialized quality metrics serve as \sphinxstylestrong{guardrails} against degenerate partitions:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Replica Consistency (RC)}: Measures whether replicas of the same node across layers are assigned to the same community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer Entropy (H)}: Measures the balance of community sizes within each layer, averaged across layers

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What are guardrails?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Guardrails are metrics that detect pathological partitions but are not primary optimization objectives. They ensure that:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Communities respect node identity across layers (RC)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Partitions are not degenerate giant clusters or extreme fragmentation (H)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Replica Consistency:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: For each node v with replicas in L\_v layers ({\color{red}\bfseries{}|L\_v|} ≥ 2):
\begin{align*}\!\begin{aligned}
RC(v) = \frac{2}{|L_v|(|L_v|-1)} \sum_{\ell_i < \ell_j} 1[c(v,\ell_i) = c(v,\ell_j)]\\
RC = \frac{1}{|\{v: |L_v|\ge 2\}|} \sum_v RC(v)\\
\end{aligned}\end{align*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RC ranges from 0 to 1:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RC = 1.0}: All replicas of each node have the same community (perfect coherence)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RC = 0.0}: No agreement (random assignment)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RC ∈ (0,1)}: Partial consistency

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer Entropy:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: For each layer ℓ with C\_ℓ communities:
\begin{align*}\!\begin{aligned}
H_\ell = -\sum_i p_i^\ell \log(p_i^\ell) / \log(|C_\ell|)\\
H = \text{mean}_\ell(H_\ell), \quad \text{clipped to } [0.1, 0.9]\\
\end{aligned}\end{align*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
H ranges from 0.1 to 0.9 (clipped):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{H ≈ 0.9}: Balanced communities in all layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{H ≈ 0.1}: Giant cluster or extreme fragmentation (degenerate)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{H ∈ (0.1,0.9)}: Normal partition

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Usage example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}quality\PYGZus{}metrics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}
