\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{When to use these metrics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RC}: When node identity across layers is important (e.g., same protein in different interaction types)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{H}: To detect degenerate partitions (giant clusters or extreme fragmentation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Both}: As sanity checks after multilayer community detection

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{AutoCommunity}: These are included by default; they contribute \textasciitilde{}22\% total weight in the default metric set

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Typical ranges:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RC \textgreater{} 0.8}: Excellent replica consistency

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RC ∈ {[}0.5, 0.8{]}}: Good consistency

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RC \textless{} 0.5}: Poor consistency (investigate layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific communities)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{H \textgreater{} 0.7}: Well\sphinxhyphen{}balanced communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{H ∈ {[}0.3, 0.7{]}}: Normal range

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{H \textless{} 0.3}: Degenerate partition (too few or too many communities)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance characteristics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RC}: O(Σ\_v {\color{red}\bfseries{}|}L\_v|\textasciicircum{}2) where L\_v is layers per node (efficient count\sphinxhyphen{}based implementation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{H}: O({\color{red}\bfseries{}|assignments|}) linear in node\sphinxhyphen{}layer assignments

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Both}: Fast enough for large networks (\textless{} 1 second for 10,000 node\sphinxhyphen{}layers)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Label\sphinxhyphen{}permutation invariance:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
RC is \sphinxstylestrong{label\sphinxhyphen{}permutation invariant}: it only compares community labels within each node across layers. Different algorithms can produce arbitrary label numbering, and RC will still work correctly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Summary of metrics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modularity (Q):} Overall quality, general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Coverage:} Simple interpretability (\% internal edges)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance:} Balances true positives and true negatives

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Conductance:} Community boundary quality (per\sphinxhyphen{}community)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Null model:} Statistical significance test

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recommendation:} Always report modularity + at least one other metric to get a complete picture.


\subsubsection{CLI Cross\sphinxhyphen{}Reference (Optional)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:cli-cross-reference-optional}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides command\sphinxhyphen{}line tools for quick community detection without writing Python code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic usage:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Detect communities using Louvain (default algorithm)}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }louvain\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }communities.json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Using Infomap (requires Infomap binary installed)}
py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }community\PYG{+w}{ }datasets/network.edgelist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }infomap\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }communities.json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Using Label Propagation (fast for large networks)}
py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }community\PYG{+w}{ }datasets/network.edgelist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }label\PYGZus{}prop\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }communities.json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} With custom resolution parameter for Louvain}
py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }community\PYG{+w}{ }datasets/network.edgelist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }louvain\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}resolution\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}.5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }communities.json
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Available algorithms:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{louvain}}: Fast Louvain method (default) \sphinxhyphen{} optimizes modularity on flattened network

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{infomap}}: Infomap algorithm \sphinxhyphen{} requires Infomap binary (\sphinxurl{https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/})

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
The current CLI \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{community}} command operates on flattened networks. For multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific community detection (with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling), use the Python API with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{louvain\_multilayer()}} as shown in the examples above. Future CLI versions may add multilayer support.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Viewing results:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After running the CLI command, you can analyze the JSON output:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} View community statistics}
py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }community\PYG{+w}{ }network.edgelist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }louvain
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Output printed to console if no \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output specified}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

For full CLI documentation, see \DUrole{xref}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{../tutorials/cli\_usage}}} or \DUrole{xref}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{../deployment/cli\_usage}}}.

\sphinxstylestrong{Further reading:}

\sphinxstylestrong{Algorithms:} {\hyperref[\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Algorithm Landscape}}}} \sphinxhyphen{} Deep dive into community detection theory

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recommended workflows:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exploratory:} Start with Louvain \(\rightarrow\) visualize \(\rightarrow\) if unsatisfied, try multilayer Louvain or Infomap

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Publication:} Run multiple algorithms \(\rightarrow\) compare \(\rightarrow\) report consensus + metrics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Large\sphinxhyphen{}scale:} Use label propagation for initial exploration \(\rightarrow\) refine with Louvain on filtered subgraph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal:} Detect communities in snapshots \(\rightarrow\) track with NMI \(\rightarrow\) visualize with alluvial diagrams

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Common pitfalls:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Resolution limit:} Modularity cannot detect communities smaller than \(\sqrt{m}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Non\sphinxhyphen{}determinism:} Many algorithms are stochastic; always set random seeds for reproducibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Overfitting:} Too many tiny communities suggests over\sphinxhyphen{}segmentation; try lower resolution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer coupling:} For multilayer networks, always try multiple \(\omega\) values

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Automatic Algorithm Selection (AutoCommunity)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:automatic-algorithm-selection-autocommunity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{When you don’t know which algorithm to use:} py3plex provides automatic algorithm selection that evaluates multiple algorithms on multiple quality metrics and picks the winner using a “most wins” decision engine.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Quick example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{auto\PYGZus{}select\PYGZus{}community}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Automatically select best algorithm}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{auto\PYGZus{}select\PYGZus{}community}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{fast}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} See why it won}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{explain}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} View leaderboard}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{leaderboard}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use the partition}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{assign\PYGZus{}partition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{partition}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{With DSL:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{auto\PYGZus{}select}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{fast}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{explain}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{How it works:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detects available algorithms (Leiden, Louvain, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Runs candidates with parameter grids (gamma, omega)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluates on multiple metrics (modularity, coverage, stability, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Selects winner by pairwise “most wins” across metrics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies bucket caps to prevent any metric category from dominating

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key parameters:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fast=True}}: Use smaller parameter grids (default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_candidates=10}}: Maximum algorithms to evaluate

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed=0}}: Random seed for determinism

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uq=False}}: Enable uncertainty quantification for stability metrics

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Result object:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.partition}}: Winning partition

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.algorithm}}: Algorithm name and parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.leaderboard}}: DataFrame ranking all candidates

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.explain()}}: Natural language explanation of why it won

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.to\_dict()}}: Serializable dictionary

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{When to use:} Exploratory analysis, comparing algorithms fairly, reproducible algorithm choice with provenance.

See AGENTS.md for complete API documentation.

\subsection{How to Simulate Multilayer Dynamics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:how-to-simulate-multilayer-dynamics}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide presents py3plex as a comprehensive framework for simulating dynamical processes on multilayer networks. We cover epidemic models (SIR, SIS), diffusion processes (random walks), and custom dynamics implementations—all with full multilayer support.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{📓 Run this guide online}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can run this tutorial in your browser without any local installation:

\sphinxhref{https://colab.research.google.com/github/SkBlaz/py3plex/blob/master/notebooks/simulate\_dynamics.ipynb}{\sphinxincludegraphics{{/home/runner/work/py3plex/py3plex/docfiles/_build/latex/.doctrees/images/e79852128a5f83c92496b9d734ca52d01e009a39/colab-badge}.svg}}
%
\begin{footnote}[10]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
\sphinxnolinkurl{https://colab.research.google.com/github/SkBlaz/py3plex/blob/master/notebooks/simulate\_dynamics.ipynb}
%
\end{footnote}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Or see the full executable example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sir\_epidemic.py}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} A loaded multilayer network (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}).


\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer dynamics in py3plex enable you to model processes where interactions occur across multiple types of relationships simultaneously. Typical use cases include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Epidemic spread}: Disease transmission through household, workplace, and social contact layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Information diffusion}: News spreading via online and offline communication channels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Random walks}: Navigation and search processes across interconnected network layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Opinion dynamics}: Belief propagation through multiple social contexts

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Simulation Pipeline}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The typical workflow for running dynamics simulations consists of five steps:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Load or build} a multilayer network using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.core.multinet}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choose a dynamics model} (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIRDynamics}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SISDynamics}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RandomWalkDynamics}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Configure parameters} and initial conditions (infection rates, starting nodes, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run the simulation} via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.run(steps=...)}} with a fixed seed for reproducibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inspect the results} object using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.get\_measure(...)}} to extract time series and summary statistics

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pipeline provides a consistent interface across all dynamics models while allowing specialized configurations for multilayer network effects.


\subsubsection{Common Concepts \& API}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:common-concepts-api}}

\paragraph{Node and Layer Representation}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:node-and-layer-representation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dynamics in py3plex operate on the \sphinxstylestrong{supra\sphinxhyphen{}network} representation, where multilayer nodes are encoded as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer)}} tuples. For example, Alice in the “friends” layer is represented as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(\textquotesingle{}Alice\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}friends\textquotesingle{})}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When you pass a multilayer network to a dynamics model:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node states are tracked per node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Infection, diffusion, or walker movements respect both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can query per\sphinxhyphen{}layer statistics after simulation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For single\sphinxhyphen{}layer NetworkX graphs, nodes are used directly without tuple encoding.


\paragraph{Time and Synchrony}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:time-and-synchrony}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All dynamics models in this guide use \sphinxstylestrong{discrete\sphinxhyphen{}time, synchronous updates}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Time advances in integer steps: t = 0, 1, 2, …

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
At each step, all nodes update simultaneously based on the state at time t

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This differs from continuous\sphinxhyphen{}time (Gillespie) models, which are also available in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.dynamics}}

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Randomness \& Reproducibility}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:randomness-reproducibility}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every dynamics model has a dedicated random number generator controlled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.set\_seed(seed)}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Setting the seed ensures:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reproducible initial conditions (which nodes start infected, which are susceptible)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reproducible stochastic transitions (infection events, recovery events, random walk steps)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consistent results across multiple runs with the same seed

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Network Requirements}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:network-requirements}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dynamics models work with:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{py3plex multilayer networks}: Full support for inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer and intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX graphs}: Single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks (directed or undirected)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Edge weights}: Epidemic models currently treat edges as unweighted contacts. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RandomWalkDynamics}} samples neighbors uniformly, so weights are ignored unless you implement a weighted variant.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Common Base Interface}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:common-base-interface}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All dynamics classes inherit from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DynamicsProcess}} (discrete\sphinxhyphen{}time) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ContinuousTimeProcess}} (continuous\sphinxhyphen{}time). The core methods are:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Initialize with network and parameters}
\PYG{n}{dynamics} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set seed for reproducibility}
\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run for specified number of steps}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract measures}
\PYG{n}{prevalence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{results}} object is always a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DynamicsResult}} instance with standardized measure extraction methods.
Time series returned by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.run(steps=k)}} include the initial state at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t=0}}, so arrays have length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k + 1}}.


\subsubsection{SIR Epidemic Model on Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:sir-epidemic-model-on-multilayer-networks}}

\paragraph{Formal Description}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:formal-description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{SIR (Susceptible\sphinxhyphen{}Infected\sphinxhyphen{}Recovered)} model describes epidemic spread with three compartments:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{S (Susceptible)}: Nodes that can become infected

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{I (Infected)}: Nodes that are currently infectious

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{R (Recovered)}: Nodes with permanent immunity (absorbing state)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Discrete\sphinxhyphen{}Time Update Rules} (synchronous):
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recovery}: Each infected node recovers (I \(\rightarrow\) R) with probability \(\gamma \in (0, 1)\) per time step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infection}: Each susceptible node with k infected neighbors becomes infected (S \(\rightarrow\) I) with probability
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}p_{\text{infect}} = 1 - (1 - \beta)^k\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\beta \in (0, 1)\) is the per\sphinxhyphen{}contact infection probability under independent transmission attempts from each infected neighbor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Absorption}: Recovered nodes remain recovered (R \(\rightarrow\) R) forever

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Extension}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On multilayer networks, the infection pressure on a node aggregates across all layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A susceptible node \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i, layer\_A)}} counts infected neighbors from both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (within \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_A}}) and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (to other layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The built\sphinxhyphen{}in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIRDynamics}} uses a single \(\beta\) value across all layers; to model heterogeneous layers, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:layer-specific-params}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific and Time\sphinxhyphen{}Varying Parameters}}}}} for a small customization pattern

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This means epidemics can spread within layers and jump between layers via inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections, mimicking real\sphinxhyphen{}world scenarios like workplace and household transmission.


\paragraph{Code Example}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:code-example}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a simple two\PYGZhy{}layer network}

    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}

\subsubsection{SIS Epidemic Model on Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:sis-epidemic-model-on-multilayer-networks}}

\paragraph{Formal Description}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:id1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{SIS (Susceptible\sphinxhyphen{}Infected\sphinxhyphen{}Susceptible)} model describes epidemics \sphinxstylestrong{without permanent immunity}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{S (Susceptible)}: Nodes that can become infected

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{I (Infected)}: Nodes that are currently infectious

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Discrete\sphinxhyphen{}Time Update Rules} (synchronous):
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recovery}: Each infected node recovers (I \(\rightarrow\) S) with probability \(\gamma\) (or \(\mu\)) per time step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infection}: Each susceptible node with k infected neighbors becomes infected (S \(\rightarrow\) I) with probability
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}p_{\text{infect}} = 1 - (1 - \beta)^k\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\beta \in (0, 1)\) is the transmission probability per contact

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No absorption}: Recovered nodes immediately return to susceptible state, allowing reinfection

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Endemic Equilibrium}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike SIR (which eventually dies out), SIS can reach an \sphinxstylestrong{endemic equilibrium} where a steady fraction of nodes remain infected. The basic reproduction number is:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}R_0 = \frac{\beta}{\gamma} \langle k \rangle\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where ⟨k⟩ is the average degree in a homogeneous\sphinxhyphen{}network, small\sphinxhyphen{}\(\beta\) approximation (using \(1 - (1 - \beta)^k \approx \beta k\)). If R\(\sb{\text{0}}\) \textgreater{} 1, endemicity is possible; if R\(\sb{\text{0}}\) ≤ 1, the epidemic dies out in this mean\sphinxhyphen{}field view (heterogeneous networks can shift the threshold).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Extension}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On multilayer networks, SIS infection pressure aggregates across all layers, similar to SIR. The endemic prevalence can differ across layers if you use layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific transmission rates.


\paragraph{Code Example}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SISDynamics}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use the same multilayer network as before}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add nodes and edges (same as SIR example)}
\PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}

    \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}

\paragraph{Comparison with SIR}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:comparison-with-sir}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The key difference between SIS and SIR:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SIR}: Forms a peak and dies out (all nodes eventually become R or remain S)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SIS}: Can sustain long\sphinxhyphen{}term endemic prevalence if R\(\sb{\text{0}}\) \textgreater{} 1

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Random Walk Dynamics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:random-walk-dynamics}}

\paragraph{Formal Description}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:id3}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk dynamics simulate the movement of a walker (or multiple walkers) on the network. At each time step:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The walker is at some node (or node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With probability \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lazy\_probability}}, the walker stays at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With probability \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1 \sphinxhyphen{} lazy\_probability}}, the walker moves to a uniformly random neighbor

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Random Walks}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On multilayer networks:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Walkers navigate both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (within a layer) and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (between layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The state is a node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuple, e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Transition probabilities are uniform over all neighbors (intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer + inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge weights in the graph are ignored in this default implementation; to bias transitions by weight, subclass and resample neighbors proportionally

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walks are fundamental for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computing stationary distributions (related to PageRank and eigenvector centrality)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modeling diffusion and search processes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Estimating hitting times between nodes

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Code Example}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:id4}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{RandomWalkDynamics}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a two\PYGZhy{}layer network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Ring structure in layer1, star structure in layer2}
\PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{15}
\PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ring}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{star}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Ring layer: circular edges}
\PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{,}
                  \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ring}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ring}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Star layer: hub\PYGZhy{}spoke (node 0 is hub)}

\paragraph{Analyzing Layer Switching}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:analyzing-layer-switching}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can analyze how often the walker switches between layers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Count layer switches}
\PYG{n}{switches} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{current\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{n}{next\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{current\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{!=} \PYG{n}{next\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{switches} \PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Total layer switches: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{switches}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Switch rate: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{switches}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This reveals how “coupled” the layers are through inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges. High switch rates indicate strong inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connectivity.

\paragraph{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Transmission Rates}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:layer-specific-transmission-rates}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIRDynamics}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SISDynamics}} accept a single scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{beta}}. To model heterogeneous transmission across layers, subclass the process and choose a layer\sphinxhyphen{}dependent \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{beta}} inside the susceptible transition:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}

\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{LayerAwareSIR}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{kwargs}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n+nb}{super}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}beta}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{kwargs}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{transition\PYGZus{}rules} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{dict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{transition\PYGZus{}rules}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} shallow copy}

        \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{transition\PYGZus{}S}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{neighbor\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{params}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
            \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{isinstance}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{tuple}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{k+kc}{None}
            \PYG{n}{beta} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{params}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{beta}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
            \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{neighbor\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
            \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}
                \PYG{n}{p\PYGZus{}infect} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{k}
                \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}} \PYG{n}{p\PYGZus{}infect}\PYG{p}{:}
                    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
            \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}

        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{transition\PYGZus{}rules}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{transition\PYGZus{}S}

\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}rates} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{household}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{workplace}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LayerAwareSIR}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}rates}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pattern mirrors the built\sphinxhyphen{}in rules while letting you vary infection pressure per layer.

After running the simulation, you can compute layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific prevalence manually:

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{isinstance}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{tuple}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer node}

            \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
        \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{state}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}

\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:time-varying-parameters-intervention-scenarios}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To model interventions (e.g., school closures, social distancing), you can run multiple simulations with different parameters for different time windows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Scenario 1: Baseline (no intervention)}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}baseline} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Scenario 2: Intervention at t=30 (reduce beta)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run phase 1 (before intervention)}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}30} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{30}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{record}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get state at t=30}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run phase 2 (with reduced beta)}
\PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}intervention} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.15}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}intervention}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Continue from same seed}
\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}intervention} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}intervention}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{70}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}30}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compare peak prevalence}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Baseline peak: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}baseline}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Intervention peak: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}intervention}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Note: For more complex time\sphinxhyphen{}varying scenarios, consider using the high\sphinxhyphen{}level simulation builder API (see next steps).}


\subsubsection{Result Objects and Metrics}

\paragraph{DynamicsResult API}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:dynamicsresult-api}}

All dynamics models return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DynamicsResult}} object from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.run()}}. This object provides:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Trajectory access}: Direct indexing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{results{[}t{]}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{results.trajectory}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Conversion}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pandas()}} for DataFrame export

\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Extracting and Analyzing Measures}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:extracting-and-analyzing-measures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run SIR simulation}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract prevalence time series}
\PYG{n}{prevalence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Prevalence array shape: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{prevalence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{shape}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (101,) for 100 steps + initial}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute summary statistics}
\PYG{n}{peak\PYGZus{}prevalence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{prevalence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{peak\PYGZus{}time} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{prevalence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{argmax}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}prevalence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{prevalence}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Peak prevalence: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{peak\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ at step }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{peak\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Final prevalence: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract state counts}
\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Available states: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute attack rate (fraction ever infected)}
\PYG{n}{total\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{s}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{s} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Total at t=0}
\PYG{n}{attack\PYGZus{}rate} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n}{total\PYGZus{}nodes}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Attack rate: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{attack\PYGZus{}rate}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For multilayer networks, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_nodes}} counts supra\sphinxhyphen{}nodes (node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuples). If you want a per\sphinxhyphen{}entity attack rate, aggregate layers first.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For further analysis with pandas:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pandas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pd}

    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute prevalence column}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nTime to peak: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{idxmax}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Reproducible Experiments \& Parameter Sweeps}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:reproducible-experiments-parameter-sweeps}}

\paragraph{Running Multiple Stochastic Realizations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:running-multiple-stochastic-realizations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Epidemic dynamics are stochastic, so we often run multiple realizations and report summary statistics:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}

\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{run\PYGZus{}sir\PYGZus{}ensemble}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}runs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Run SIR simulation n\PYGZus{}runs times with different seeds.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{n}{peak\PYGZus{}prevalences} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{n}{attack\PYGZus{}rates} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}

    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{seed} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}runs}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{peak\PYGZus{}prevalence\PYGZus{}std}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{peak\PYGZus{}prevalences}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attack\PYGZus{}rate\PYGZus{}mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{attack\PYGZus{}rates}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attack\PYGZus{}rate\PYGZus{}std}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{attack\PYGZus{}rates}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run ensemble}
\PYG{n}{stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{run\PYGZus{}sir\PYGZus{}ensemble}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}runs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Attack rate: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{stats}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attack\PYGZus{}rate\PYGZus{}mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ \(\pm\) }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{stats}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attack\PYGZus{}rate\PYGZus{}std}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Parameter Grid Sweep}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:parameter-grid-sweep}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To explore how outcomes depend on parameters, run a grid sweep:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pandas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pd}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use a standard network for reproducibility}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{karate\PYGZus{}club\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Parameter grid}
\PYG{n}{beta\PYGZus{}values} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.4}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}values} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.15}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run grid}
\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}grid} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{beta} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{beta\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{gamma} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{n}{prevalence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}grid}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
            \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{beta}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{gamma}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R0\PYGZus{}approx}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{beta} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n}{gamma} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mf}{4.6}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Mean\PYGZhy{}field R0 ≈ (β/γ)\PYGZlt{}k\PYGZgt{}; \PYGZlt{}k\PYGZgt{} ≈ 4.6 here (small\PYGZhy{}β assumption)}
            \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{peak\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{prevalence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{peak\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{prevalence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{argmax}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attack\PYGZus{}rate}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to DataFrame}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}grid}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Custom Dynamics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:custom-dynamics}}

\paragraph{Extending BaseDynamics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:extending-basedynamics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To implement domain\sphinxhyphen{}specific dynamics, subclass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DynamicsProcess}} and define:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initialize\_state(self, seed=None)}}: Return initial state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step(self, state, t)}}: Update state for one time step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
(Optional) Custom measure computation methods

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Contract}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initialize\_state}} must return a state object (dict, list, or custom)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step}} must take the current state and return the new state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both methods can access \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{self.graph}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{self.rng}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{self.params}}

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Example: Threshold Model}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:example-threshold-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We implement a simple threshold model where nodes adopt a binary opinion if enough neighbors have adopted:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{DynamicsProcess}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{\PYGZus{}utils}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{iter\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{iter\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}neighbors}

\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{ThresholdDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{DynamicsProcess}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Threshold model: nodes adopt state 1 if fraction of neighbors exceeds threshold.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}

    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}adopters}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n+nb}{super}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{threshold} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{threshold}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}adopters} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}adopters}

    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{initialize\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Initialize with some nodes in state 1, rest in state 0.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
        \PYG{n}{rng} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rng} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{seed} \PYG{o+ow}{is} \PYG{k+kc}{None} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{iter\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Randomly select initial adopters}
        \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}adopters} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{int}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}adopters}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{adopter\PYGZus{}indices} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{choice}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{size}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}adopters}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{replace}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{adopters} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{adopter\PYGZus{}indices}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{adopters} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{step}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{t}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Update rule: adopt if fraction of neighbors \PYGZgt{}= threshold.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
        \PYG{n}{new\PYGZus{}state} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

        \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{p}{:}
            \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{:}
                \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Already adopted, stay adopted}
                \PYG{n}{new\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}
            \PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}
                \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Count adopting neighbors}
                \PYG{n}{neighbors} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{iter\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}neighbors}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
                \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{o+ow}{not} \PYG{n}{neighbors}\PYG{p}{:}
                    \PYG{n}{new\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}
                    \PYG{k}{continue}

                \PYG{n}{adopting\PYGZus{}neighbors} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{neighbors} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
                \PYG{n}{fraction} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{adopting\PYGZus{}neighbors} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{neighbors}\PYG{p}{)}

                \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Adopt if threshold exceeded}
                \PYG{n}{new\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{fraction} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{threshold} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}

        \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{new\PYGZus{}state}

    \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}adopters}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Count adoption over time}
\PYG{n}{adoption\PYGZus{}counts} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{:}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Initial adopters: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{adoption\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Final adopters: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{adoption\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Adoption rate: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{adoption\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\paragraph{Adding Custom Measures}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:adding-custom-measures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To expose custom measures through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.get\_measure()}}, override the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute\_measure}} method:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{ThresholdDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{DynamicsProcess}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... (same as above) ...}

    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{compute\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{measure\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Compute custom measures for threshold model.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
        \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{measure\PYGZus{}name} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{adoption\PYGZus{}fraction}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}
            \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Fraction of nodes in state 1 over time}
            \PYG{n}{fractions} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
            \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{:}
                \PYG{n}{fractions}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{state}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{state}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
            \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{fractions}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{measure\PYGZus{}name} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{cascade\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}
            \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Final number of adopters}
            \PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}state} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}
            \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}
            \PYG{k}{raise} \PYG{n+ne}{ValueError}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Unknown measure: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{measure\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Now you can use:}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{adoption\PYGZus{}frac} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{adoption\PYGZus{}fraction}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{cascade\PYGZus{}size} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{cascade\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Cascade size: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{cascade\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pattern makes your custom dynamics consistent with built\sphinxhyphen{}in models.


\subsubsection{Query Dynamics Results with DSL}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:query-dynamics-results-with-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL) to query and analyze simulation results efficiently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After running dynamics simulations, the DSL provides powerful tools for querying infected nodes, analyzing layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific patterns, and extracting subpopulations. This is especially useful for multilayer networks where dynamics vary across layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A dynamics simulation result object (from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIRDynamics}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SISDynamics}}, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Familiarity with DSL basics (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Query Multilayer Graphs with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL}}}} for full tutorial)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Attaching Dynamics State as Node Attributes}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:attaching-dynamics-state-as-node-attributes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To use DSL for querying simulation results, first attach the dynamics state to the network as node attributes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{py3plex/datasets/\PYGZus{}data/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run SIR simulation}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Attach final state to network as node attributes}
\PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}state} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{sir\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{state}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Also add a numeric version for filtering}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{is\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{is\PYGZus{}recovered}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{is\PYGZus{}susceptible}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Composable:} Chain operations to build complex analyses

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Integration:} Seamlessly combine dynamics state with network metrics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance:} DSL optimizes query execution for large multilayer networks

\end{itemize}

\subsection{How to Run Random Walk Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_random_walks:how-to-run-random-walk-algorithms}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_random_walks::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Generate network embeddings and node representations using random walk algorithms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} A loaded network (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
All embedding helpers in py3plex return a mapping from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer)}} tuples to dense vectors of length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dimensions}}. Single\sphinxhyphen{}layer inputs still keep the layer entry so you can tell layers apart in multiplex graphs.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where to find this data

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples in this guide create networks programmatically for clarity. You can also:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use built\sphinxhyphen{}in generators: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from py3plex.algorithms import random\_generators}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load from repository files: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{datasets/multiedgelist.txt}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fetch real\sphinxhyphen{}world datasets: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from py3plex.datasets import fetch\_multilayer}}

\end{itemize}
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsubsection{Node2Vec Embeddings}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_random_walks:node2vec-embeddings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node2Vec generates vector representations of nodes by simulating biased random walks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{wrappers}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{train\PYGZus{}node2vec}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a sample network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access embeddings}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxtitleref{p} and \sphinxtitleref{q} parameters control the walk behavior:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{p} (return parameter): Cost of immediately revisiting the previous node (low \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}} = easy to backtrack; high \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}} = discouraged)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{q} (in\sphinxhyphen{}out parameter): Balance between staying near the previous node versus exploring new territory (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q \textgreater{} 1}} ≈ breadth\sphinxhyphen{}first/local, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q \textless{} 1}} ≈ depth\sphinxhyphen{}first/outward)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Think of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}} as controlling backtracking and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q}} as controlling locality; tune them together to steer walks toward either local neighborhoods or long\sphinxhyphen{}range exploration.

\PYG{p}{)}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{similarity} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{cosine\PYGZus{}similarity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{vec1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{vec2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Parameter Tuning}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_random_walks:parameter-tuning}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk hyperparameters meaningfully change embedding quality. Use small validation loops to pick settings that balance accuracy and runtime, and fix seeds (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{workers}}) when you want reproducibility across runs.

                \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{embeddings\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}metrics.csv}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Exported }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node embeddings with metadata}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
