\subsection{How to Export and Serialize Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:how-to-export-and-serialize-networks}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Save multilayer networks to files and load them back—quick persistence,
interoperable edge lists, and analysis\sphinxhyphen{}ready formats.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} A network to export (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}). All
examples assume an in\sphinxhyphen{}memory \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network}} instance.


\subsubsection{Quick Save and Load}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:quick-save-and-load}}

\paragraph{Using Pickle (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:using-pickle-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pickle is the quickest way to persist a network within Python environments when
you do not need cross\sphinxhyphen{}language compatibility.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pickle}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create or load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save to file}
\PYG{k}{with} \PYG{n+nb}{open}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.pkl}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{wb}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{pickle}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dump}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load from file}
\PYG{k}{with} \PYG{n+nb}{open}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.pkl}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{rb}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{loaded\PYGZus{}network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pickle}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{loaded\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only unpickle files from trusted sources, and prefer the same Python + py3plex
versions for best compatibility. Use a text format (CSV/JSON) if you need
portability.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsubsection{Export as Edge List}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:export-as-edge-list}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use plain text or CSV when you want human\sphinxhyphen{}readable exports or interoperability
with tools outside Python.


\paragraph{Simple Text Format}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:simple-text-format}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Write a plain text edge list with node IDs, layers, and weights. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_edges}}
returns edges as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{((node, layer), (node, layer))}} tuples. Each line below
follows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source source\_layer target target\_layer weight}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export edges to text file}
\PYG{k}{with} \PYG{n+nb}{open}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edges.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{w}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edge}
        \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{source}
        \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{target}

        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get edge attributes}
        \PYG{n}{attrs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edge\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{weight} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{attrs}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{write}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{weight}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{CSV Format}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:csv-format}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a CSV edge list with explicit columns for nodes, layers, and weights.
CSV is easier to load in spreadsheets and dataframes than the plain text format.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pandas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pd}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to DataFrame}
\PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edge}
    \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{source}
    \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{target}

    \PYG{n}{attrs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edge\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{attrs}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network\PYGZus{}edges.csv}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Export as JSON}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:export-as-json}}

\paragraph{Full Network Structure}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:full-network-structure}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Capture nodes, layers, edge endpoints, and their attributes in a single JSON
document for easy round\sphinxhyphen{}tripping. JSON keeps attribute dictionaries intact and
readable.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{json}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build JSON structure}
\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{nodes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layers}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add nodes}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}attrs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}node\PYGZus{}attributes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{nodes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attributes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}attrs}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edge}
    \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{source}
    \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{target}

    \PYG{n}{attrs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edge\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attributes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{attrs}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save}
\PYG{k}{with} \PYG{n+nb}{open}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.json}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{w}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{json}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dump}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{indent}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Load from JSON}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:load-from-json}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recreate a multilayer network from the exported JSON representation.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{json}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load JSON}
\PYG{k}{with} \PYG{n+nb}{open}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.json}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{r}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{json}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Reconstruct network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges (nodes created automatically)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}

        \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{attributes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Export to NetworkX}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:export-to-networkx}}

\paragraph{Convert to Single\sphinxhyphen{}Layer NetworkX Graph}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:convert-to-single-layer-networkx-graph}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flatten multilayer data into a single NetworkX graph, keeping the layer as a
node attribute. This drops parallel edges between layers and merges nodes with
the same ID across layers.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Flatten to single layer}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edge}
    \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{source}
    \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{target}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add nodes with layer info}
    \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edge}
    \PYG{n}{attrs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edge\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{attrs}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save as GraphML}
\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}graphml}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.graphml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Export Specific Layer}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:export-specific-layer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Persist just one layer to a simpler graph file.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract single layer}
\PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{n}{subgraph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to NetworkX}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edge}
    \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Just node IDs; include weights if needed}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save}
\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}edgelist}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer\PYGZus{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{.edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{High\sphinxhyphen{}Performance: Apache Arrow/Parquet}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:high-performance-apache-arrow-parquet}}

\paragraph{For Large Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:for-large-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use columnar storage (Arrow/Parquet) to handle large edge lists efficiently.
These formats preserve data types, compress well, and load quickly for analytics
workloads.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pyarrow}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pa}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pyarrow}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{parquet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pq}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert edges to table}
\PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edge}
    \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{source}
    \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{target}

    \PYG{n}{attrs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edge\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{target}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}node}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{attrs}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create Arrow table}
\PYG{n}{table} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pa}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save as Parquet}
\PYG{n}{pq}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}table}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.parquet}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Load from Parquet}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:load-from-parquet}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rebuild a network from a Parquet edge list. Ensure \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pyarrow}} is installed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pyarrow}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{parquet}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pq}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Reconstruct network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{row} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{iterrows}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{weight}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Export Statistics and Results}

\paragraph{Save Analysis Results}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Persist computed metrics (via DSL) for later inspection or sharing with

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{node\PYGZus{}statistics.csv}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{communities.csv}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Batch Export}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:batch-export}}

\paragraph{Export Multiple Formats}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize:export-multiple-formats}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a small export bundle so you can hand off the same network in different
formats.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{json}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pickle}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pandas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pd}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Prepare reusable structures}
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{edges\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}df}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{records} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

\subsection{How to Visualize Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/visualize_networks:how-to-visualize-multilayer-networks}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/visualize_networks::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Create publication\sphinxhyphen{}ready visualizations of multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} A loaded network (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}). Most
snippets reuse a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network}} object created in the quick plot example; swap in
your own network if you already have one loaded.

    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Customizing Visualizations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/visualize_networks:customizing-visualizations}}

\paragraph{Node Sizes and Colors}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/visualize_networks:node-sizes-and-colors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The built\sphinxhyphen{}in hairball plot draws the aggregated network with layer\sphinxhyphen{}based colors.
You can override sizing and colors explicitly to emphasize node importance:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{hairball\PYGZus{}plot}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute degrees for sizing}
\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}order} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}sizes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}order}
\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ax} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subplots}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{figsize}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{8}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{8}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{hairball\PYGZus{}plot}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{ax}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{ax}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{legend}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{layout\PYGZus{}algorithm}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{force}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{alpha\PYGZus{}channel}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.6}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{network\PYGZus{}sized.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dpi}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{300}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{bbox\PYGZus{}inches}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{tight}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Edge Weights}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/visualize_networks:edge-weights}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Widths based on stored weight (default to 1); clamp to keep faint edges visible}

    \PYG{n+nb}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{n}{pos} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{spring\PYGZus{}layout}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.6}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{figure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{figsize}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{8}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{8}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}networkx}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{pos}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{,}

    \PYG{n}{width}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{edge\PYGZus{}widths}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.7}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{off}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{tight\PYGZus{}layout}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Layout Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/visualize_networks:layout-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Switch layouts to highlight different structures: force\sphinxhyphen{}directed for overall
connectivity, circular for equal treatment of nodes within a layer, or diagonal
layouts for explicit layer separation.

\subsubsection{DSL\sphinxhyphen{}Driven Visualization Workflows}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/visualize_networks:dsl-driven-visualization-workflows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use DSL queries to select and visualize specific network subsets.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL enables you to create targeted visualizations by filtering nodes and
edges before rendering. This is essential for large multilayer networks where
visualizing everything is impractical. Unless otherwise noted, the examples
below reuse the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network}} instance built in the basic visualization section.

\subsection{How to Query Multilayer Graphs with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:how-to-query-multilayer-graphs-with-the-sql-like-dsl}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s SQL\sphinxhyphen{}inspired Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL) to query, filter, and analyze multilayer networks. The DSL is a \sphinxstylestrong{first\sphinxhyphen{}class query language} specifically designed for multilayer graph structures, providing both string syntax for interactive exploration and a type\sphinxhyphen{}safe builder API for production code.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{📓 Run this guide online}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can run this tutorial in your browser without any local installation:

\sphinxhref{https://colab.research.google.com/github/SkBlaz/py3plex/blob/master/notebooks/query\_with\_dsl.ipynb}{\sphinxincludegraphics{{/home/runner/work/py3plex/py3plex/docfiles/_build/latex/.doctrees/images/e79852128a5f83c92496b9d734ca52d01e009a39/colab-badge}.svg}}
%
\begin{footnote}[11]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
\sphinxnolinkurl{https://colab.research.google.com/github/SkBlaz/py3plex/blob/master/notebooks/query\_with\_dsl.ipynb}
%
\end{footnote}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Or see the full executable example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{example\_dsl\_builder\_api.py}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What Makes This DSL Special:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Graph\sphinxhyphen{}aware}: Unlike generic query languages, the DSL understands multilayer structures—layers, layer intersections, intralayer vs. interlayer edges, and (node, layer) tuple semantics.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dual interfaces}: String syntax for rapid prototyping in notebooks; builder API (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}) for IDE autocompletion and type checking.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Integrated computation}: Compute centrality, clustering, and other network metrics directly in queries, with results returned as pandas DataFrames or NetworkX graphs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal support}: Query network snapshots and time ranges when your network includes temporal information.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A loaded \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} object (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Basic familiarity with multilayer network concepts (nodes, layers, intralayer/interlayer edges)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For complete DSL grammar and operator reference, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{DSL Reference}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pick your interface: string syntax for quick experiments, builder API for reusable production code with IDE support

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Conceptual Overview}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:conceptual-overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL has \sphinxstylestrong{two complementary interfaces} that compile to the same internal representation:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{String Syntax} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute\_query(network, "SELECT nodes WHERE ...")}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like, human\sphinxhyphen{}readable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ideal for interactive exploration in Jupyter notebooks or the REPL

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Quick one\sphinxhyphen{}liners for common queries

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Builder API} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q.nodes().where(...).compute(...).execute(network)}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pythonic, chainable methods

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Type\sphinxhyphen{}safe with IDE autocompletion

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recommended for production code and complex workflows

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mental Model:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A typical DSL query follows this pipeline:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
SELECT nodes/edges
\(\rightarrow\) FROM LAYERS (restrict to specific layers)
\(\rightarrow\) WHERE (filter by attributes or special predicates)
\(\rightarrow\) COMPUTE (calculate metrics like degree, centrality)
\(\rightarrow\) ORDER BY (sort results)
\(\rightarrow\) LIMIT (cap number of results)
\(\rightarrow\) EXPORT (materialize as DataFrame, NetworkX graph, etc.)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key Concepts:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Nodes as (node, layer) tuples}: In multilayer networks, a node may appear in multiple layers. The DSL represents these as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_name)}} pairs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer set algebra}: Combine layers with set operations (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}} union, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} intersection, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}} difference, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}}} complement). The new LayerSet algebra enables expressive layer selection like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"* \sphinxhyphen{} coupling"{]}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"(ppi | gene) \& disease"{]}}}. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Layer Set Algebra}}}} for complete documentation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Special predicates}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{intralayer=True}} selects edges within a layer; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interlayer=("layer1", "layer2")}} selects edges crossing specific layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Lazy execution}: Queries are built incrementally and executed only when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(network)}} is called.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}Q\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{} and \textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}L\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{} helpers}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}} builds queries; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} builds layer expressions. Import both from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.dsl}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comparison to SQL:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Think of the DSL as SQL for graphs:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \textgreater{} 5}} ≈ SQL’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE degree \textgreater{} 5}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
But instead of tables, you’re querying \sphinxstylestrong{nodes and edges} with \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer and temporal attributes}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer filters and graph\sphinxhyphen{}specific predicates (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{intralayer}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interlayer}}) have no SQL equivalent

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{String Syntax (Quick and Readable)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:string-syntax-quick-and-readable}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The string syntax provides a concise, SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like way to express queries. Best for exploratory analysis and quick investigations.


\paragraph{Basic SELECT}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:basic-select}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select all nodes and inspect the result:

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where to find this data

\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples in this guide use one of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Built\sphinxhyphen{}in data generators} like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_generators.random\_multilayer\_ER(...)}} (recommended for self\sphinxhyphen{}contained examples)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example files} from the repository at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{datasets/multiedgelist.txt}} or similar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{built\sphinxhyphen{}in datasets module}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from py3plex.datasets import fetch\_multilayer}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For this example, we’ll create a simple network programmatically:
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a simple multilayer network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{charlie}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{charlie}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all nodes}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading from files

\sphinxAtStartPar
To load from a file in the repository:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Using a file from the datasets/ directory}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/multiedgelist.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Or using an absolute path}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}
\PYG{n}{path} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{join}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dirname}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nv+vm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}file\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Note:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute\_query}} returns a dict\sphinxhyphen{}like result. Keys are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node, layer)}} tuples representing node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} attribute counts how many distinct layers the node appears in across the entire network. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{len(result)}} gives the number of returned items, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.items()}} yields the full (key, value) pairs.


\paragraph{Filter by Layer}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:filter-by-layer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restrict queries to nodes in a specific layer:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes in the \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{} layer only}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ layer: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Understanding Layer Filters:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer="friends"}} selects only the node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer == "friends"}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This does \sphinxstylestrong{not} select all occurrences of nodes across layers—only their representation in the specified layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count \textgreater{}= 2}} to find nodes appearing in multiple layers (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} is the number of distinct layers for that node)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example with statistics:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ COMPUTE degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Average degree in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Max degree in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\paragraph{Filter by Property}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:filter-by-property}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use comparisons to filter nodes by computed or intrinsic attributes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} High\PYGZhy{}degree nodes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{High\PYGZhy{}degree nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer nodes with high degree}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5 AND layer\PYGZus{}count \PYGZgt{}= 2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{High\PYGZhy{}degree multilayer nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supported operators:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!=}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple conditions} are combined with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AND}}. For more complex logic, use the builder API (see below).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output (counts will vary with your data):}

\paragraph{Compute Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:compute-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{COMPUTE}} clause calculates network metrics and attaches them to result rows. This is where the DSL becomes powerful for analysis:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute degree and betweenness centrality for nodes in \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{} layer}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{COMPUTE degree COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to pandas for analysis}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top nodes by betweenness centrality:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Summary statistics:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Builder API (Type\sphinxhyphen{}Safe)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:builder-api-type-safe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{builder API is the recommended approach for production code}. It provides:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
IDE autocompletion and inline documentation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Type checking with tools like mypy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clearer error messages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Easier refactoring and composition of queries

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All builder queries compile to the same AST as string queries, ensuring consistent semantics.


\paragraph{Basic Queries}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:basic-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create and execute queries using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} imports:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all nodes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Total nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes from a specific layer}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ layer: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Query reusability:} You can define a query once and execute it with different networks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}query} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execute on multiple networks}
\PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}network1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}network2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network2}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Filtering}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:filtering}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}} to add filter conditions. The builder API uses Django\sphinxhyphen{}style \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_}} suffixes for comparisons:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Filter by property}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes with degree \PYGZgt{} 5: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multiple conditions (combined with AND)}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gte}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Multilayer high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supported comparison suffixes:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_gt}}: greater than (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_gte}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_ge}}: greater than or equal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}=}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_lt}}: less than (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_lte}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_le}}: less than or equal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}=}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_eq}}: equal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_ne}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_neq}}: not equal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!=}})

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Understanding} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
In multilayer networks, a node may appear in multiple layers. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} attribute indicates how many layers the node participates in:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count\_\_gte=2}}: nodes appearing in at least 2 layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count\_\_eq=1}}: nodes appearing in exactly 1 layer (layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific nodes)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is useful for identifying “connector” nodes that bridge multiple contexts.


\paragraph{Computing Metrics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:computing-metrics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute()}} to calculate network metrics. Metrics are computed efficiently and attached to result rows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute multiple metrics}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to DataFrame and analyze}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get top nodes by a metric}
\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nlargest}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 10 nodes by betweenness centrality:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}betweenness}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Order of operations:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute()}} can be called at any point in the chain

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filters (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}}) can reference computed metrics only if the metric is computed \sphinxstylestrong{before} the filter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For best performance, filter first, then compute:

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good: Filter first, then compute}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output (illustrative):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
                  id  degree  betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality  clustering

4   (grace, social)      11                 0.221000    0.509091
...

\paragraph{Computing Metrics with Uncertainty}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:computing-metrics-with-uncertainty}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{New in py3plex 1.0:} The DSL now supports \sphinxstylestrong{first\sphinxhyphen{}class uncertainty} for computed metrics. This allows you to estimate statistical uncertainty (confidence intervals, standard deviations) for network statistics via bootstrap, perturbation, or Monte Carlo methods.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why uncertainty matters:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Networks are often noisy or sampled (e.g., social networks with missing edges)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Centrality metrics can be sensitive to small perturbations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uncertainty quantification helps distinguish signal from noise

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Required for robust statistical inference and hypothesis testing

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic usage:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute degree with uncertainty estimation}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}
         \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
         \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
         \PYG{n}{uncertainty}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}
         \PYG{n}{method}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{perturbation}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} or \PYGZdq{}bootstrap\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}seed\PYGZdq{}}
         \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}samples}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,}          \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} number of resamples}
         \PYG{n}{ci}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.95}                 \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} confidence interval level}
     \PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access uncertainty information}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Results contain mean, std, and quantiles for each metric}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} The \PYGZsq{}degree\PYGZsq{} column now has dict values with uncertainty info}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Uncertainty methods:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"perturbation"}}: Drop a small fraction of edges/nodes randomly (default: 5\%)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"bootstrap"}}: Resample nodes/edges with replacement

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"seed"}}: Run stochastic algorithms with different random seeds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"jackknife"}}: Leave\sphinxhyphen{}one\sphinxhyphen{}out resampling

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Parameters:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uncertainty}} (bool): Enable uncertainty estimation (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{method}} (str): Resampling strategy (default: “perturbation”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n\_samples}} (int): Number of resamples (default: 50)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci}} (float): Confidence interval level, e.g., 0.95 for 95\% CI (default: 0.95)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example with confidence intervals:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find hubs with uncertainty bounds}
\PYG{n}{hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}
         \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
         \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
         \PYG{n}{uncertainty}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}
         \PYG{n}{method}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{perturbation}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}

     \PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use cases:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comparing networks}: Test if centrality differences between networks are statistically significant

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Robust ranking}: Identify nodes that consistently rank high across perturbations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network inference}: Quantify uncertainty when inferring networks from noisy data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Hypothesis testing}: Generate null distributions for significance testing

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance notes:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uncertainty estimation is \sphinxstylestrong{opt\sphinxhyphen{}in} and only runs when explicitly requested

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cost scales linearly with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n\_samples}} (e.g., 100 samples ≈ 100× slower)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use smaller \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n\_samples}} (20\sphinxhyphen{}50) for exploration, larger (100\sphinxhyphen{}500) for publication

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perturbation is fastest; bootstrap and jackknife are more expensive

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\paragraph{Sorting and Limiting}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:sorting-and-limiting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_by()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit()}} to control result ordering and size:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get top 10 nodes by degree}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZdq{} prefix for descending}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 10 highest\PYGZhy{}degree nodes:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: degree=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{itemize}

\subsubsection{Working with Results}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:working-with-results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL queries return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QueryResult}} object that provides multiple ways to access and export data. Understanding how to work with results is crucial for integrating DSL queries into analysis pipelines.


\paragraph{Access as Dictionary}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:access-as-dictionary}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QueryResult}} provides dictionary\sphinxhyphen{}like access via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.items()}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Iterate over all items}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: degree=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Inspect one sample entry}
\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}key}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}value} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{next}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{iter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Sample key type: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}key}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Sample key: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}key}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Sample value: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{p}{]}

\paragraph{Filter Results}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:filter-results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can filter results in two ways: \sphinxstylestrong{using the DSL’s} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}} \sphinxstylestrong{clause} (recommended) or \sphinxstylestrong{post\sphinxhyphen{}processing} with Python/pandas.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 1: Filter in the query (recommended for large networks):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Filter before computation for efficiency}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 2: Filter the result dictionary (for small networks or ad\sphinxhyphen{}hoc filtering):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Pure Python filtering}
\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{data}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{High\PYGZhy{}degree nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 3: Filter the DataFrame (most flexible for complex conditions):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use pandas boolean indexing}
\PYG{n}{filtered} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Complex conditions}
\PYG{n}{interesting\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance note:} For very large networks (millions of nodes), filtering in the DSL query (Option 1) is most efficient because it avoids materializing unnecessary results. For smaller networks, pandas filtering (Option 3) is often more convenient.


\subsubsection{Advanced Queries}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:advanced-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This section showcases the DSL’s power for sophisticated multilayer network analysis. These patterns are common in research and can be adapted to your specific needs.


\paragraph{Multiple Layer Selection}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:multiple-layer-selection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxstylestrong{layer algebra} to combine layers. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} object supports set operations (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}} for union, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} for intersection, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}} for difference):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Union: nodes/edges from EITHER layer}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Combined nodes from }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ and }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Average degree across both layers: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Set semantics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"friends"{]} | L{[}"work"{]}}}: \sphinxstylestrong{Union} of nodes/edges from both layers (nodes appearing in either layer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"friends"{]} \& L{[}"work"{]}}}: \sphinxstylestrong{Intersection} (see next section)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"friends"{]} \sphinxhyphen{} L{[}"work"{]}}}: \sphinxstylestrong{Difference} (nodes in friends but not work)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use case:} Compare activity across related contexts. For example, analyze user behavior across social and professional networks together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\paragraph{Layer Intersection}

    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{These are }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{connector}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes bridging social and professional contexts}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Semantics:}
\begin{itemize}

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
