\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ high\PYGZhy{}degree pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get unique nodes involved}
\PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Unique nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Example 4: Cross\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Hub Detection}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:example-4-cross-layer-hub-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Find nodes that appear in multiple layers and have high degree in each.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} This requires multiple pattern queries}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find nodes in social layer}
\PYG{n}{social\PYGZus{}hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{returning}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find nodes in work layer}
\PYG{n}{work\PYGZus{}hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{returning}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find intersection (nodes in both)}
\PYG{n}{social\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{social\PYGZus{}hubs}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{n}{work\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{work\PYGZus{}hubs}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{n}{cross\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{social\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}} \PYG{n}{work\PYGZus{}nodes}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Cross\PYGZhy{}layer hubs: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{cross\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}hubs}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Working with Results}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:working-with-results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PatternQueryResult}} object provides multiple ways to access matches. Use raw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rows}} for programmatic iteration, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_pandas}} for tabular analysis, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_nodes}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_edges}} when you want to pass results back into graph algorithms.


\paragraph{Accessing Rows}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:accessing-rows}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all matches as list of dictionaries}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{match} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rows}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Match: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{match}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} e.g., \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}a\PYGZsq{}: (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{}), \PYGZsq{}b\PYGZsq{}: (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{})\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.count}} is the number of rows returned, equivalent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{len(result.rows)}}.
Each row maps your variable names to concrete \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node, layer)}} tuples.


\paragraph{Converting to Pandas}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:converting-to-pandas}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Now use pandas operations}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export to CSV}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pattern\PYGZus{}matches.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Column order follows the variables you specified with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.returning(...)}}; if you did not set it, all variables are returned in declaration order.


\paragraph{Extracting Nodes}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:extracting-nodes}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all matched nodes (as tuples)}
\PYG{n}{all\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get unique nodes only}
\PYG{n}{unique\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes for specific variables}
\PYG{n}{a\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{vars}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Extracting Edges}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:extracting-edges}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all matched edges as tuples}
\PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Each edge is a (source\PYGZus{}tuple, target\PYGZus{}tuple) pair}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{src}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dst} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Edge: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{src}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{dst}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Creating Subgraphs}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:creating-subgraphs}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create induced subgraph of matched nodes}
\PYG{n}{subgraph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}subgraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Now use NetworkX operations}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Subgraph has }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Subgraph has }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create one subgraph per match}
\PYG{n}{subgraphs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}subgraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{per\PYGZus{}match}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Created }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{subgraphs}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ subgraphs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Filtering Results}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:filtering-results}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Filter matches using a predicate}
\PYG{n}{filtered} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{match}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{match}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{startswith}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{A}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Limit number of results}
\PYG{n}{limited} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} return new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PatternQueryResult}} objects; they do not modify the original result.


\subsubsection{Query Execution Planning}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:query-execution-planning}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.explain()}} to see how the pattern will be executed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{plan} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{explain}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Root variable: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{root\PYGZus{}var}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Join order: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{var}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o+ow}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{join\PYGZus{}order}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Estimated complexity: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{estimated\PYGZus{}complexity}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example Output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Root variable: a
Join order: [\PYGZsq{}a\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}b\PYGZsq{}]
Estimated complexity: 1000
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The planner chooses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}} as the root because it has the most restrictive predicates (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree\_\_gt=3}}), which will generate fewer candidates.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{estimated\_complexity}} field is a relative heuristic, useful for comparing different patterns rather than predicting exact runtime.


\subsubsection{Performance Tips}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:performance-tips}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Add Predicates Early:} The more selective predicates you add to the root variable, the faster the query.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good: Restrictive predicate on first node}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Less efficient: No predicates}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Layer Constraints:} Layer filters significantly reduce the search space.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good: Restrict to one layer}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Less efficient: Search all layers}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Set Limits:} For large networks, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.limit()}} to cap results.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Constraints:} Add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a != b}} constraints to avoid self\sphinxhyphen{}loops if not needed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a != b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Return only needed variables:} Reducing the result width lowers serialization overhead.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{returning}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Advanced Features}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:advanced-features}}

\paragraph{Constraints}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:constraints}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Global constraints that apply across variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} All\PYGZhy{}different constraint}
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a != b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b != c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a != c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Returning Specific Variables}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:returning-specific-variables}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, all variables are returned. You can select specific ones:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{returning}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Only return endpoints}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Result only contains \PYGZsq{}a\PYGZsq{} and \PYGZsq{}c\PYGZsq{} columns}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Execution Options}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:execution-options}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set maximum matches}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}matches}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set timeout (in seconds)}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{timeout}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\paragraph{Pattern Matching vs. DSL Node/Edge Queries}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:pattern-matching-vs-dsl-node-edge-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use node/edge queries when you need individual elements. Use pattern matching when you need to find subgraph structures.


\subsubsection{Limitations and Future Work}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:limitations-and-future-work}}

\paragraph{Current Limitations (v1)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:current-limitations-v1}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fixed\sphinxhyphen{}length paths only:} Variable\sphinxhyphen{}length paths like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(a)\sphinxhyphen{}{[}*1..3{]}\sphinxhyphen{}(b)}} not yet supported

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No optional matching:} All pattern elements must match

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No UNION patterns:} Cannot express “match pattern A OR pattern B”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Limited aggregation:} Aggregation over matches not yet implemented

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These features are planned for future versions while maintaining the current clean API.


\paragraph{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Start simple:} Begin with small patterns and add complexity incrementally

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Test on small data:} Validate pattern logic on toy networks before scaling up

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use explain():} Check execution plans for complex queries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Combine with DSL:} Use pattern matching for structure, DSL for attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Document patterns:} Add comments explaining complex pattern logic

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:troubleshooting}}

\paragraph{Pattern Returns No Matches}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:pattern-returns-no-matches}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Your pattern should match but returns 0 results.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check layer constraints — are nodes actually in the layers you specified?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Verify predicates — are the thresholds too restrictive?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.explain()}} to see the execution plan

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Test with simpler patterns first

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check if your network has the expected structure

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Debug: Check basic statistics first}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Social layer has }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{intralayer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Network has }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ intralayer edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Too Many Matches}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:too-many-matches}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Pattern returns too many results.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add more predicates to narrow the search

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.limit()}} to cap results

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add layer constraints to restrict search space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.constraint("a != b")}} to avoid duplicates

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Limit results}
\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Slow Performance}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:slow-performance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Pattern matching takes too long.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add selective predicates to the root variable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use layer constraints to reduce search space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider breaking pattern into smaller sub\sphinxhyphen{}patterns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.explain()}} to check estimated complexity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set timeout to avoid runaway queries

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set timeout}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{timeout}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{How to Build Analysis Pipelines with Dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style Operations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:how-to-build-analysis-pipelines-with-dplyr-style-operations}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Chain operations to build reproducible analysis workflows on node or edge tables.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} Load a network first (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes(...)}} returns a chainable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NodeFrame}} (view over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree}}, etc.); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edges(...)}} returns an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EdgeFrame}}. Examples below use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NodeFrame}} and end with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pandas()}} to materialize results.


\subsubsection{Quickstart}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:quickstart}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter \(\rightarrow\) add a column \(\rightarrow\) sort \(\rightarrow\) convert to pandas:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}ops}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{nodes}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build pipeline: filter \(\rightarrow\) add a column \(\rightarrow\) sort \(\rightarrow\) convert to pandas}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{score}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Available Operations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:available-operations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Common verbs you can chain on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes(...)}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edges(...)}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter}}: keep rows that satisfy a predicate

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mutate}}: add or modify columns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select}}: choose columns (and optionally reorder)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arrange}}: sort by a column or key function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}} + \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summarise}}: aggregate per group

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head}}: keep the first \sphinxstyleemphasis{n} rows (useful for previews)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{filter()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:filter}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select rows based on conditions. Chain multiple filters for readability:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{mutate()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:mutate}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add or modify columns using callables that receive each row (a dict\sphinxhyphen{}like object):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}squared}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}hub}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{select()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:select}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose specific columns (and optionally reorder them):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{select}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{arrange()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:arrange}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sort results (ascending by default, or descending with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reverse=True}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Descending}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{group\_by() and summarise()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:group-by-and-summarise}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregate by one or more columns. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summarise}} expects functions that return scalars (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{len}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{summarise}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{count}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Illustrative output (values depend on your data):}

\subsubsection{Complex Pipelines}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:complex-pipelines}}

\paragraph{Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Step Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:multi-step-analysis}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combine several verbs to narrow down to the most active nodes. This example assumes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree}} columns already exist (e.g., after computing node statistics):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 1: Filter active nodes}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 2: Add computed score}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{activity\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 3: Filter by score}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{activity\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 4: Sort by score}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{activity\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 5: Get top 20}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to pandas}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Combining with DSL}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:combining-with-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mix dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style operations with DSL queries to narrow down candidates, then enrich them:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}ops}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{nodes}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use the same network as above}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use DSL to select nodes and compute measures once}
\PYG{n}{dsl\PYGZus{}result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5 COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{selected} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dsl\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{dsl\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{computed}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use dplyr\PYGZhy{}style to filter and transform the same nodes}
\PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{selected}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{betweenness}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{betweenness}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{centrality\PYGZus{}rank}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{betweenness}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{centrality\PYGZus{}rank}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:scikit-learn-style-pipelines}}

Use the built\sphinxhyphen{}in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pipeline}} to chain reusable steps (each step implements \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform}} and receives the previous output). The first step should handle \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}} input (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LoadStep}} does). \begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pipeline}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Pipeline}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LoadStep}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{FilterNodes}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ComputeStats}

\PYG{n}{pipe} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Pipeline}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{load}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LoadStep}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{filter}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{FilterNodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{stats}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ComputeStats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{include\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pipe}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{stats}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Custom steps can wrap scikit\sphinxhyphen{}learn components if they implement \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform}} (and optionally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fit}}) to accept the previous step’s output and return the next input.

        \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{name}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{stats}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{params}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{include\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{with} \PYG{n+nb}{open}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pipeline.json}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{w}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{:}

\paragraph{Reload and Rebuild}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:reload-and-rebuild}}

\subsubsection{DSL\sphinxhyphen{}Driven Analysis Workflows}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/reproduce_workflows:dsl-driven-analysis-workflows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s DSL to create reproducible, declarative analysis pipelines.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL expresses analysis workflows as queries rather than imperative code, keeping them readable and reproducible. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}} builds a query, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} is a layer helper, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute\_query}} returns dictionaries keyed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer)}} tuples.


\paragraph{Basic DSL Workflow Pattern}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/reproduce_workflows:basic-dsl-workflow-pattern}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Template for DSL\sphinxhyphen{}first analysis:} Keep the pipeline linear—load, query, refine, export—so each step can be repeated with different parameters.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1. Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{py3plex/datasets/\PYGZus{}data/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2. Query and filter nodes with DSL}
\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Community Detection + DSL Workflow}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Combine community detection with DSL queries:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{collections}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Counter}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Detect communities}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Attach as node attributes}

    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{COMMUNITY\PYGZhy{}BASED ANALYSIS}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{70}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Query each community}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{sorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}ids}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use DSL to get community members}
    \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE community=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{members} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute community metrics}
    \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{community}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Statistics}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}degree} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{d} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}betw} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{d} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}degree} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}betw} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Layer composition}
    \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}counts} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Counter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{members}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Community }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Size: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{members}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Avg degree: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Avg betweenness: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}betw}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.6f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Layer composition: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{dict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Notes:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute\_query}} returns a dictionary; access community members via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result{[}"nodes"{]}}} as shown. Community labels live on the NetworkX backing graph (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network.core\_network}}), so they persist across subsequent DSL queries.


\paragraph{Dynamics + DSL Workflow}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Epidemic simulation with DSL\sphinxhyphen{}based analysis:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{EPIDEMIC ANALYSIS}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{70}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Per\PYGZhy{}layer infection analysis}

    \PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Counter}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{sir\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{unknown}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{total} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Batch Processing}

\subsection{Multilayer Networks 101}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:multilayer-networks-101}}\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter explains what multilayer networks are, when to use them, and how to choose the right type for your data—without flattening away important structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{You will learn:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
What distinguishes multilayer from single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Types: multiplex, heterogeneous, temporal, interdependent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When to use multilayer modeling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Common pitfalls to avoid

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Key ideas to keep in mind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{layer} labels the context of an interaction (relationship type, time slice, modality).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} is the atomic unit; the same node can appear in multiple layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Coupling} uses inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges that link the same entity across layers, with a weight controlling how strongly layers influence each other. When the weight is 0, layers are independent; higher weights make layers behave more coherently.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{What are Multilayer Networks?}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:what-are-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer network} models systems with multiple types of relationships, node types, or interaction contexts while keeping each interaction labeled by its layer. Each edge carries both endpoints \sphinxstyleemphasis{and} the layer context, so interactions remain distinguishable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:} A researcher’s social world includes coauthors, colleagues, students, and Twitter followers. These are different relationship types with different meanings. A multilayer network keeps them as separate \sphinxstylestrong{layers} rather than flattening into one graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Traditional vs. Multilayer:}

\subsubsection{Types of Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:types-of-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples below use simple edge lists to show how different modeling choices map to different layer structures. Choose the structure that matches (a) whether node identities repeat across layers and (b) whether relationships are interchangeable or context\sphinxhyphen{}specific.


\paragraph{Multiplex Networks}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:multiplex-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Same nodes, different relationship types.} Use when the \sphinxstyleemphasis{entities} are the same everywhere, but interactions mean different things per layer.

    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:} Social networks across platforms, transportation via air/rail/road, communication via email/phone/chat.

\sphinxstylestrong{Tip:} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges typically connect identical nodes across layers to model the idea that “Alice in friends” is still Alice in “colleagues.”

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:} Academic networks (authors, papers, venues), e\sphinxhyphen{}commerce (users, products, sellers), biomedical (drugs, diseases, targets).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tip:} Keep node identifiers disjoint across types (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P1}} is always a paper) to avoid accidental coupling.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:} Communication over time, social dynamics, disease spread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tip:} Choose time\sphinxhyphen{}slice granularity that matches the process of interest—too coarse hides dynamics, too fine yields sparse noise. Adjacent slices can be coupled with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges to allow information to move through time.


\paragraph{Interdependent Networks}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:interdependent-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple networks where nodes depend on each other rather than sharing identity.} Dependencies capture “if X fails in layer A, Y fails in layer B,” not “X is the same as Y.”

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:} Power grid depends on communication network, supply chains, cyber\sphinxhyphen{}physical systems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tip:} Model dependencies explicitly with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges that indicate which nodes fail together or require coordination; these edges can connect different node IDs across layers and often have direction (who depends on whom).


\subsubsection{When to Use Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:when-to-use-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use multilayer modeling when:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple relationship types matter} — Friendship and professional connections behave differently.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node roles vary by context} — A hub in work may be peripheral in hobbies.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer interactions are important} — Transportation failures in one mode affect others.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal evolution matters} — Relationships change over time and order matters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{System\sphinxhyphen{}level properties emerge} — Cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer dependencies affect resilience, spreading, or coordination.

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Choosing a Modeling Approach}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:choosing-a-modeling-approach}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ask these questions:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers vs. attributes?} If relationships differ in \sphinxstyleemphasis{kind} (email vs. meeting), use layers. If they differ only in \sphinxstyleemphasis{intensity} (weight, frequency), keep one layer and add attributes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Same or different nodes?} Same entities in all layers \(\rightarrow\) multiplex. Different entity types \(\rightarrow\) heterogeneous (avoid forcing identity coupling).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Coupling strength?} When identities repeat across layers, set an inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer weight \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega ≥ 0}} to control how tightly node copies move together (e.g., start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega=1.0}} for identity coupling; reduce it if layers should diverge).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal structure?} If order matters, use time\sphinxhyphen{}sliced layers with optional coupling between adjacent slices; only aggregate into a static network when chronology is irrelevant.

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{What Goes Wrong When You Flatten}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:what-goes-wrong-when-you-flatten}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flattening throws away layer information. Typical failure modes include:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community structure destroyed:} Flattening can create spurious bridges between groups that are distinct in the layer structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Centrality becomes misleading:} A researcher with 2 coauthors and 500 Twitter followers has degree 502 when flattened, but academic influence is only 2. Centrality scores mix incomparable interaction modes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Path analysis fails:} Email \(\rightarrow\) meeting transitions matter for information flow but are invisible in a flattened network, so path\sphinxhyphen{}based predictions over\sphinxhyphen{} or under\sphinxhyphen{}estimate reachability.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer semantics disappear:} Once layers are merged, you can no longer tell which mode of interaction drove a result.


\subsubsection{Common Pitfalls}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:common-pitfalls}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Over\sphinxhyphen{}aggregating} — Combining layers that should stay separate; prefer explicit layers when semantics differ.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Under\sphinxhyphen{}aggregating} — Too many ultra\sphinxhyphen{}sparse layers; use edge weights or coarser bins instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Ignoring coupling} — Treating layers as independent when nodes correspond; set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega}} explicitly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Wrong coupling strength} — Too high forces artificial consistency; too low loses cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer information.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mismatched identifiers} — Same entity must have the same ID across layers for identity coupling to work.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inconsistent time slicing} — Changing window sizes mid\sphinxhyphen{}analysis hides or invents trends; keep cadence consistent.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Key Terminology}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:key-terminology}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges} — Within a single layer (same layer ID on both endpoints)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges} — Between layers (often identity edges connecting the same node across layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} tuples, the fundamental unit for most algorithms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix} — Block matrix encoding both intra\sphinxhyphen{} and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections; shape is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(n·L) × (n·L)}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} nodes appearing in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Coupling} — Strength of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (often \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega}}); controls how strongly layers influence one another

\end{itemize}

\subsection{The py3plex Core Model}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:the-py3plex-core-model}}\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{In which we look under the hood at how py3plex represents multilayer networks, understand the node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair representation, and learn to work with the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix.}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
In the previous chapter, you learned \sphinxstyleemphasis{what} multilayer networks are conceptually. Now we’ll see \sphinxstyleemphasis{how} py3plex represents them in code—and why these design choices matter for your analysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Understanding the internal representation will help you:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Debug unexpected behavior (why does my network have twice as many nodes as I expected?)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integrate with NetworkX (how do I use existing algorithms on my multilayer network?)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Scale to large networks (when should I use sparse matrices? how much memory will this take?)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extend py3plex (how do I add my own algorithms?)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Network Types: Multilayer vs Multiplex}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:network-types-multilayer-vs-multiplex}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex supports two network types that determine how layers and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections are handled:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Networks} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network\_type=\textquotesingle{}multilayer\textquotesingle{}}}, default)

\sphinxAtStartPar
General multilayer networks where each layer can have a different set of nodes. No automatic coupling edges are created.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use when layers represent different node types (e.g., authors, papers, venues)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use when nodes naturally appear in only some layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges must be explicitly added

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Heterogeneous network: authors and papers are different node types}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multilayer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{author1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{paper1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
     \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{authors}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{papers}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex Networks} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network\_type=\textquotesingle{}multiplex\textquotesingle{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Special case where all layers share the same set of nodes but with different relationship types. After loading, coupling edges are automatically created between each node and its counterparts in other layers.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use when the same entities (people, cities) are connected via multiple relationship types

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Coupling edges are auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type=\textquotesingle{}coupling\textquotesingle{}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter coupling edges using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_edges(multiplex\_edges=False)}}

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Social network: same people, different relationship types}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends\PYGZus{}and\PYGZus{}colleagues.edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Coupling edges are auto\PYGZhy{}created between (Alice, friends) \PYGZlt{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} (Alice, colleagues)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get only explicit edges (exclude auto\PYGZhy{}coupling)}
\PYG{n}{explicit\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all edges including coupling}
\PYG{n}{all\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{The \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} Class}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:the-multi-layer-network-class}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The central data structure in py3plex is the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} class, which provides a high\sphinxhyphen{}level API for working with multilayer networks while maintaining full compatibility with NetworkX.


\paragraph{Basic Structure}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:basic-structure}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a multilayer network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} The underlying NetworkX graph}
\PYG{n}{nx\PYGZus{}graph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} MultiDiGraph or MultiGraph}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Layer management}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} List of layer names}
\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}map} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}map}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Layer name to ID mapping}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Key Components}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:key-components}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. Core NetworkX Graph}

\sphinxAtStartPar
At its heart, py3plex uses a NetworkX \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiDiGraph}} (for directed networks) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiGraph}} (for undirected networks) to store all nodes and edges.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access the underlying graph}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use any NetworkX function}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{2. Layer Encoding}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are internally encoded as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} tuples to distinguish the same logical node across different layers.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Node \PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{} in layer \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{} is stored as (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{})}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access all node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}pair} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}), ...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{3. Layer Mapping}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex maintains bidirectional mappings between layer names and internal layer IDs for efficient lookups.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get layer mapping}
\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}map} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}map}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}: 0, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}: 1, ...\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{4. Attributes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Node and edge attributes are stored directly in the underlying NetworkX graph and can be accessed and modified using standard NetworkX patterns.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add node with attributes}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{age}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{30}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edge with attributes}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.8}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{close}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Internal Representation}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:internal-representation}}

\paragraph{Node\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Pairs}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:node-layer-pairs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The key concept in py3plex’s internal model is the \sphinxstylestrong{node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair}: a tuple \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} that uniquely identifies a node in a specific layer.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Same logical node, different layers}

\PYG{n}{alice\PYGZus{}colleagues} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

This representation allows:

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different attributes per node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Efficient layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations

\end{itemize}
