\subsubsection{Supra\sphinxhyphen{}Adjacency Matrix}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:supra-adjacency-matrix}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix is a block matrix representation that encodes the entire multilayer network structure in one object. It respects the ordering of node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs (by layer, then by node within each layer), so always check your node ordering before interpreting row or column indices.


\paragraph{Mathematical Definition}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:mathematical-definition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a multilayer network with \(L\) layers and \(n_\alpha\) nodes in layer \(\alpha\), the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix \(\mathbf{S}\) stacks the intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer adjacency blocks with the inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling blocks. With layer\sphinxhyphen{}major ordering of node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs, it has the block form:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{S} = \begin{bmatrix}
A_1 & C_{12} & \cdots & C_{1L} \\
C_{21} & A_2 & \cdots & C_{2L} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
C_{L1} & C_{L2} & \cdots & A_L
\end{bmatrix}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^{n_\alpha \times n_\alpha}\) is the adjacency matrix of layer \(\alpha\) (intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C_{\alpha\beta} \in \mathbb{R}^{n_\alpha \times n_\beta}\) is the coupling matrix between layers \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) (inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n_\text{total} = \sum_{\alpha=1}^L n_\alpha\) is the total number of node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs across all layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The full matrix has size \(n_\text{total} \times n_\text{total}\)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In multiplex networks, \(n_\alpha\) is typically the same for all layers, so \(\mathbf{S}\) becomes an \((N \cdot L) \times (N \cdot L)\) matrix. For undirected networks, \(A_\alpha = A_\alpha^\top\) and \(C_{\alpha\beta} = C_{\beta\alpha}^\top\); for directed networks these blocks can be asymmetric. Identity coupling corresponds to \(C_{\alpha\beta} = \omega I\) (with coupling weight \(\omega\)) when layers share node identities.


\paragraph{Numeric Example}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:numeric-example}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider a simple multiplex network with 3 nodes (A, B, C) and 2 layers. In layer 1, A\sphinxhyphen{}B are connected. In layer 2, B\sphinxhyphen{}C are connected. The nodes are the same across layers (multiplex structure).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network structure:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Layer 1:        Layer 2:
A \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} B   C     A   B \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} C
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node ordering:} We order nodes as (A,L1), (B,L1), (C,L1), (A,L2), (B,L2), (C,L2).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer blocks:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer 1 adjacency matrix (A\(\sb{\text{1}}\)):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
     A   B   C
A [  0   1   0 ]
B [  1   0   0 ]
C [  0   0   0 ]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer 2 adjacency matrix (A\(\sb{\text{2}}\)):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
     A   B   C
A [  0   0   0 ]
B [  0   0   1 ]
C [  0   1   0 ]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling blocks (C\(\sb{\text{1}}\)\(\sb{\text{2}}\) and C\(\sb{\text{2}}\)\(\sb{\text{1}}\)):}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In a multiplex network, we typically add identity coupling—each node connects to itself across layers with the chosen coupling weight (here 1.0):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
C\(\sb{\text{1}}\)\(\sb{\text{2}}\) = C\(\sb{\text{2}}\)\(\sb{\text{1}}\)ᵀ =
     A   B   C
A [  1   0   0 ]
B [  0   1   0 ]
C [  0   0   1 ]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Full supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (6×6):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
          Layer 1        |     Layer 2
       A    B    C       |  A    B    C
L1  A [ 0    1    0      |  1    0    0 ]
    B [ 1    0    0      |  0    1    0 ]
    C [ 0    0    0      |  0    0    1 ]
   \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}|\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}+\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
L2  A [ 1    0    0      |  0    0    0 ]
    B [ 0    1    0      |  0    0    1 ]
    C [ 0    0    1      |  0    1    0 ]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The diagonal 3×3 blocks are the within\sphinxhyphen{}layer adjacencies (A\(\sb{\text{1}}\) and A\(\sb{\text{2}}\)). The off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal 3×3 blocks are the coupling matrices (C\(\sb{\text{1}}\)\(\sb{\text{2}}\) and C\(\sb{\text{2}}\)\(\sb{\text{1}}\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What this enables:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer shortest paths:} A path from (A,L1) to (C,L2) must go through B: (A,L1)\(\rightarrow\)(B,L1)\(\rightarrow\)(B,L2)\(\rightarrow\)(C,L2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Spectral methods:} Eigenvalues of S capture multilayer structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Matrix operations:} All linear algebra works on the full system

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Construction}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:construction}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Dense version (for small networks only)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Shape: (total\PYGZus{}nodes, total\PYGZus{}nodes)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} where total\PYGZus{}nodes = sum of nodes across all layers}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Shape: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{shape}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Memory Implications}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:memory-implications}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Let \(n_\text{total} = \sum_{\alpha=1}^L n_\alpha\) (the number of node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs). The supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix is \(n_\text{total} \times n_\text{total}\). If every layer has \(N\) nodes, then \(n_\text{total} = N \cdot L\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Worked estimates (assuming equal nodes per layer and 8\sphinxhyphen{}byte floats, ignoring library overhead):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Small network (100 nodes, 3 layers):} 300×300 = 90,000 entries \(\rightarrow\) \textasciitilde{}720 KB dense

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Medium network (1,000 nodes, 5 layers):} 5,000×5,000 = 25 million entries \(\rightarrow\) \textasciitilde{}200 MB dense

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Large network (10,000 nodes, 10 layers):} 100,000×100,000 = 10 billion entries \(\rightarrow\) \textasciitilde{}80 GB dense (impractical)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Always use sparse=True} for networks with more than \textasciitilde{}1,000 total node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs. Sparse matrices only store non\sphinxhyphen{}zero entries, reducing memory from \(O(n_\text{total}^2)\) potential entries to roughly \(O(\text{edges} + \text{coupling edges})\) actual non\sphinxhyphen{}zeros.

\subsubsection{How py3plex Uses NetworkX Under the Hood}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:how-py3plex-uses-networkx-under-the-hood}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is built on top of NetworkX, using it as the storage and algorithm backend. Understanding this architecture helps you leverage the full NetworkX ecosystem.


\paragraph{The Role of MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:the-role-of-multigraph-multidigraph}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Internally, py3plex stores all nodes and edges in a single NetworkX \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiGraph}} (for undirected) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiDiGraph}} (for directed networks). The multilayer structure is encoded through the node representation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} What you write in py3plex:}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} What\PYGZsq{}s actually stored in NetworkX:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes: (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}),}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}        (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{})}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edges: ((\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{})),}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}        ((\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}))}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This means:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{All NetworkX algorithms work directly} on the underlying graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuples are just nodes} to NetworkX—it doesn’t “know” about layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Attributes are stored as NetworkX attributes} and persist across operations

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Attribute Propagation}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:attribute-propagation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When you add nodes or edges with attributes, they’re stored in the NetworkX graph:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Node attributes}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{role}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{admin}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edge attributes}

\subsubsection{Design Trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:design-trade-offs}}

\paragraph{Node\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Pairs vs. Alternative Representations}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:node-layer-pairs-vs-alternative-representations}}

py3plex’s node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair representation is one of several possible designs. Here’s why it was chosen:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative 1: Separate graphs per layer}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Instead of py3plex:}

\PYG{n}{layer2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{layer1}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{layer2}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pros:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simple, familiar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Easy layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific analysis

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No representation of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Manual bookkeeping for cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Can’t compute multilayer paths or centrality directly

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative 2: Single graph with edge type attributes}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Instead of py3plex:}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{MultiGraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pros:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Single graph structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edges carry type information

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes can’t have layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same node in different contexts is the same node (can’t have Alice be central in one layer and peripheral in another)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges to the same node are impossible

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{py3plex approach: Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} py3plex representation:}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pros:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Preserves both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allows layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific node attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compatible with NetworkX algorithms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enables proper multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supports identity coupling and cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node names are tuples (less intuitive for simple cases)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Memory usage is multiplied by number of layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NetworkX algorithms treat node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs as independent nodes (need py3plex wrappers for multilayer semantics)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{py3plex’s choice:} The node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair approach was chosen because it correctly models multilayer semantics while maintaining NetworkX compatibility. The downsides (tuple names, memory) are acceptable trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs for the flexibility and correctness gained.


\paragraph{Consequences for Algorithm Implementation}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:consequences-for-algorithm-implementation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair design has implications:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer extraction is subsetting:} To get layer 1, you filter nodes where the layer component equals “layer1”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Identity coupling is explicit:} Cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges between the same entity must be added explicitly (or automatically in multiplex mode)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supra\sphinxhyphen{}matrix is derivable:} The supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix can be computed from the graph structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX algorithms work but need interpretation:} Betweenness on the full graph treats cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges as normal edges

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Consequences for I/O}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:consequences-for-i-o}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair representation affects serialization:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Standard formats work:} GraphML, GML can store tuple nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Human\sphinxhyphen{}readable formats need mapping:} Edgelists typically use separate columns for node and layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Arrow/Parquet are efficient:} Modern columnar formats handle the structure naturally

\end{enumerate}

\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}gml}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G\PYGZus{}export}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{output.gml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:performance-considerations}}

\paragraph{Sparse vs. Dense Matrices}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:sparse-vs-dense-matrices}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks, always use sparse matrix representations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good: Sparse matrix (efficient for large networks)}
\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Bad: Dense matrix (memory\PYGZhy{}intensive)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Only use for small networks (\PYGZlt{} 1000 nodes)}
\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj\PYGZus{}dense} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Memory Usage}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:memory-usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs mean that a node appearing in \(L\) layers occupies \(L\) times the memory of a single\sphinxhyphen{}layer network. For networks with many layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific analysis when possible

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use subnetwork extraction to work with smaller portions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Performance and Scalability Best Practices}}}} for optimization strategies

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Tensor\sphinxhyphen{}Like Indexing}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:tensor-like-indexing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can access neighbors and edge attribute dictionaries using tensor\sphinxhyphen{}like notation on the underlying NetworkX graph:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get some nodes and edges}
\PYG{n}{some\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{some\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access adjacency view for a node (neighbors and edge dictionaries)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Neighbors of }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{some\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{adjacency\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access node attributes explicitly}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Node attributes for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{some\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}attrs}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Design Principles}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:design-principles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex follows several key design principles:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. NetworkX Compatibility}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All operations maintain compatibility with NetworkX, allowing seamless use of the rich NetworkX ecosystem.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{2. Lazy Evaluation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Expensive operations like supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix construction are computed on demand and cached when appropriate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{3. Graceful Degradation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional features (like Infomap community detection or advanced visualizations) fail gracefully with informative error messages if dependencies are missing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{4. Extensibility}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The modular design makes it easy to extend py3plex with custom algorithms and visualizations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{5. Flexibility}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple ways to construct and manipulate networks to suit different workflows and use cases.


\subsubsection{Comparison with Other Representations}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:comparison-with-other-representations}}

\paragraph{Why Node\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Pairs?}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:why-node-layer-pairs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternative representations exist, but py3plex’s node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair approach offers key advantages over the two common options:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Separate graphs per layer:} Simple, but loses inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer information and requires manual bookkeeping for cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer operations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Single graph with edge type attributes:} Keeps everything in one graph, but cannot distinguish node context across layers or attach layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific node attributes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs (py3plex):} Preserves both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer structure, supports layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific attributes, and stays compatible with NetworkX algorithms while enabling multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Core Philosophy}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:core-philosophy}}

\paragraph{Simple, Off\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}Shelf Functionality}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:simple-off-the-shelf-functionality}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Principle:} Provide ready\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}use tools that work out of the box with minimal configuration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{In practice:} keep the first example minimal, without mandatory boilerplate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Simple, intuitive API}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} List format: [source, source\PYGZus{}layer, target, target\PYGZus{}layer, weight]}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Works immediately}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rationale:} Researchers and practitioners need tools that are easy to adopt without extensive setup or configuration. py3plex minimizes the barrier to entry for multilayer network analysis by keeping the first run frictionless.


\paragraph{NetworkX Compatibility}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:networkx-compatibility}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Principle:} Build on NetworkX rather than reinventing the wheel.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{In practice:} py3plex wraps a NetworkX graph and keeps it accessible.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Direct access to NetworkX graph}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use any NetworkX function}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{community}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rationale:} NetworkX is the de facto standard for network analysis in Python. By building on it, py3plex:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Leverages a mature, well\sphinxhyphen{}tested codebase

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Provides access to hundreds of NetworkX algorithms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ensures interoperability with the broader Python ecosystem (e.g., pandas, scipy)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces learning curve for users familiar with NetworkX, while adding multilayer semantics

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Modular Architecture}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:modular-architecture}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Principle:} Separate concerns into independent, composable modules.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Structure:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{hairball\PYGZus{}plot}

\sphinxstylestrong{Rationale:} Modular design allows users to:

\subsubsection{Implementation Principles}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:implementation-principles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These principles translate the philosophy into everyday coding patterns inside py3plex.


\paragraph{Flexibility}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:flexibility}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Principle:} Support multiple ways to accomplish tasks, accommodating different workflows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multiple ways to create networks}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Method 1: Direct edge addition}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Method 2: Load from file}

\sphinxstylestrong{In practice:} combine qualitative checks (structure) with quantitative ones (scores, timings).
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Benchmark scripts comparing to reference implementations when available

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validation against known network properties (e.g., degree sequences, connectivity)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Performance metrics for representative network sizes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recorded assumptions when a formal ground truth is unavailable

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rationale:} Validation ensures:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Implementations are correct

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Performance is acceptable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Results match published literature

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Algorithm Landscape}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:algorithm-landscape}}\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide provides a narrative overview of the algorithm families available in py3plex, highlighting when to use each type of algorithm for multilayer network analysis. It complements the API reference with plain\sphinxhyphen{}language guidance, trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs, and cues for multilayer specifics.


\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides algorithms in seven main categories that work on multilayer graphs encoded as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} pairs:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community Detection} \sphinxhyphen{} Finding groups of densely connected nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Centrality \& Importance} \sphinxhyphen{} Measuring node and edge importance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network Statistics} \sphinxhyphen{} Computing network\sphinxhyphen{}level and layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific metrics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Random Walks \& Embeddings} \sphinxhyphen{} Node representations and sampling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node Ranking \& Classification} \sphinxhyphen{} Ordering and classifying nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Visualization \& Layout} \sphinxhyphen{} Rendering and spatial arrangement

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Benchmarking \& Generation} \sphinxhyphen{} Testing and synthetic network creation

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For detailed parameter lists and API reference, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/algorithm_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Algorithm Roadmap}}}}. Use this page to choose a method family, then dive into the reference for parameters.


\subsubsection{Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Identify groups of nodes that are more densely connected to each other than to the rest of the network (within or across layers). In multilayer settings, decide whether communities should stay layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific or span layers via coupling (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega}} controls inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer links; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega = 0}} means layers do not interact).


\paragraph{When to Use}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:when-to-use}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use community detection when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Discover functional modules in biological networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find social groups in multilayer social networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify topical clusters in citation networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understand organizational structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detect anomalies (nodes that don’t fit any community)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Algorithm Families}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:algorithm-families}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modularity\sphinxhyphen{}Based Methods}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Best for:} Fast community detection on large networks

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Louvain} \sphinxhyphen{} Fast, greedy modularity optimization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Leiden} \sphinxhyphen{} Improved version of Louvain with better stability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Louvain} \sphinxhyphen{} Extends Louvain to multiple layers with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling (set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega \textgreater{} 0}} when layers should interact; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} tunes community resolution)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Fast (scales to millions of nodes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Easy to use (minimal parameters)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Resolution limit (may miss small communities)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Stochastic (different runs give different results)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Single\PYGZhy{}layer Louvain}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{best\PYGZus{}partition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer Louvain (gamma: resolution, omega: inter\PYGZhy{}layer coupling)}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Flow\sphinxhyphen{}Based Methods}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Best for:} Finding communities based on information flow

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infomap} \sphinxhyphen{} Minimizes description length of random walks (treat multilayer by adding explicit inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges or by aggregating first)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Walktrap} \sphinxhyphen{} Based on random walk distances (single\sphinxhyphen{}layer)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Theoretically grounded (information theory)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Finds hierarchical structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Slower than modularity methods

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ May require external binaries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Sensitive to how inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges are weighted (add or scale them explicitly before running on multilayer data)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Infomap (requires binary)}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/path/to/infomap}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Overlapping Community Detection}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Best for:} Networks where nodes belong to multiple communities

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NoRC} \sphinxhyphen{} Network of Ranked Communities (overlapping membership)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Clique Percolation} \sphinxhyphen{} Based on overlapping cliques

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) More realistic for many real networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Captures multi\sphinxhyphen{}role nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ More complex to interpret

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Computationally expensive

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} NoRC overlapping communities}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{NoRC\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Choosing a Community Detection Method}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:choosing-a-community-detection-method}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this decision tree (follow the first condition that applies):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Do you need overlapping communities?
├─ Yes \(\rightarrow\) NoRC or Clique Percolation (expect overlapping memberships)
└─ No
   └─ Is your network multilayer?
      ├─ Yes \(\rightarrow\) Multilayer Louvain or Leiden
      └─ No
         └─ What\PYGZsq{}s most important?
            ├─ Speed \(\rightarrow\) Louvain
            ├─ Stability \(\rightarrow\) Leiden
            └─ Theory / flow objective \(\rightarrow\) Infomap
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Centrality \& Importance}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:centrality-importance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Quantify the importance of nodes or edges in the network, per layer or aggregated. Decide whether to keep \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node, layer)}} pairs separate (preserves context) or to aggregate scores per entity after aligning identifiers.


\paragraph{When to Use}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:id1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use centrality measures when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify influential nodes (e.g., key proteins, opinion leaders)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find bottlenecks in flow networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prioritize nodes for intervention or study

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understand network vulnerability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Analyze node roles across layers

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Algorithm Families}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:id2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Degree\sphinxhyphen{}Based Centrality}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Measures:} Local connectivity

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Degree Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} Number of connections

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Degree} \sphinxhyphen{} Degree summed across layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Versatility} \sphinxhyphen{} Participation across layers (counts how many layers a node engages with; higher means broader presence)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Quick assessment of connectivity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identifying hubs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Local importance measures; supply \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weight}} if edge weights matter

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Single\PYGZhy{}layer degree centrality}
\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}cent} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer versatility}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}statistics} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mls}
\PYG{n}{versatility} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{versatility\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{centrality\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Distance\sphinxhyphen{}Based Centrality}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Measures:} Global position in network

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Closeness Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} Average distance to all other nodes (computed within connected components)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Betweenness Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} Fraction of shortest paths through node

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Harmonic Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} Harmonic mean of distances (stable on disconnected graphs)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identifying central nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finding information brokers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understanding information flow (run per connected component if closeness is used, or switch to harmonic variants)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Betweenness centrality}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Closeness centrality}
\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Eigenvector\sphinxhyphen{}Based Centrality}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Measures:} Importance based on connections to important nodes

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Eigenvector Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} First eigenvector of adjacency matrix (requires connectivity within each component; compute per component)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PageRank} \sphinxhyphen{} Google’s ranking algorithm (damping factor controls teleportation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{HITS} \sphinxhyphen{} Hubs and authorities (use on directed graphs)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ranking web pages or citations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finding influential nodes in social networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Authority/hub analysis

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} PageRank}
\PYG{n}{pagerank} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pagerank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Eigenvector centrality}
\PYG{n}{eigenvector} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{eigenvector\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Choosing a Centrality Measure}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:choosing-a-centrality-measure}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider these questions:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Local vs. Global?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Local \(\rightarrow\) Degree centrality
\sphinxhyphen{} Global \(\rightarrow\) Closeness or betweenness

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Direct connections or influence?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Direct \(\rightarrow\) Degree
\sphinxhyphen{} Influence \(\rightarrow\) PageRank or eigenvector

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network type?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Directed \(\rightarrow\) PageRank or HITS
\sphinxhyphen{} Undirected \(\rightarrow\) Any method
\sphinxhyphen{} Weighted \(\rightarrow\) Use weight\sphinxhyphen{}aware versions (pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weight}} to the function)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Computational cost?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Large network \(\rightarrow\) Degree or PageRank (fast)
\sphinxhyphen{} Small network \(\rightarrow\) Betweenness (expensive but informative)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer handling?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Keep per\sphinxhyphen{}layer scores when layer context matters
\sphinxhyphen{} Aggregate across layers only after aligning node identifiers

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Node Ranking \& Classification}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:node-ranking-classification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Order nodes by importance or predict node labels using network\sphinxhyphen{}derived features. In multilayer settings, decide whether to rank per layer or on an aggregated view, and whether to treat layers as features.


\paragraph{When to Use}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:id3}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use ranking or classification when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prioritize entities (recommendations, audits, interventions)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Score candidates for follow\sphinxhyphen{}up analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Train classifiers from structural features (centrality, embeddings)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combine multilayer evidence into a single ordering

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Approaches}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:approaches}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rank with centrality:} Use degree/PageRank/eigenvector (per layer or aggregated); normalize if layers differ in size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rank with random walks:} Use multilayer random\sphinxhyphen{}walk methods (e.g., MultiXRank) to blend within\sphinxhyphen{}layer and cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer signals; tune restart probability to control locality.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Classify with embeddings:} Generate node embeddings (Node2Vec/DeepWalk/LINE) then train a downstream classifier (e.g., scikit\sphinxhyphen{}learn). Include layer ID as a feature if labels depend on layer context.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Hybrid scores:} Combine statistical features (degree, clustering, participation coefficient) with embeddings for models that need both local and global cues.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:network-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Characterize network structure at the global, layer, or node level without committing to a specific downstream task. These checks help validate data quality before heavier modeling.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validate network models

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Monitor network evolution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detect anomalies

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\paragraph{Choosing Walk Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:choosing-walk-parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{walk\_length:}

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Medium (40\sphinxhyphen{}80): Balanced, standard choice

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
q = 1: Balanced

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
q \textgreater{} 1: BFS\sphinxhyphen{}like (stay in local neighborhood)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Create synthetic networks for testing and validation without risking production data.


\paragraph{When to Use}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:id8}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use synthetic network generation when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Test algorithm performance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validate implementations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create controlled experiments

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate training data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Benchmark scalability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Produce reproducible baselines (fix \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} when available)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Generator Families}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:generator-families}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Random Network Models}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Erdős\sphinxhyphen{}Rényi} \sphinxhyphen{} Random edges with fixed probability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Barabási\sphinxhyphen{}Albert} \sphinxhyphen{} Preferential attachment (scale\sphinxhyphen{}free)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Watts\sphinxhyphen{}Strogatz} \sphinxhyphen{} Small\sphinxhyphen{}world networks

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use ER for null models, BA for heavy\sphinxhyphen{}tailed degree distributions, and WS when you need clustering with short paths.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}

    \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{probability}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Benchmark Networks}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LFR benchmark (with ground\sphinxhyphen{}truth communities)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Configuration model (preserving degree distribution)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Block model (with planted partition)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pick LFR when you need ground truth for community detection, configuration for degree\sphinxhyphen{}preserving nulls, and block models for controllable meso\sphinxhyphen{}scale structure.

\paragraph{Louvain Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{reference/algorithm_reference:louvain-algorithm}}\label{\detokenize{reference/algorithm_reference:id2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Path:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{community\_detection.community\_louvain}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Functions:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{generate\_dendrogram(graph, partition, weight, resolution, randomize, random\_state)}} \sphinxhyphen{} Hierarchical communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{induced\_graph(partition, graph, weight)}} \sphinxhyphen{} Create quotient graph

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Best for:} Fast community detection on large single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complexity:} Roughly O(m) per iteration on sparse graphs; multiple passes are performed

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Runnable Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{louvain}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a network with clear community structure}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{karate\PYGZus{}club\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Detect communities}

\PYG{n}{overlap} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge\PYGZus{}overlap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{correlation} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{inter\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}correlation}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsection{DSL Reference}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:dsl-reference}}\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Complete reference for the py3plex DSL (Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language) for querying multilayer networks.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For task\sphinxhyphen{}oriented usage, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Query Multilayer Graphs with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL}}}}.
This page is a complete reference with all syntax and operators.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex DSL provides two interfaces:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{String syntax:} SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like queries for quick exploration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Builder API:} Type\sphinxhyphen{}safe Python interface for production code (autocomputes referenced metrics)

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{String Syntax Reference}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:string-syntax-reference}}

\paragraph{Basic Structure}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:basic-structure}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
SELECT \PYGZlt{}target\PYGZgt{} [FROM \PYGZlt{}layers\PYGZgt{}] [WHERE \PYGZlt{}conditions\PYGZgt{}] [COMPUTE \PYGZlt{}metrics\PYGZgt{}] [ORDER BY \PYGZlt{}field\PYGZgt{}] [LIMIT \PYGZlt{}n\PYGZgt{}]
[AT \PYGZlt{}timestamp\PYGZgt{} | DURING \PYGZlt{}start\PYGZgt{} TO \PYGZlt{}end\PYGZgt{}]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AT}} for a single time point and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DURING}} for closed intervals (ISO 8601 strings).


\paragraph{Targets}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:targets}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes}} — Select nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edges}} — Select edges (experimental; limited coverage support)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Layer Selection}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:layer-selection}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
FROM layer=\PYGZdq{}layer\PYGZus{}name\PYGZdq{}
FROM layers IN (\PYGZdq{}layer1\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}layer2\PYGZdq{})
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FROM}} is omitted, all layers are considered.


\paragraph{Conditions}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:conditions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Operators:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}} — Equal

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}} — Greater than

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} — Less than

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}=}} — Greater than or equal

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}=}} — Less than or equal

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!=}} — Not equal

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Logical operators:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AND}} — Both conditions must be true

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OR}} — Either condition must be true

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NOT}} — Negate a condition

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5
WHERE layer=\PYGZdq{}friends\PYGZdq{} AND degree \PYGZgt{} 3
WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5 OR betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality \PYGZgt{} 0.1
WHERE NOT layer=\PYGZdq{}spam\PYGZdq{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
String values must be wrapped in double quotes.


\paragraph{Compute Clause}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:compute-clause}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate metrics for selected nodes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
COMPUTE degree
COMPUTE degree betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality
COMPUTE clustering pagerank
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Available metrics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree}} — Node degree

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{betweenness\_centrality}} — Betweenness centrality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closeness\_centrality}} — Closeness centrality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clustering}} — Clustering coefficient

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pagerank}} — PageRank score

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} — Number of layers node appears in

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Metrics are computed after filtering and layer selection. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/algorithm_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Algorithm Roadmap}}}} for the complete metric list.


\paragraph{Order By}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:order-by}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ORDER BY degree
ORDER BY \PYGZhy{}degree  \PYGZsh{} Descending (prefix with \PYGZhy{})
ORDER BY betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify multiple keys in sequence; each key may be prefixed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}} for descending order.


\paragraph{Limit}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:limit}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
LIMIT 10
LIMIT 100
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Complete Examples}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:complete-examples}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes from specific layer}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes FROM layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 3 }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ORDER BY \PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{LIMIT 10}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

        \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}k}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{end\PYGZus{}grouping}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{coverage}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{exact}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Wildcard Layer Selection}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:wildcard-layer-selection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"*"{]}}} to select all layers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} All layers}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} All layers except \PYGZdq{}bots\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{bots}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Layer algebra still works}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{spam}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{verified}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{General Grouping}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:general-grouping}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Group by arbitrary attributes (not just layer):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Group by multiple attributes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{community}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{community}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}k}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{end\PYGZus{}grouping}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Coverage filtering is currently supported only for \sphinxstylestrong{node queries}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge queries with coverage will raise a clear \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DslExecutionError}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grouping requires computed attributes or inherent node properties (like layer)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Working with Results}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:working-with-results}}

\paragraph{Result Object}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:result-object}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QueryResult}} with items, computed attributes, and metadata:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Counts and identifiers}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{p}{)}    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} number of nodes/edges}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} first few nodes (use .edges for edge queries)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Attributes are aligned lists keyed by metric name}
\PYG{n}{degrees} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{attributes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{deg} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{zip}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{degrees}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{deg}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execution metadata (e.g., grouping, ordering)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{meta}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Convert to Pandas}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:convert-to-pandas}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multiindex}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{include\PYGZus{}grouping}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expand\_uncertainty=True}} to unpack UQ\sphinxhyphen{}aware metrics into multiple columns.


\subsubsection{Extensibility}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:extensibility}}

\paragraph{Custom Operators}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:custom-operators}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Register custom DSL operators:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{register\PYGZus{}operator}

\PYG{n+nd}{@register\PYGZus{}operator}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{my\PYGZus{}metric}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{my\PYGZus{}custom\PYGZus{}metric}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{context}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Compute custom metric for a node.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Your implementation}
    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{value}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{dev/code_architecture::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Architecture and Design}}}} for plugin development.


\subsubsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference:performance-considerations}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compute metrics once:} Don’t recompute in multiple queries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Filter early:} Use WHERE before COMPUTE

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Limit results:} Use LIMIT for large networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific:} Query single layers when possible

\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Layer Set Algebra}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:layer-set-algebra}}\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Layer Set Algebra feature provides a first\sphinxhyphen{}class, composable system for
selecting and manipulating layer sets in multilayer networks. Instead of manually
specifying lists of layers, you can use set\sphinxhyphen{}theoretic operations to express
complex layer selections.


\subsubsection{Why Layer Set Algebra?}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:why-layer-set-algebra}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In multilayer network analysis, you often need to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select “all layers except the coupling layer”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combine biological layers for aggregate analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find the intersection of layers where a node appears

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reuse layer group definitions across multiple queries

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Layer Set Algebra makes these operations expressive, composable, and safe.


\subsubsection{Quick Start}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:quick-start}}

\paragraph{Basic Operations}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:basic-operations}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{LayerSet}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create layer sets}
\PYG{n}{social} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LayerSet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{work} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LayerSet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Union: layers in either social OR work}
\PYG{n}{both} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{social} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{work}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Intersection: layers in both social AND work}
\PYG{n}{shared} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{social} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}} \PYG{n}{work}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Difference: layers in social but NOT in work}
\PYG{n}{social\PYGZus{}only} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{social} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{work}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Complement: all layers EXCEPT social}
\PYG{n}{not\PYGZus{}social} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{o}{\PYGZti{}}\PYG{n}{social}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{String Expressions}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:string-expressions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For convenience, you can write layer expressions as strings:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Parse from string}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LayerSet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{parse}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{* \PYGZhy{} coupling}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Or use L[...] syntax (auto\PYGZhy{}detects expressions)}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{* \PYGZhy{} coupling}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{(ppi | gene) \PYGZam{} disease}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social | work | hobby}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Integration with Queries}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:integration-with-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use layer sets in any DSL query:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Query nodes from all layers except coupling}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{* \PYGZhy{} coupling}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Complex layer selection}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{(social | work) \PYGZam{} \PYGZti{}coupling}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Set Operations}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:set-operations}}

\paragraph{Union: A | B}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:union-a-b}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The union operation combines layers from multiple sets.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Select nodes from social OR work layers}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social | work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Equivalent to:}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LayerSet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LayerSet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ASCII Venn Diagram:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐
│ Social  │     │  Work   │
│    ┌────┴─────┴────┐    │
│    │   RESULT      │    │
└────┴────────────────┴────┘
   A | B = \PYGZob{}social, work\PYGZcb{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Intersection: A \& B}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:intersection-a-b}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The intersection operation selects only layers present in both sets.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes that appear in both layer A AND layer B}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layerA \PYGZam{} layerB}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ASCII Venn Diagram:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐
│    A    │     │    B    │
│    ┌────┼─────┼────┐    │
│    │    │ RES │    │    │
└────┴────┼─────┼────┴────┘
          A \PYGZam{} B
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Difference: A \sphinxhyphen{} B}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:difference-a-b}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The difference operation removes layers in B from A.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} All layers except coupling}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{* \PYGZhy{} coupling}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Social layers but not bots}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social \PYGZhy{} bots}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ASCII Venn Diagram:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐
│    A    │     │    B    │
│  ┌──────┼─────┤         │
│  │ RES  │     │         │
└──┴──────┼─────┴─────────┘
   A \PYGZhy{} B = A without B
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Complement: \textasciitilde{}A}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:complement-a}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The complement operation returns all layers except those in A.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Everything except social layer}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{o}{\PYGZti{}}\PYG{n}{LayerSet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Equivalent to:}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{* \PYGZhy{} social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ASCII Venn Diagram:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
┌─────────────────────────┐
│     All Layers (*)      │
│                         │
│  ┌───────┐              │
│  │   A   │    RESULT    │
│  └───────┘              │

\item {}

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{enumerate}

    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o}{!=} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{coupling}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}
