\subsubsection{Why Layer Set Algebra Matters}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:why-layer-set-algebra-matters}}

\paragraph{For Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:for-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer networks have a unique challenge: layer selection is a first\sphinxhyphen{}class
operation, not an afterthought. Traditional graph analysis tools don’t provide
built\sphinxhyphen{}in support for layer algebra, forcing users to write imperative code
with loops and conditionals.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer Set Algebra brings the following benefits:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expressiveness}: Complex layer selections become one\sphinxhyphen{}liners

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Composability}: Combine layer expressions with set operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reusability}: Define named groups once, use everywhere

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Safety}: Late evaluation with validation at execution time

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Maintainability}: Clear, declarative code is easier to understand

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Algebraic Properties}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:algebraic-properties}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer Set Algebra follows standard set theory laws:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Idempotence}: A | A = A, A \& A = A

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Commutativity}: A | B = B | A, A \& B = B \& A

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Associativity}: (A | B) | C = A | (B | C)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Distributivity}: A \& (B | C) = (A \& B) | (A \& C)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{De Morgan’s Laws}: \textasciitilde{}(A | B) = \textasciitilde{}A \& \textasciitilde{}B, \textasciitilde{}(A \& B) = \textasciitilde{}A | \textasciitilde{}B

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complement}: A | \textasciitilde{}A = {\color{red}\bfseries{}*}, A \& \textasciitilde{}A = ∅

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These properties enable query optimization and reasoning about layer selections.

\subsubsection{Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:troubleshooting}}

\paragraph{Common Issues}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:common-issues}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. Empty Layer Set Warning}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nonexistent}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{resolve}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} UserWarning: Layer expression resolved to empty set}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution}: Check layer names, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{warn\_empty=False}} to suppress, or use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict=True}} to raise an error instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{2. Unknown Layer Error}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{typo\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{resolve}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{strict}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} UnknownLayerError: Layer \PYGZsq{}typo\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZsq{} not found}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution}: Verify layer names with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network.layers}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network.get\_layers()}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{3. Syntax Error in Expression}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social \PYGZam{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Missing right operand}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} DslSyntaxError: Unexpected end of expression}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution}: Check expression syntax, ensure all operators have operands.


\paragraph{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{reference/layer_set_algebra:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Named Groups} for complex layer sets you’ll reuse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prefer String Expressions} for readability: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"* \sphinxhyphen{} coupling"{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Complement} instead of listing all other layers: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}LayerSet("exclude")}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Document Layer Groups} with comments explaining their purpose

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Test Layer Resolution} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.explain(network)}} before running expensive queries

\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}First Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:uncertainty-first-statistics}}\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex implements an \sphinxstylestrong{uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}first statistics system} where every statistic is represented as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(value + uncertainty + provenance)}}. This design makes uncertainty a core part of statistics computation, not an afterthought.


\paragraph{Key Principles}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:key-principles}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Every statistic is a StatValue}: No plain floats/ints escaping internal computation paths. Even deterministic values carry \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Delta(0)}} uncertainty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Uncertainty is first\sphinxhyphen{}class}: Uncertainty can be summarized, sampled, propagated through arithmetic, and used in queries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Backward compatible}: Existing code expecting floats works via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float(statvalue)}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Registry discipline}: Statistics must have an uncertainty model to be registered.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reproducible}: Random processes (bootstrap/MC) support explicit seeds tracked in provenance.

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Core Components}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:core-components}}

\paragraph{StatValue}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:statvalue}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatValue}} is the fundamental container for statistics:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{stats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{StatValue}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Delta}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Provenance}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a deterministic statistic}
\PYG{n}{sv} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{StatValue}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{value}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.42}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{uncertainty}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{Delta}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{provenance}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{Provenance}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{delta}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access value}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{float}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 0.42}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Query uncertainty}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 0.0}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ci}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.95}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (0.42, 0.42)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{robustness}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1.0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key Methods:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float(sv)}}: Convert to point estimate (backward compatibility)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sv.mean()}}: Alias for value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sv.std()}}: Standard deviation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sv.ci(level=0.95)}}: Confidence interval

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sv.robustness()}}: Robustness score in {[}0, 1{]}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sv.to\_json\_dict()}}: Serialize to JSON

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Uncertainty Models}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:uncertainty-models}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Five concrete uncertainty models are provided:


\subparagraph{Delta}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:delta}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Deterministic or known\sphinxhyphen{}precision uncertainty.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{stats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Delta}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Perfect certainty}
\PYG{n}{d} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Delta}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Small known error}

\sphinxstylestrong{Properties:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}: Returns sigma

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci(level)}}: Returns symmetric interval based on sigma

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample(n, seed)}}: Returns constant samples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Propagation: Analytic error propagation when both are Delta

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Gaussian}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:gaussian}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normal distribution uncertainty.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{stats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Gaussian}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Exact CI computation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Properties:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci(level)}}: Exact Gaussian CI using z\sphinxhyphen{}scores

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample(n, seed)}}: Generates Gaussian samples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Bootstrap}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:bootstrap}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Store bootstrap samples (relative to point estimate)}

\PYG{n}{b} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Bootstrap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{samples}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute CI from percentiles}
\PYG{n}{low}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{high} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{b}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ci}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.95}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Properties:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}: Sample standard deviation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci(level)}}: Percentile\sphinxhyphen{}based CI

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample(n, seed)}}: Resample from stored samples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Statistics Registry}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:statistics-registry}}

The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticsRegistry}} enforces that every registered statistic has an uncertainty model.

\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{degree\PYGZus{}uncertainty}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{kwargs}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{Delta}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Deterministic}

\PYG{n}{spec} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{StatisticSpec}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{estimator}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{compute\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{uncertainty\PYGZus{}model}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}uncertainty}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{assumptions}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{deterministic}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{supports}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{directed}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{weighted}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Arithmetic with Uncertainty}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:arithmetic-with-uncertainty}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
StatValue supports arithmetic operations with automatic uncertainty propagation.

\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:basic-operations}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{stats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{StatValue}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Gaussian}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Provenance}

\PYG{n}{sv2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{StatValue}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Gaussian}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.15}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Provenance}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{gaussian}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Addition}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sv1} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{sv2}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{float}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 3.0}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZti{}0.180 (sqrt(0.1\(\sp{\text{2}}\) + 0.15\(\sp{\text{2}}\)))}

\paragraph{Scalar Operations}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:scalar-operations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
StatValue supports operations with scalars:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{sv} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{StatValue}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Gaussian}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Provenance}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{gaussian}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Scalar addition}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sv} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 5.0 (uncertainty unchanged)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Scalar multiplication}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sv} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 4.0 (uncertainty scaled)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Scalar division}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sv} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1.0 (uncertainty scaled)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Propagation Rules}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:propagation-rules}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Delta + Delta}: Analytic error propagation (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{σ\_sum = sqrt(σ1\(\sp{\text{2}}\) + σ2\(\sp{\text{2}}\))}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Gaussian + Gaussian}: Exact propagation for addition/subtraction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complex operations}: Monte Carlo propagation (4096 samples by default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Scalar operations}: Direct computation, uncertainty scaled appropriately

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Filtering and Queries}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:filtering-and-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Statistics with uncertainty can be filtered using selectors:


\paragraph{Selector Syntax}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:selector-syntax}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{attribute\_\_component\_\_operator=value}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Components:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}: Point estimate (default if omitted)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}}: Standard deviation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci95\_\_width}}: Width of 95\% CI

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{robustness}}: Robustness score

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Operators:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt}}: Greater than

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gte}}: Greater than or equal

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt}}: Less than

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lte}}: Less than or equal

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq}}: Equal

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{reference/uncertainty_first_statistics:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Always use StatValue internally}: Even for deterministic stats, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Delta(0)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Provide uncertainty models}: Every registered statistic must have one

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use seeds for reproducibility}: Pass explicit seeds to bootstrap/MC operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choose appropriate models}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Deterministic \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Delta(0)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Known distribution \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Gaussian}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Empirical estimation \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bootstrap}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Empirical}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No distribution assumption \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Interval}}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Check robustness}: Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sv.robustness()}} to assess reliability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Export uncertainty}: Include uncertainty columns in exports for downstream analysis

\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{Core Modules}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:core-modules}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Main class for multilayer network analysis and manipulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This class provides a comprehensive toolkit for creating, analyzing, and
visualizing multilayer networks where nodes can exist in multiple layers
and edges can connect nodes within or across layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported Network Types (network\_type parameter):}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multilayer} (default): General multilayer networks with arbitrary
layer structure. Each layer can have a different set of nodes.
Suitable for heterogeneous networks (e.g., authors\sphinxhyphen{}papers\sphinxhyphen{}venues)
or networks where nodes naturally appear in only some layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multiplex}: Special case where all layers share the same node set
but with different edge types. After loading a network, automatic
coupling edges are created between each node and its counterparts
in other layers. Suitable for social networks with multiple
relationship types (e.g., friend, colleague, family layers).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Choosing the Right Network Type:}
\sphinxlineitem{Key Features:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dict\sphinxhyphen{}based API for adding nodes and edges (see add\_nodes() and add\_edges())

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NetworkX interoperability via to\_networkx() and from\_networkx()

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple I/O formats (edgelist, GML, GraphML, gpickle, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualization methods for multilayer layouts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection and centrality analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk and embedding generation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Hypergraph Support:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This class does NOT natively support true hypergraphs (edges connecting
more than two nodes). For hypergraph\sphinxhyphen{}like structures, consider:
\sphinxhyphen{} Using bipartite projections (nodes and hyperedges as separate node types)
\sphinxhyphen{} The incidence gadget encoding via to\_homogeneous\_hypergraph()
\sphinxhyphen{} External hypergraph libraries with conversion utilities

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes in multilayer networks are represented as (node\_id, layer) tuples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use add\_nodes() and add\_edges() with dict format for easiest interaction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See examples/ directory for usage patterns and best practices

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add edges to the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method supports multiple input formats for specifying edges between nodes
in different layers. The most common format is dict\sphinxhyphen{}based.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_dict\_list}} \textendash{} Edge data in one of the supported formats (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Format of edge data (‘dict’, ‘list’, or ‘px\_edge’)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns self for method chaining

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
self

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported Formats:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dict format (recommended):}
{\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}}{\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}}python
\{
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
‘source’: ‘node1’,          \# Source node ID
‘target’: ‘node2’,          \# Target node ID
‘source\_type’: ‘layer1’,    \# Source layer name
‘target\_type’: ‘layer2’,    \# Target layer name (can be same as source)
‘weight’: 1.0,              \# Optional: edge weight
‘type’: ‘interaction’       \# Optional: edge type/label
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{List format:}
\sphinxtitleref{{[}node1, layer1, node2, layer2{]}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{px\_edge format:}
\sphinxtitleref{((node1, layer1), (node2, layer2), \{‘weight’: 1.0\})}

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add nodes to the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes in a multilayer network are identified by both their ID and the layer
they belong to. This method adds nodes using a dict\sphinxhyphen{}based format.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_dict\_list}} \textendash{} Node data as a dict or list of dicts (see format below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Format of node data (currently only ‘dict’ is supported)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns self for method chaining

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
self

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Dict Format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}}{\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}}python
\{
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
‘source’: ‘node\_id’,    \# Node identifier (can be string or number)
‘type’: ‘layer\_name’,   \# Layer this node belongs to
‘weight’: 1.0,          \# Optional: node weight/importance
‘label’: ‘display’      \# Optional: display label
\# … any other node attributes
\end{quote}

\end{description}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci curvature on the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method provides flexible computation of Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci curvature
at different levels of the multilayer network:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{core mode}: Compute curvature on the aggregated (flattened) network

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{layers mode}: Compute curvature separately for each layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{supra mode}: Compute curvature on the full supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph including
both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mode}} \textendash{} Scope of computation. Options: “core”, “layers”, “supra”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer identifiers to process (only for mode=”layers”).
If None, all layers are processed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci parameter in {[}0, 1{]} controlling the mass
distribution. Default: 0.5.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight\_attr}} \textendash{} Name of edge attribute containing weights. Default: “weight”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{curvature\_attr}} \textendash{} Name of edge attribute to store curvature values.
Default: “ricciCurvature”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Verbosity level. Options: “INFO”, “DEBUG”, “ERROR”. Default: “ERROR”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{backend\_kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional keyword arguments for OllivierRicci constructor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{inplace}} \textendash{} If True, update internal graphs. If False, return new graphs
without modifying the network. Default: True.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{interlayer\_weight}} \textendash{} Weight for inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling edges (only for
mode=”supra”). Default: 1.0.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping scope identifiers to NetworkX graphs with computed
curvatures:
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”core”: \{“core”: graph\_with\_curvature\}
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”layers”: \{layer\_id: graph\_with\_curvature, …\}
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”supra”: \{“supra”: supra\_graph\_with\_curvature\}

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{RicciBackendNotAvailable}} \textendash{} If GraphRicciCurvature is not installed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If mode is invalid or layers contains invalid identifiers.

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci flow on the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ricci flow iteratively adjusts edge weights based on their Ricci curvature,
effectively revealing and enhancing community structure. After Ricci flow,
edges with negative curvature (community boundaries) have reduced weights,
while edges with positive curvature have increased weights.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mode}} \textendash{} Scope of computation. Options: “core”, “layers”, “supra”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer identifiers to process (only for mode=”layers”).
If None, all layers are processed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci parameter in {[}0, 1{]}. Default: 0.5.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of Ricci flow iterations. Default: 10.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} \textendash{} Ricci flow method. Options: “OTD” (Optimal Transport Distance,
recommended), “ATD” (Average Transport Distance). Default: “OTD”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight\_attr}} \textendash{} Name of edge attribute containing weights. After Ricci flow,
these weights are updated to reflect the flow metric.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{curvature\_attr}} \textendash{} Name of edge attribute for curvature values.
Default: “ricciCurvature”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Verbosity level. Options: “INFO”, “DEBUG”, “ERROR”. Default: “ERROR”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{backend\_kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional keyword arguments for OllivierRicci constructor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{inplace}} \textendash{} If True, update internal graphs. If False, return new graphs.
Default: True.

\sphinxAtStartPar

mode=”supra”). Default: 1.0.

\end{itemize}

Convert a temporal edge DataFrame to edge tuple list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extracts edges from a pandas DataFrame with temporal/activity information
and converts them to a list of edge tuples suitable for network construction.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_df}} \textendash{} pandas DataFrame with columns:
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_first: Source node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_second: Target node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} layer\_name: Layer identifier

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{List of edge tuples in format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
(node\_first, node\_second, layer\_first, layer\_second, weight)
where weight is always 1

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
list

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All values are converted to strings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edges are assigned weight=1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both source and target are assumed to be in the same layer

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Execute a DSL query on this multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a convenience method that provides first\sphinxhyphen{}class access to the
py3plex DSL (Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language) for querying multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Supports both SELECT and MATCH queries:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{SELECT queries:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
net.execute\_query(‘SELECT nodes WHERE layer=”transport”’)
net.execute\_query(‘SELECT * FROM nodes IN LAYER “ppi” WHERE degree \textgreater{} 10’)

\sphinxlineitem{MATCH queries (Cypher\sphinxhyphen{}like):}
\sphinxAtStartPar
net.execute\_query(‘MATCH (g:Gene)\sphinxhyphen{}{[}r{]}\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}(t:Gene) RETURN g, t’)
net.execute\_query(‘MATCH (a)\sphinxhyphen{}{[}e{]}\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}(b) IN LAYER “ppi” WHERE a.degree \textgreater{} 5 RETURN a, b’)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{query}} \textendash{} DSL query string

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For SELECT queries: ‘nodes’ or ‘edges’ list, ‘count’, optional ‘computed’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For MATCH queries: ‘bindings’ list, ‘count’, ‘type’

\end{itemize}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary containing query results

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.dsl.DSLSyntaxError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{DSLSyntaxError}}}}} \textendash{} If query syntax is invalid

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.dsl.DSLExecutionError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{DSLExecutionError}}}}} \textendash{} If query cannot be executed

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }                \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\index{fill\_tmp\_with\_edges() (py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method)@\spxentry{fill\_tmp\_with\_edges()}\spxextra{py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network.fill_tmp_with_edges}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fill temporary layer graphs with edges from a DataFrame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Populates the emptied layer graphs (created by remove\_layer\_edges) with
edges from a temporal/activity DataFrame. Useful for temporal network
analysis where edge sets change over time.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_df}} \textendash{} pandas DataFrame with columns:
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_first: Source node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_second: Target node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} layer\_name: Layer identifier

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires remove\_layer\_edges() to be called first

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edges are grouped by layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modifies self.tmp\_layers in place

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each edge is stored as ((node\_first, layer), (node\_second, layer))

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{AttributeError}} \textendash{} If self.tmp\_layers doesn’t exist (call remove\_layer\_edges first)

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These examples require proper network setup and are for illustration only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Iterate over edges in the network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method behaves differently based on the network\_type:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multilayer}: Returns all edges without filtering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multiplex}: By default, filters out coupling edges (auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated
inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges connecting each node to itself in other layers).
Set multiplex\_edges=True to include coupling edges.

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{data}} \textendash{} If True, return edge data along with edge tuples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multiplex\_edges}} \textendash{} If True, include coupling edges in multiplex networks.
Only relevant when network\_type=’multiplex’. Coupling edges are
automatically added to connect each node to its counterparts
in other layers.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Yields}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge tuples, optionally with data. For multiplex networks with
multiplex\_edges=False, coupling edges are excluded.

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If network\_type is not ‘multilayer’ or ‘multiplex’.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix in the specified sparse format.
This method provides a tensor\sphinxhyphen{}like view of the multilayer network,
useful for mathematical analysis and matrix\sphinxhyphen{}based algorithms.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sparsity\_type}} \textendash{} Sparse matrix format to use. Options include:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘bsr’ (default): Block Sparse Row format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘csr’: Compressed Sparse Row format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘csc’: Compressed Sparse Column format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘coo’: Coordinate format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘lil’: List of Lists format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘dok’: Dictionary of Keys format

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix in specified format

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}

scipy.sparse matrix

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_network}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{input\_file}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{directed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{input\_type}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}gml\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{label\_delimiter}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}\textquotesingle{}}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load a network from file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method loads and prepares a given network. The behavior depends on
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network\_type}} set during initialization:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multilayer}: Network is loaded as\sphinxhyphen{}is. No automatic edges are added.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multiplex}: After loading, coupling edges are automatically created
between each node and its counterparts in other layers. These edges
have type=’coupling’ and can be filtered via get\_edges().

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_file}} \textendash{} Path to the network file to load

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether the network is directed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Format of the input file. Supported values:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘gml’: Graph Modeling Language format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘graphml’: GraphML XML format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘edgelist’: Simple edge list (source target {[}weight{]})
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiedgelist’: Multilayer edge list (node1 layer1 node2 layer2 weight)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiplex\_edges’: Multiplex format (layer node1 node2 weight)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiplex\_folder’: Folder with layer files
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘gpickle’: Python pickle format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘nx’: NetworkX graph object
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘sparse’: Sparse matrix format

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{label\_delimiter}} \textendash{} Delimiter used to separate layer names in node labels

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for method chaining. Populates self.core\_network, self.labels,
and self.activity.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For multiplex networks, use input\_type=’multiplex\_edges’ or
‘multiplex\_folder’ with network\_type=’multiplex’ to get automatic
coupling edges.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load multilayer network (no automatic coupling)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multilayer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{data.gml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{gml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load multiplex network (automatic coupling edges)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{data.edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

For example, for betweenness\_centrality you can pass:
\sphinxhyphen{} weight: Edge attribute to use as weight
\sphinxhyphen{} normalized: Whether to normalize betweenness values
\sphinxhyphen{} distance: Edge attribute to use as distance (for closeness\_centrality)

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Unweighted betweenness centrality
centralities = network.monoplex\_nx\_wrapper(“betweenness\_centrality”)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Weighted betweenness centrality
centralities = network.monoplex\_nx\_wrapper(“betweenness\_centrality”, kwargs=\{“weight”: “weight”\})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# With multiple parameters
centralities = network.monoplex\_nx\_wrapper(“betweenness\_centrality”,
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
kwargs=\{“weight”: “weight”, “normalized”: True\})
\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{remove\_layer\_edges() (py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method)@\spxentry{remove\_layer\_edges()}\spxextra{py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network.remove_layer_edges}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{remove\_layer\_edges}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove all edges from separate layer graphs while keeping nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method creates empty copies of each layer graph with all nodes intact
but no edges. Useful for reconstructing networks with different edge sets
or for temporal network analysis.
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires split\_to\_layers() to be called first

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stores empty layer graphs in self.tmp\_layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Original graphs in self.separate\_layers remain unchanged

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All nodes and their attributes are preserved

Save the network to a file in various formats.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method exports the multilayer network to different file formats
for persistence, sharing, or use with other tools.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{output\_file}} \textendash{} Path where the network should be saved

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{output\_type}} \textendash{} Format for saving (‘edgelist’, ‘multiedgelist’,
‘multiedgelist\_encoded’, or ‘gpickle’)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported Formats:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘edgelist’: Simple edge list format (standard NetworkX)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘multiedgelist’: Multilayer edge list with layer information

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘multiedgelist\_encoded’: Multilayer edge list with integer encoding

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘gpickle’: Python pickle format (preserves all attributes)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Serialize the multilayer network to an edgelist file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Converts the network to a numeric edgelist format suitable for external tools
and algorithms that require integer node/layer identifiers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edgelist\_file}} \textendash{} Path to output edgelist file (default: “./tmp/tmpedgelist.txt”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tmp\_folder}} \textendash{} Temporary folder for intermediate files (default: “tmp”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{out\_folder}} \textendash{} Output folder for results (default: “out”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multiplex}} \textendash{} If True, use multiplex format (node layer node layer weight)
If False, use simple edgelist format (node1 node2 weight)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Inverse node mapping (numeric\_id \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} original\_node\_tuple)}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this to decode results from external algorithms

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{File Formats:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplex format: node1\_id layer1\_id node2\_id layer2\_id weight

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simple format: node1\_id node2\_id weight

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates tmp\_folder and out\_folder if they don’t exist

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are mapped to sequential integers starting from 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layers are mapped to sequential integers starting from 0 (multiplex mode)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edges have weight 1 unless explicitly specified

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example requires file output \sphinxhyphen{} for illustration only.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{multiplex}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use node\PYGZus{}mapping to decode results}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_homogeneous\_hypergraph}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Transform a multiplex network into a homogeneous graph using incidence gadget encoding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method encodes the multiplex structure where each layer is represented by
a unique prime number signature. Each edge becomes an edge\sphinxhyphen{}node connected to
its endpoints and a cycle of length prime\sphinxhyphen{}1 that encodes the layer.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tuple (H, node\_mapping, edge\_info)} \textendash{}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{H}{[}networkx.Graph{]}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Homogeneous unlabeled graph encoding the multiplex structure.

\sphinxlineitem{node\_mapping}{[}dict{]}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Maps each original node to its vertex\sphinxhyphen{}node in H.

\sphinxlineitem{edge\_info}{[}dict{]}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mapping from each edge\sphinxhyphen{}node in H to its (layer, endpoints) tuple.

\end{description}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples} \textendash{} Example requires sympy dependency \sphinxhyphen{} for illustration only.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} network = multi\_layer\_network(directed=False)  \# doctest} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{+SKIP})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} network.add\_nodes({[}\{‘source’} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{‘1’, ‘type’: ‘A’\}, \{‘source’: ‘2’, ‘type’: ‘A’\}{]}, input\_type=’dict’)  \# doctest: +SKIP})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} network.add\_edges({[}\{‘source’} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{‘1’, ‘target’: ‘2’, ‘source\_type’: ‘A’, ‘target\_type’: ‘A’\}{]}, input\_type=’dict’)  \# doctest: +SKIP})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} H, node\_map, edge\_info = network.to\_homogeneous\_hypergraph()  \# doctest} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{+SKIP})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} print(f”Homogeneous graph has \{len(H.nodes())\} nodes”)  \# doctest} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{+SKIP})

\end{itemize}


\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This transformation uses prime\sphinxhyphen{}based signatures to encode layers:
\sphinxhyphen{} Each layer is assigned a unique prime number (2, 3, 5, 7, …)
\sphinxhyphen{} Each edge in layer with prime p is connected to a cycle of length p
\sphinxhyphen{} The cycle structure uniquely identifies the layer

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert the multilayer network to a NetworkX graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a copy of the core network as a NetworkX graph. The returned graph
preserves all node and edge attributes, including layer information for
multilayer networks (where nodes are typically (node\_id, layer) tuples).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A NetworkX graph (MultiGraph or MultiDiGraph depending on network type)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
nx.Graph

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{nx\PYGZus{}graph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}networkx}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nx\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{\PYGZlt{}class \PYGZsq{}networkx.classes.multigraph.MultiGraph\PYGZsq{}\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For multilayer networks, nodes are tuples: (node\_id, layer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edge attributes (weight, type, etc.) are preserved

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned graph is a copy, not a reference

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualize the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Supports multiple visualization styles:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘diagonal’: Layer\sphinxhyphen{}centric diagonal layout with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘hairball’: Aggregate hairball plot of all layers
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘flow’ or ‘alluvial’: Layered flow visualization with horizontal bands
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘sankey’: Sankey diagram showing inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer flow strength

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Performance Notes:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks (\textgreater{}500 nodes), visualization performance may degrade:
\sphinxhyphen{} Layout computation can be slow (O(n\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) for force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layouts)
\sphinxhyphen{} Rendering many edges is memory and CPU intensive
\sphinxhyphen{} Consider filtering or sampling for exploratory visualization
\sphinxhyphen{} Use simpler layouts or increase layout iteration limits

\sphinxAtStartPar
Approximate rendering times on typical hardware:
\sphinxhyphen{} 100 nodes: \textless{}1 second
\sphinxhyphen{} 500 nodes: 5\sphinxhyphen{}10 seconds
\sphinxhyphen{} 1000 nodes: 30\sphinxhyphen{}60 seconds
\sphinxhyphen{} 5000+ nodes: Several minutes, may run out of memory

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

Visualize the aggregated core network using Ricci\sphinxhyphen{}flow\sphinxhyphen{}based layout.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method is a high\sphinxhyphen{}level wrapper for Ricci\sphinxhyphen{}flow\sphinxhyphen{}based visualization
of the core (aggregated) network. It automatically computes Ricci flow
if not already done and creates an informative layout that emphasizes
geometric structure and communities.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of Ricci flow iterations. Default: 10.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_type}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm (“mds”, “spring”, “spectral”). Default: “mds”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{dim}} \textendash{} Dimensionality of layout (2 or 3). Default: 2.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional arguments passed to visualize\_multilayer\_ricci\_core.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualize individual layers using Ricci\sphinxhyphen{}flow\sphinxhyphen{}based layouts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method creates visualizations of individual layers with layouts
derived from Ricci flow. Layers can share a common coordinate system
(for easier comparison) or have independent layouts.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer identifiers to visualize. If None, uses all layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci parameter. Default: 0.5.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of Ricci flow iterations. Default: 10.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_type}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm. Default: “mds”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{share\_layout}} \textendash{} If True, use shared coordinates across layers. Default: True.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional arguments passed to visualize\_multilayer\_ricci\_layers.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple of (figure, layer\_positions\_dict).

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{RicciBackendNotAvailable}} \textendash{} If GraphRicciCurvature is not installed.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method visualizes the complete multilayer structure including both
intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (within layers) and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (coupling between
layers) using a layout derived from Ricci flow.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_type}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm. Default: “mds”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{dim}} \textendash{} Dimensionality (2 or 3). Default: 2.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional arguments passed to visualize\_multilayer\_ricci\_supra.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysiglinewithargsret

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{input\_name}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{directed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}MultiGraph\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }MultiDiGraph\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }None\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parse an edgelist file with multiple edge types.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads a text file where each line represents an edge, optionally with weights
and edge types. Lines starting with ‘\#’ are treated as comments.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{File Format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
node1 node2 {[}weight{]} {[}edge\_type{]}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lines starting with ‘\#’ are ignored (comments)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_name}} \textendash{} Path to edgelist file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to create a directed graph

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
(parsed\_graph, None for labels)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple{[}Union{[}nx.MultiGraph, nx.MultiDiGraph{]}, None{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All nodes are assigned to a “null” layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default weight is 1 if not specified

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge type is optional (4th column)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Handles both 2\sphinxhyphen{}column (node pairs) and 3+ column formats

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} File content:}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} A B 1.0 friendship}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} B C 2.0 collaboration}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{parse\PYGZus{}edgelist\PYGZus{}multi\PYGZus{}types}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edges.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}  
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parse a multiplex edgelist file where each line specifies layer and edge.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{File Format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
layer node1 node2 {[}weight{]}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each line: layer\_id source\_node target\_node {[}optional\_weight{]}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_name}} \textendash{} Path to multiplex edgelist file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to create a directed graph

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
(parsed\_graph, None for labels)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple{[}Union{[}nx.MultiGraph, nx.MultiDiGraph{]}, None{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each edge belongs to a specific layer (first column)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are represented as (node\_id, layer) tuples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default weight is 1 if not specified

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edges have type=’default’ attribute

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically couples nodes across layers for multiplex structure

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} File content:}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} layer1 A B 1.5}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} layer2 A B 2.0}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} layer1 B C 1.0}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{parse\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}  
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Creates nodes: (A, layer1), (A, layer2), (B, layer1), etc.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parse a folder containing multiplex network files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Expects a folder with specific file formats for edges, layers, and optional activity.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Expected Files:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\color{red}\bfseries{}*}.edges: Edge information (format: layer\_id node1 node2 weight)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
layers.txt: Layer definitions (format: layer\_id layer\_name)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
activity.txt: Optional temporal activity (format: node1 node2 timestamp layer\_name)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_folder}} \textendash{} Path to folder containing multiplex network files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to create a directed graph

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Union{[}nx.MultiGraph, nx.MultiDiGraph{]}: Parsed multilayer graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
None: Placeholder for labels (not used)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pd.DataFrame: Time series activity data (empty if no activity.txt)

\end{itemize}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple containing

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses glob to find files with specific extensions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer mapping is built from layers.txt

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Activity data is optional and returned as pandas DataFrame

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are represented as (node\_id, layer\_id) tuples

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Folder structure:}

{{ $\rightarrow$ Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}Graph\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }None\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parse SPIN format edgelist file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
SPIN format includes node pairs with edge tags and optional weights.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{File Format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
node1 node2 tag {[}weight{]}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each line: source\_node target\_node edge\_tag {[}optional\_weight{]}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_name}} \textendash{} Path to SPIN edgelist file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to create directed graph (currently creates undirected)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
(parsed\_graph, None for labels)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple{[}nx.Graph, None{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently always returns nx.Graph (undirected) regardless of directed parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge tag is stored in edge ‘type’ attribute

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default weight is 1 if not specified (4th column)

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} B C gene\PYGZus{}regulation 0.80}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{parse\PYGZus{}spin\PYGZus{}edgelist}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{spin\PYGZus{}edges.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\item {}

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate a simple multiplex multilayer stochastic block model (SBM) network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function creates a multilayer network with:
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxtitleref{n\_nodes} nodes shared across all layers,
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxtitleref{n\_layers} layers,
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxtitleref{n\_blocks} latent communities (blocks),
\sphinxhyphen{} within\sphinxhyphen{}block edge probability \sphinxtitleref{p\_in},
\sphinxhyphen{} between\sphinxhyphen{}block edge probability \sphinxtitleref{p\_out},
\sphinxhyphen{} optional diagonal inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling with probability \sphinxtitleref{coupling}
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
between replicas of the same node across layers.
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The block memberships are shared across layers in this simple model,
and the same block probability matrix is used for all layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_layers}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_nodes}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of nodes (shared across all layers).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_blocks}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of blocks (communities).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p\_in}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Edge probability for edges within the same block.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p\_out}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Edge probability for edges between different blocks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{coupling}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Probability of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges between replicas of the same node
in different layers. Defaults to 0.0 (no inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Whether to generate directed layers. Defaults to False.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{network} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{multi\_layer\_network}) \textendash{} The generated multilayer network.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{metadata} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{SBMMetadata}) \textendash{} Ground\sphinxhyphen{}truth metadata containing block memberships and block matrix.

\end{itemize}


\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node IDs are strings “v0”, “v1”, …, “v\{n\_nodes\sphinxhyphen{}1\}”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer names are strings “L0”, “L1”, …, “L\{n\_layers\sphinxhyphen{}1\}”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edges are inserted via the py3plex list\sphinxhyphen{}based API:
{[}src\_node, src\_layer, dst\_node, dst\_layer, weight{]}.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}SBM}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}blocks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{p\PYGZus{}in}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{p\PYGZus{}out}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{coupling}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}

{{ $\rightarrow$ str}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get the absolute path to a data file in the repository.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function searches for data files in multiple locations to support both:
\sphinxhyphen{} Running examples from a cloned repository
\sphinxhyphen{} Running scripts/notebooks from any directory with datasets locally available

\sphinxAtStartPar
Search order:
1. Relative to the calling script’s directory (for examples in cloned repo)
2. Relative to current working directory (for notebooks/user scripts)
3. Relative to py3plex package location (for editable installs)
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{relative\_path}} \textendash{} Path relative to repository root (e.g., “datasets/intact02.gpickle”)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Absolute path to the file

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
str

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexIOError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexIOError}}}}} \textendash{} If the file cannot be found in any search location

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{utils}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}data\PYGZus{}path}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{path} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}data\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/intact02.gpickle}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exists}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{True}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When py3plex is installed via pip, datasets are not included in the package.
Users should either:
\sphinxhyphen{} Clone the repository and run examples from there
\sphinxhyphen{} Download datasets separately and place them relative to their scripts
\sphinxhyphen{} Use current working directory with datasets folder
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.utils.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_rng}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{seed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }Generator\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Generator}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get a NumPy random number generator with optional seed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This provides a unified interface for random state management across
the library, ensuring reproducibility when a seed is provided.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility. Can be:
\sphinxhyphen{} None: Use default unseeded generator
\sphinxhyphen{} int: Seed value for the generator
\sphinxhyphen{} np.random.Generator: Pass through existing generator

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialized random number generator

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.random.Generator

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Reproducible random number}
\PYG{g+go}{0.7739560485559633}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng1}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{rng2}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{True}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{existing\PYGZus{}rng} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{123}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{existing\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng} \PYG{o+ow}{is} \PYG{n}{existing\PYGZus{}rng}
\PYG{g+go}{True}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Contracts:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: result is a NumPy random Generator

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses numpy.random.Generator (modern API introduced in NumPy 1.17)
rather than the legacy numpy.random.RandomState API.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Negative seeds are converted to positive values by taking absolute value
to ensure compatibility with NumPy’s SeedSequence.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.exceptions@\spxentry{py3plex.exceptions}}\index{py3plex.exceptions@\spxentry{py3plex.exceptions}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.exceptions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Custom exception types for the py3plex library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module defines domain\sphinxhyphen{}specific exceptions to provide clear error messages
and enable better error handling throughout the library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Py3plex follows Rust’s approach to error messages:
\sphinxhyphen{} Clear, descriptive error messages
\sphinxhyphen{} Error codes (e.g., PX101, PX201)
\sphinxhyphen{} Helpful suggestions for fixing issues
\sphinxhyphen{} “Did you mean?” suggestions for typos
\sphinxhyphen{} Context showing the relevant location in files
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Example usage:}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{exceptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{InvalidLayerError}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k}{raise} \PYG{n}{InvalidLayerError}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{available\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{family}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social\PYGZus{}media}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{suggestion}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Did you mean }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social\PYGZus{}media}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{?}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}

\subsubsection{Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL)}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:domain-specific-language-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL v2 for Multilayer Network Queries.

\sphinxAtStartPar

analyzing multilayer networks. DSL v2 introduces:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unified AST representation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pythonic builder API (Q, L, Param)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific abstractions (layer algebra, intralayer/interlayer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Improved ergonomics (ORDER BY, LIMIT, EXPLAIN, rich results)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional progress logging for debugging and monitoring

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL Extensions (v2.1):
6. Network comparison (C.compare())
7. Null models (N.model())
8. Path queries (P.shortest(), P.random\_walk())
9. Plugin system for user\sphinxhyphen{}defined operators (@dsl\_operator)

\PYG{g+gp}{... }     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alias}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{bc}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxlineitem{The DSL also supports a string syntax:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
SELECT nodes
FROM LAYER(“social”) + LAYER(“work”)
WHERE intralayer AND degree \textgreater{} 5
COMPUTE betweenness\_centrality AS bc
ORDER BY bc DESC
LIMIT 20
TO pandas

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All frontends (string DSL, builder API) compile into a single AST which is
executed by the same engine, ensuring consistent behavior.
