Automatically detect communities using the AutoCommunity meta\sphinxhyphen{}algorithm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns an assignment table with columns:
\sphinxhyphen{} node: Node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} layer: Layer name (nullable for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks)
\sphinxhyphen{} community: Community assignment
\sphinxhyphen{} confidence: Assignment confidence (0\sphinxhyphen{}1)
\sphinxhyphen{} entropy: Assignment entropy (uncertainty measure)
\sphinxhyphen{} margin: Margin between top two community assignments
\sphinxhyphen{} community\_size: Size of the assigned community
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically select best community detection algorithm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Runs multiple community detection algorithms with parameter grids,
evaluates them on multiple quality metrics (bucketed), and selects
the winner using a “most wins” decision engine.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{fast}} \textendash{} Use fast mode with smaller parameter grids (default: True)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_candidates}} \textendash{} Maximum number of algorithm candidates (default: 10)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Master random seed for reproducibility (default: 0)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for chaining (execute() will run auto\sphinxhyphen{}selection)

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Main builder for pattern queries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Provides a fluent API for constructing pattern queries. The builder
accumulates pattern elements (nodes, edges, constraints) and produces
a PatternGraph IR object that can be compiled and executed.
\subsubsection*{Example}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Global defaults for uncertainty estimation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This class provides a way to configure default parameters for
uncertainty estimation that will be used when uncertainty=True
is passed to compute() but specific parameters are omitted.
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set global defaults}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{uncertainty}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{defaults}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{enabled}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}boot}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{ci}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.95}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{bootstrap\PYGZus{}unit}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{bootstrap\PYGZus{}mode}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{resample}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Now compute() will use these defaults}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method computes aggregations over the result set. It supports:
\sphinxhyphen{} Built\sphinxhyphen{}in aggregation functions: mean(), sum(), min(), max(), std(), var(), median(), quantile(attr, p), count()
\sphinxhyphen{} Direct attribute references for last/first value
\sphinxhyphen{} Lambda functions for custom aggregations

The aggregations are computed after grouping if active, otherwise globally.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**aggregations}} \textendash{}

\sphinxhyphen{} Key is the output column name
\sphinxhyphen{} Value is either:
\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Run community detection and attach partition to network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This operator runs community detection on the network and attaches the
resulting partition so it can be queried or used in subsequent operations.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported algorithms:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
“leiden”: Multilayer Leiden algorithm (production\sphinxhyphen{}ready with UQ)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
“louvain”: Multilayer Louvain algorithm

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
“infomap”: Infomap (if available)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
“label\_propagation\_supra”: Supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph label propagation (hard labels)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
“label\_propagation\_consensus”: Multiplex consensus label propagation (hard labels)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Leiden specifically, use in combination with .uq() for uncertainty
quantification. Label propagation algorithms support deterministic execution
with random\_state for reproducibility.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} \textendash{} Community detection algorithm (default: “leiden”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s). Higher \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} more communities. (default: 1.0)
Not used for label\_propagation algorithms.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Interlayer coupling strength. Higher \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} stronger coupling. (default: 1.0)
For label\_propagation\_supra: weight of identity links between layers.
Not used for label\_propagation\_consensus.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_iterations}} \textendash{} Number of iterations for iterative methods (default: 2)
For label\_propagation\_supra: maps to max\_iter (default: 100)
For label\_propagation\_consensus: maps to max\_iter (default: 25)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility. If None, uses 0. (default: None)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition\_name}} \textendash{} Name to assign to this partition (default: “default”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional algorithm\sphinxhyphen{}specific parameters:
\sphinxhyphen{} projection: “none” or “majority” (label\_propagation\_supra only)
\sphinxhyphen{} inner\_max\_iter: int (label\_propagation\_consensus only, default: 50)
\sphinxhyphen{} max\_iter: int (override default iterations for label propagation)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for chaining

\end{description}\end{quote}

\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Results are attached to the network under partition\_name

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combining with .uq() enables probabilistic community detection

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default random\_state=None becomes 0 for determinism

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks, consider tuning omega and gamma for performance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Label propagation algorithms use hard labels with random tie\sphinxhyphen{}breaking

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically detect communities and join annotations to nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extends the node query with community assignment annotations:
\sphinxhyphen{} community: Community assignment
\sphinxhyphen{} confidence: Assignment confidence (0\sphinxhyphen{}1)
\sphinxhyphen{} entropy: Assignment entropy (uncertainty measure)
\sphinxhyphen{} margin: Margin between top two community assignments
\sphinxhyphen{} community\_size: Size of the assigned community
\sphinxhyphen{} layer: Layer name (nullable for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks)

\sphinxAtStartPar
These annotations can be filtered with .where() like any other attribute.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility (default: None)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{fast}} \textendash{} Use fast mode with smaller parameter grids (default: True)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional parameters passed to auto\_select\_community

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for chaining (execute() will run auto detection and join)

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Attach a robustness contract to the query (certification\sphinxhyphen{}grade).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Contracts ensure that query conclusions are stable under structural
perturbations. This is distinct from uncertainty quantification:
\sphinxhyphen{} UQ quantifies uncertainty of estimates (error bars)
\sphinxhyphen{} Contracts certify robustness of conclusions (stable/unstable)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Contracts provide:
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxstylestrong{Typed failure modes}: Clear classification of why a contract might fail
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxstylestrong{Auto\sphinxhyphen{}inference}: Sensible defaults for perturbation, predicates, samples
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxstylestrong{Repair mechanisms}: Stable cores, tiers, stable nodes
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxstylestrong{Determinism}: Default seed=0 ensures reproducibility
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxstylestrong{Provenance}: Full replay capability
\begin{quote}\begin{description}

\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{contract}} \textendash{} Robustness contract object from py3plex.contracts

\sphinxAtStartPar
Configure coverage filtering across groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Coverage determines which items appear in the final result based on
how many groups they appear in after grouping and top\_k filtering.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mode}} \textendash{} Coverage mode:
\sphinxhyphen{} “all”: Keep items that appear in ALL groups
\sphinxhyphen{} “any”: Keep items that appear in AT LEAST ONE group
\sphinxhyphen{} “at\_least”: Keep items that appear in at least k groups (requires k/threshold parameter)
\sphinxhyphen{} “exact”: Keep items that appear in exactly k groups (requires k/threshold parameter)
\sphinxhyphen{} “fraction”: Keep items that appear in at least p fraction (0\sphinxhyphen{}1) of groups (requires p parameter)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{k}} \textendash{} Threshold for “at\_least” or “exact” modes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{threshold}} \textendash{} Alias for k parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Fraction threshold (0.0\sphinxhyphen{}1.0) for “fraction” mode. E.g., p=0.67 means at least 67\% of groups

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{group}} \textendash{} Group attribute for coverage (defaults to primary grouping context)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{id\_field}} \textendash{} Field to use for identity matching (default: “id” for nodes)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for chaining

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If mode is invalid or required parameters are missing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If called without prior grouping

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Two modes:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Execution Plan Mode} (no arguments):
Returns an ExplainQuery that shows the execution plan when executed.
This is like SQL EXPLAIN \sphinxhyphen{} it shows what the query will do.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Explanations Mode} (with arguments):
Attaches explanations to each result row (typically nodes), such as:
\sphinxhyphen{} Community membership and size
\sphinxhyphen{} Top neighbors by weight/degree
\sphinxhyphen{} Layer footprint (which layers the node appears in)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set query\sphinxhyphen{}scoped sensitivity analysis configuration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sensitivity analysis tests the robustness of query CONCLUSIONS (rankings,
sets, communities) under controlled perturbations. This is DISTINCT from
uncertainty quantification (.uq()):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
UQ (.uq()): Estimates uncertainty of metric VALUES (mean, std, CI)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sensitivity (.sensitivity()): Assesses stability of CONCLUSIONS

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The sensitivity analysis runs the query on multiple perturbed versions
of the network and measures how much the conclusions change using
stability metrics like Jaccard@k and Kendall\sphinxhyphen{}τ.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturb}} \textendash{} Perturbation method:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘edge\_drop’: Randomly drop edges
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘degree\_preserving\_rewire’: Rewire while preserving degrees

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{grid}} \textendash{} Perturbation strength grid (default: {[}0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2{]})
Interpretation depends on perturbation method (e.g., fraction of edges)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_samples}} \textendash{} Number of samples per grid point for averaging (default: 30)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility (default: None)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{metrics}} \textendash{} Stability metrics to compute (default: {[}‘kendall\_tau’{]})
Options: ‘jaccard\_at\_k(k)’, ‘kendall\_tau’, ‘variation\_of\_information’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{scope}} \textendash{} Analysis scope (default: ‘global’)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘global’: Overall stability curves
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘per\_node’: Node\sphinxhyphen{}level influence scores
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘per\_layer’: Layer\sphinxhyphen{}level influence scores

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional perturbation\sphinxhyphen{}specific parameters:
\sphinxhyphen{} layer\_aware: Whether to preserve layer structure (default: True)
\sphinxhyphen{} max\_attempts: Max rewiring attempts (for rewiring methods)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for chaining

\end{description}\end{quote}

\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sensitivity results include stability curves (metric vs perturbation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike UQ, sensitivity does NOT report mean/std/CI for values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sensitivity analyzes how CONCLUSIONS change, not value uncertainty

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Results can identify tipping points where conclusions collapse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Per\sphinxhyphen{}node/per\sphinxhyphen{}layer scope provides local influence attribution

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes summary statistics per group when grouping is active,
or globally if no grouping is set. Aggregation expressions are
strings like “mean(degree)”, “max(degree)”, “n()”.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported aggregations:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
n() / count() : count of items

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mean(attr) : mean value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
median(attr) : median value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sum(attr) : sum of values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
min(attr) : minimum value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max(attr) : maximum value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
std(attr) : standard deviation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
var(attr) : variance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
quantile(attr, p) : p\sphinxhyphen{}th quantile (e.g., quantile(degree, 0.95))

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add sliding window specification for temporal analysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Enables queries that operate over sliding time windows, useful for
streaming algorithms and temporal pattern analysis.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{window\_size}} \textendash{} Size of each window. Can be:
\sphinxhyphen{} Numeric: treated as timestamp units
\sphinxhyphen{} String: duration like “7d”, “1h”, “30m”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{step}} \textendash{} Step size between windows (defaults to window\_size for non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping).
Same format as window\_size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start}} \textendash{} Optional start time for windowing (defaults to network’s first timestamp)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{end}} \textendash{} Optional end time for windowing (defaults to network’s last timestamp)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{aggregation}} \textendash{} How to aggregate results across windows:
\sphinxhyphen{} “list”: Return list of per\sphinxhyphen{}window results
\sphinxhyphen{} “concat”: Concatenate DataFrames
\sphinxhyphen{} “avg”: Average numeric columns

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for chaining

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar

key columns are included in the DataFrame

\sphinxAtStartPar
Decorator to register a Python function as a DSL operator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This decorator allows users to define custom operators that can be used
in DSL queries. The decorated function should accept a DSLExecutionContext
as its first argument, followed by any keyword arguments.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{name}} \textendash{} Operator name (defaults to function name if not provided)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{description}} \textendash{} Human\sphinxhyphen{}readable description (defaults to function docstring)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{category}} \textendash{} Optional category for organization (e.g., “centrality”, “dynamics”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{overwrite}} \textendash{} If True, allow replacing existing operators

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decorator function that registers the operator

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZsq{}\PYGZsq{}Compute resilience score for current layers.\PYGZsq{}\PYGZsq{}\PYGZsq{}}

\subsubsection{Uncertainty Quantification}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:uncertainty-quantification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uncertainty estimation tools and supporting types for ranking and inference tasks.
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.uncertainty@\spxentry{py3plex.uncertainty}}\index{py3plex.uncertainty@\spxentry{py3plex.uncertainty}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.uncertainty}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
First\sphinxhyphen{}class uncertainty support for py3plex.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides types and utilities for representing statistics with
uncertainty information. The core idea is that every statistic is an object
that can carry a distribution:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Deterministic mode: object has mean with std=None (certainty 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uncertainty mode: object has mean, std, quantiles populated

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This makes uncertainty “first\sphinxhyphen{}class” \sphinxhyphen{} it’s baked into how numbers exist in
the library, not bolted on later.
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{uncertainty}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{StatSeries}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{StatSeries}\PYG{p}{(}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute co\sphinxhyphen{}assignment probability matrix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
P(i, j) = probability that nodes i and j are in the same community.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This can be computed in sparse mode (top\sphinxhyphen{}k neighbors only) to save memory.

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{topk}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=50}}) \textendash{} Number of top co\sphinxhyphen{}assignments to keep per node (if sparse=True)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{threshold}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=0.0}}) \textendash{} Minimum co\sphinxhyphen{}assignment probability to store (if sparse=True)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Distribution over community partitions with lazy evaluation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Represents a collection of community detection runs, providing methods
to compute summary statistics like co\sphinxhyphen{}association matrices, consensus
partitions, and node\sphinxhyphen{}level confidence metrics.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All expensive computations (co\sphinxhyphen{}association, consensus, alignment) are
performed lazily and cached for efficiency.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partitions}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{list}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ of }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} List of partition arrays. Each array has shape (n\_nodes,) with
integer community labels. All arrays must have the same length
and correspond to the same node ordering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{nodes}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{list}}) \textendash{} Ordered list of node identifiers corresponding to partition indices.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weights}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Per\sphinxhyphen{}partition weights (e.g., modularity scores), shape (n\_partitions,).
If None, all partitions are weighted equally.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{meta}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Metadata about the distribution generation:
\sphinxhyphen{} method: Algorithm name (e.g., “multilayer\_louvain”)
\sphinxhyphen{} n\_runs: Number of partitions
\sphinxhyphen{} resampling: Resampling strategy (“seed”, “bootstrap”, “perturbation”)
\sphinxhyphen{} gamma: Resolution parameter(s) used
\sphinxhyphen{} seed: Base random seed
\sphinxhyphen{} n\_jobs: Number of parallel jobs
\sphinxhyphen{} layers: List of layer names (for multilayer networks)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Align partition labels to a reference using Hungarian matching.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After alignment, membership probabilities P(node\_i in community\_k)
can be computed meaningfully. Alignment solves the label correspondence
problem (community 0 in partition A may correspond to community 3 in B).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method modifies internal state and caches aligned partitions.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{reference}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{\{\textquotesingle{}medoid\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}first\textquotesingle{}\}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ or }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} Reference partition for alignment:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘medoid’: Use medoid partition as reference
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘first’: Use first partition as reference
\sphinxhyphen{} np.ndarray: Use provided partition as reference

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{metric}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{\{\textquotesingle{}overlap\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}nmi\textquotesingle{}\}}}) \textendash{} Metric for computing cost matrix for Hungarian algorithm:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘overlap’: Maximize overlap (intersection) between communities
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘nmi’: Maximize normalized mutual information

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns self for method chaining.

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
self

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{dist} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{CommunityDistribution}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute co\sphinxhyphen{}association matrix: P(node\_i and node\_j in same community).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The co\sphinxhyphen{}association matrix measures how often each pair of nodes appears
in the same community across all partitions. This is label\sphinxhyphen{}permutation
invariant (does not require alignment).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mode}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{\{\textquotesingle{}auto\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}dense\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}sparse\textquotesingle{}\}}}) \textendash{} Output mode:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘dense’: Return full n×n numpy array
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘sparse’: Return dict mapping node\_idx to list of (neighbor\_idx, prob)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘auto’: Choose based on n\_nodes (sparse if \textgreater{} 2000)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{topk}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=50}}) \textendash{} For sparse mode, keep only top\sphinxhyphen{}k highest co\sphinxhyphen{}association neighbors
per node. Set to \sphinxhyphen{}1 to keep all non\sphinxhyphen{}zero entries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sample\_pairs}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} For very large graphs, approximate co\sphinxhyphen{}association by sampling this
many node pairs uniformly. If None, compute exactly.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If mode=’dense’: Array of shape (n\_nodes, n\_nodes) with co\sphinxhyphen{}assoc probs.
If mode=’sparse’: Dict mapping node\_idx to list of (neighbor\_idx, prob).

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray or dict

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{dist} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{CommunityDistribution}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{coassoc\PYGZus{}dense} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{coassociation}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{dense}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{coassoc\PYGZus{}dense}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} P(node 0 and 1 in same community)}
\PYG{g+go}{0.75}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{coassoc\PYGZus{}sparse} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{dist}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{coassociation}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{sparse}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{topk}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{coassoc\PYGZus{}sparse}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Top 10 most co\PYGZhy{}associated nodes with node 0}
\PYG{g+go}{[(2, 0.9), (5, 0.85), ...]}

Compute per\sphinxhyphen{}node margin (confidence gap).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Margin is the difference between the two most frequent community
assignments. Requires label alignment if using membership probs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If alignment not available, uses consensus confidence as proxy.

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\end{description}\end{quote}

Compute consensus partition using node marginals (UQ spine version).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This reducer depends on NodeMarginalReducer to provide marginal
distributions. It extracts the consensus labels from the marginals.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a thin wrapper that extracts consensus from NodeMarginalReducer
output, following the design principle that ConsensusReducer uses
marginals from NodeMarginalReducer.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute per\sphinxhyphen{}node marginal membership distributions (UQ spine version).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This reducer is the canonical implementation for the UQ execution spine.
It tracks the frequency of each community label for each node across
samples and computes:
\sphinxhyphen{} Node entropy: H(node) = \sphinxhyphen{}sum\_k p\_k * log(p\_k)
\sphinxhyphen{} Maximum membership probability: max\_c p(node, c)
\sphinxhyphen{} Consensus labels: argmax\_c p(node, c)

\sphinxAtStartPar
This replaces NodeEntropyReducer as the primary reducer for partition UQ.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_nodes}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_ids}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{list}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Node identifiers (for mapping back to nodes)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

Internal representation of a partition (community assignment).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the unified output format returned by base\_callable that gets
fed into reducers for uncertainty quantification.

\sphinxAtStartPar
PartitionOutput is a thin adapter that wraps community detection results
into a standard format. Community algorithms return node \(\rightarrow\) community
assignments, and this class normalizes that representation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create PartitionUQ from UQResult (UQ spine integration).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This factory method creates a PartitionUQ from a UQResult produced
by run\_uq() with the appropriate reducers. It expects:
\sphinxhyphen{} NodeMarginalReducer output (required)
\sphinxhyphen{} StabilityReducer output (optional)


\paragraph{Note: Co\sphinxhyphen{}assignment matrix computation}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:note-co-assignment-matrix-computation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the co\sphinxhyphen{}assignment matrix is NOT computed when using the
UQ spine approach. This is intentional for memory efficiency. If you
need the co\sphinxhyphen{}assignment matrix, you must:
1. Add CoAssignmentReducer to your UQPlan.reducers list
2. Extract the result from uq\_result.reducer\_outputs{[}‘CoAssignmentReducer’{]}
3. Manually set it on the PartitionUQ object after construction

\sphinxAtStartPar
Probabilistic community detection result with backward compatibility.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This class wraps CommunityDistribution to provide:
1. Backward\sphinxhyphen{}compatible hard labels (deterministic view)
2. Probabilistic membership distributions (uncertainty view)
3. Node\sphinxhyphen{}level uncertainty metrics (entropy, confidence)
4. Community\sphinxhyphen{}level stability metrics
5. Partition\sphinxhyphen{}space variability metrics
\begin{quote}\begin{description}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{distribution}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.CommunityDistribution}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{CommunityDistribution}}}}}) \textendash{} The underlying distribution of community partitions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{consensus\_method}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=\textquotesingle{}medoid\textquotesingle{}}}) \textendash{} Method for computing consensus partition (‘medoid’ or ‘cluster\_coassoc’).

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{Reducer (class in py3plex.uncertainty)@\spxentry{Reducer}\spxextra{class in py3plex.uncertainty}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.Reducer}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{class\DUrole{w}{ }}}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.uncertainty.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{Reducer}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ABC}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Base protocol for online reducers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reducers follow the online aggregation pattern:
1. Initialize state in \_\_init\_\_
2. update(sample\_output) \sphinxhyphen{} accumulate from one sample
3. finalize() \sphinxhyphen{} compute final result
4. reset() \sphinxhyphen{} clear state for reuse

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reducers must be:
\sphinxhyphen{} Online: Process samples one at a time
\sphinxhyphen{} Composable: Multiple reducers can run in parallel
\sphinxhyphen{} Memory\sphinxhyphen{}efficient: Don’t store all samples (unless explicitly needed)
\sphinxhyphen{} Independent: No dependencies on DSL or QueryResult
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reducers MUST NOT control execution flow

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reducers MUST NOT depend on sample order (unless explicitly designed to)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reducers SHOULD be deterministic given the same sample sequence

\end{itemize}

\sphinxhyphen{} certainty = 1.0

\sphinxhyphen{} mean contains the average across runs
\sphinxhyphen{} std contains the standard deviation

\sphinxAtStartPar
Canonical specification for UQ execution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
UQPlan encapsulates all information needed to execute uncertainty
quantification for any algorithm. It is:
\sphinxhyphen{} Strategy\sphinxhyphen{}agnostic (seed, perturbation, bootstrap, jackknife)
\sphinxhyphen{} Reducer\sphinxhyphen{}driven (reducers compute statistics online)
\sphinxhyphen{} Reproducible (seed controls all randomness)
\sphinxhyphen{} Memory\sphinxhyphen{}efficient (storage\_mode controls what to keep)

Add multiplicative noise to edge weights.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This noise model multiplies each edge weight by a random factor
drawn from a specified distribution. Useful for testing sensitivity
to weight uncertainty.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{dist}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}) \textendash{} Distribution type: “lognormal”, “uniform”, or “normal”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sigma}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Scale parameter for the distribution
\sphinxhyphen{} lognormal: standard deviation of log\sphinxhyphen{}weights
\sphinxhyphen{} uniform: half\sphinxhyphen{}width of interval
\sphinxhyphen{} normal: standard deviation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{clip\_min}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Minimum weight value (default: 0.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{clip\_max}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Maximum weight value (default: None)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bootstrap a metric for uncertainty estimation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function resamples the graph by unit (edges, nodes, or layers) and
recomputes the metric on each bootstrap sample to estimate uncertainty.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} The multilayer network to analyze.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{metric\_fn}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{callable}}) \textendash{} Function that takes a network and returns a dict mapping items (usually
nodes) to metric values. Must have signature:
metric\_fn(network) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} Dict{[}item\_id, float{]}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_boot}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=200}}) \textendash{} Number of bootstrap replicates.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{unit}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default="edges"}}) \textendash{} What to resample: “edges”, “nodes”, or “layers”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mode}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default="resample"}}) \textendash{} Resampling mode:
\sphinxhyphen{} “resample”: Sample with replacement (classic bootstrap)
\sphinxhyphen{} “permute”: Permute the units (permutation test)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ci}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=0.95}}) \textendash{} Confidence interval level (e.g., 0.95 for 95\% CI).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_jobs}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Number of parallel jobs. If None, uses config.DEFAULT\_N\_JOBS.
If 1, runs serially. If \textgreater{}1, runs in parallel.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary with keys:
\sphinxhyphen{} “mean”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with mean values
\sphinxhyphen{} “std”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with standard errors
\sphinxhyphen{} “ci\_low”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with lower CI bounds
\sphinxhyphen{} “ci\_high”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with upper CI bounds
\sphinxhyphen{} “index”: List of item IDs
\sphinxhyphen{} “n\_boot”: Number of bootstrap replicates used
\sphinxhyphen{} “method”: String describing the bootstrap method

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bootstrap resample network edges with replacement.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates a new network by sampling edges with replacement from the
original network. The new network has approximately the same number
of edges, but some may be duplicated and some omitted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Never modifies the input network} \sphinxhyphen{} returns a new copy.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} Input network to resample (will not be modified).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{preserve\_layers}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=True}}) \textendash{} If True, preserve layer labels and structure.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
New network with bootstrapped edges.

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{multi\_layer\_network}}}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For undirected networks, each undirected edge is treated as a single
unit for resampling (not resampled twice as two directed edges).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Clopper\sphinxhyphen{}Pearson exact confidence interval for a binomial proportion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a more conservative (wider) interval than Wilson score, guaranteed
to have at least the nominal coverage. Useful when exactness is critical.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{successes}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of successes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_trials}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Total number of trials

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=0.05}}) \textendash{} Significance level (e.g., 0.05 for 95\% CI)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower and upper bounds of the confidence interval

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
tuple of (float, float)

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Based on the beta distribution relationship to the binomial.
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{clopper\PYGZus{}pearson\PYGZus{}interval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{(0.39..., 0.60...)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{metric\_fn}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Callable\DUrole{p}{{[}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{multi\_layer\_network}}}\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }ndarray\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{o}{*}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{n\_runs}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{resampling}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.types.ResamplingStrategy}]{\sphinxcrossref{ResamplingStrategy}}}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{random\_seed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{perturbation\_params}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}str\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }Any\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Estimate uncertainty for a network statistic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the main entry point for adding uncertainty to any statistic.
It runs the metric function multiple times with different random seeds
or network perturbations, then computes mean, std, and quantiles.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} The network to analyze.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{metric\_fn}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{callable}}) \textendash{} Function that computes a statistic. Must accept a network and return:
\sphinxhyphen{} dict{[}node, float{]} for per\sphinxhyphen{}node statistics
\sphinxhyphen{} float for scalar statistics
\sphinxhyphen{} np.ndarray for array statistics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_runs}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Number of runs for uncertainty estimation. If None, uses the
default from the current uncertainty config.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resampling}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.ResamplingStrategy}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ResamplingStrategy}}}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Strategy for resampling. If None, uses default from config.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturbation\_params}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Parameters for perturbation strategies. For example:
\{“edge\_drop\_p”: 0.05, “node\_drop\_p”: 0.02\}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If metric\_fn returns a dict: StatSeries with uncertainty info
If metric\_fn returns a scalar: float (mean value)
The returned object has mean, std, and quantiles populated.

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.StatSeries}]{\sphinxcrossref{StatSeries}}} or float

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{uncertainty}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{estimate\PYGZus{}uncertainty}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ResamplingStrategy}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a simple network}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{L0}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{L0}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define a metric function}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{my\PYGZus{}metric}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Return per\PYGZhy{}node degree}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }        \PYG{n}{degrees}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{degree}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{perturbation\PYGZus{}params}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edge\PYGZus{}drop\PYGZus{}p}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Mean degree values}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{std}   \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Std deviation of degrees}

\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For SEED strategy: runs the metric with different random seeds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

Generate an ensemble of community partitions with UQ.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the main entry point for probabilistic community detection.
It generates multiple partitions using the specified resampling strategy
and returns a CommunityDistribution for analysis.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} The network to analyze.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{algorithm}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=\textquotesingle{}louvain\textquotesingle{}}}) \textendash{} Community detection algorithm. Supported:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘louvain’: Louvain modularity optimization
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘label\_propagation’: Label propagation
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘infomap’: Infomap (requires infomap package)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=\textquotesingle{}seed\textquotesingle{}}}) \textendash{} Resampling method for uncertainty estimation:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘seed’: Run algorithm with different random seeds (Monte Carlo)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘perturbation’: Perturb edges before each run
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘bootstrap’: Bootstrap resample nodes or edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_samples}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=50}}) \textendash{} Number of partitions to generate in the ensemble.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Base random seed for reproducibility. If provided, generates
deterministic sequence of seeds for parallel runs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturbation\_rate}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=0.1}}) \textendash{} For method=’perturbation’: fraction of edges to perturb (0.0 to 1.0).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.uncertainty.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{nmi}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{partition1}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{ndarray}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{partition2}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{ndarray}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{method}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}arithmetic\textquotesingle{}}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Normalized Mutual Information between two partitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
NMI normalizes mutual information by the arithmetic or geometric
mean of the entropies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
NMI is:
\sphinxhyphen{} Symmetric
\sphinxhyphen{} In range {[}0, 1{]}
\sphinxhyphen{} 1 iff partitions are identical (up to label permutation)
\sphinxhyphen{} 0 if independent
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition1}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} First partition, shape (n,) with integer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition2}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} Second partition, shape (n,) with integer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default="arithmetic"}}) \textendash{} Normalization method:
\sphinxhyphen{} “arithmetic”: 2*I(X,Y) / (H(X) + H(Y))
\sphinxhyphen{} “geometric”: I(X,Y) / sqrt(H(X) * H(Y))
\sphinxhyphen{} “max”: I(X,Y) / max(H(X), H(Y))
\sphinxhyphen{} “min”: I(X,Y) / min(H(X), H(Y))

\end{itemize}

{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Normalized Mutual Information between two partitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
NMI normalizes mutual information by the arithmetic or geometric
mean of the entropies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
NMI is:
\sphinxhyphen{} Symmetric
\sphinxhyphen{} In range {[}0, 1{]}
\sphinxhyphen{} 1 iff partitions are identical (up to label permutation)
\sphinxhyphen{} 0 if independent
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition1}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} First partition, shape (n,) with integer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition2}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} Second partition, shape (n,) with integer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default="arithmetic"}}) \textendash{} Normalization method:
\sphinxhyphen{} “arithmetic”: 2*I(X,Y) / (H(X) + H(Y))
\sphinxhyphen{} “geometric”: I(X,Y) / sqrt(H(X) * H(Y))
\sphinxhyphen{} “max”: I(X,Y) / max(H(X), H(Y))
\sphinxhyphen{} “min”: I(X,Y) / min(H(X), H(Y))

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normalized mutual information in {[}0, 1{]}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
float

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute metric on null models for statistical significance testing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function generates null models of the network (e.g., via degree\sphinxhyphen{}preserving
rewiring) and computes the metric on each null network. It then computes
z\sphinxhyphen{}scores and p\sphinxhyphen{}values for the observed metric values.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} The multilayer network to analyze.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{metric\_fn}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{callable}}) \textendash{} Function that takes a network and returns a dict mapping items (usually
nodes) to metric values. Must have signature:
metric\_fn(network) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} Dict{[}item\_id, float{]}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_null}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=200}}) \textendash{} Number of null model replicates to generate.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{model}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default="degree\_preserving"}}) \textendash{} Null model type:
\sphinxhyphen{} “degree\_preserving”: Rewire edges while preserving degree sequence
\sphinxhyphen{} “erdos\_renyi”: Random graph with same density
\sphinxhyphen{} “configuration”: Configuration model matching degree distribution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_jobs}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Number of parallel jobs. If None, uses config.DEFAULT\_N\_JOBS.
If 1, runs serially. If \textgreater{}1, runs in parallel.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary with keys:
\sphinxhyphen{} “observed”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with observed metric values
\sphinxhyphen{} “mean\_null”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with mean null values
\sphinxhyphen{} “std\_null”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with std of null values
\sphinxhyphen{} “zscore”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with z\sphinxhyphen{}scores
\sphinxhyphen{} “pvalue”: np.ndarray of shape (n\_items,) with two\sphinxhyphen{}tailed p\sphinxhyphen{}values
\sphinxhyphen{} “index”: List of item IDs
\sphinxhyphen{} “n\_null”: Number of null replicates used
\sphinxhyphen{} “model”: String describing the null model

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Z\sphinxhyphen{}scores indicate how many standard deviations the observed value is from
the null distribution mean

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
P\sphinxhyphen{}values are two\sphinxhyphen{}tailed by default: P({\color{red}\bfseries{}|Z|} \textgreater{}= {\color{red}\bfseries{}|Z\_observed|}) under the null.
For one\sphinxhyphen{}tailed tests, users can compute p\_one\_sided = p\_two\_sided / 2 and
check the sign of z\sphinxhyphen{}score to determine the direction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
High {\color{red}\bfseries{}|z\sphinxhyphen{}score|} and low p\sphinxhyphen{}value indicate statistical significance

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Execute uncertainty quantification according to plan.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the canonical UQ execution function. It implements the
following strict execution semantics:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize RNG sequence from plan.seed

\item {} \begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{For i in range(n\_samples):}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\alph}{enumii}{enumiii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Derive per\sphinxhyphen{}sample RNG

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply NoiseModel (or NoNoise)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Call base\_callable(net\_i, rng\_i)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pass output to ALL reducers

\end{enumerate}

\end{description}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
After loop, call finalize() on reducers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assemble UQResult

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Attach centralized provenance

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
ABSOLUTE RULES:
\sphinxhyphen{} No reducer may control execution
\sphinxhyphen{} No algorithm may loop internally for UQ
\sphinxhyphen{} No sample outputs stored unless storage\_mode == “samples”
\begin{quote}\begin{description}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{partition1}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{ndarray}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{partition2}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{ndarray}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Variation of Information between two partitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
VI(X, Y) = H(X) + H(Y) \sphinxhyphen{} 2*I(X, Y)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where H is entropy and I is mutual information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
VI is:
\sphinxhyphen{} Symmetric: VI(X, Y) = VI(Y, X)
\sphinxhyphen{} Non\sphinxhyphen{}negative: VI(X, Y) \textgreater{}= 0
\sphinxhyphen{} Zero iff partitions are identical (up to label permutation)
\sphinxhyphen{} Bounded by 2*log(n) where n is number of elements
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition1}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} First partition, shape (n,) with integer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition2}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} Second partition, shape (n,) with integer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=False}}) \textendash{} If True, normalize by log(n) to get value in {[}0, 2{]}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Variation of information distance

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
float

\end{description}\end{quote}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.uncertainty.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{vi}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{partition1}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{ndarray}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{partition2}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{ndarray}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Variation of Information between two partitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
VI(X, Y) = H(X) + H(Y) \sphinxhyphen{} 2*I(X, Y)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where H is entropy and I is mutual information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
VI is:
\sphinxhyphen{} Symmetric: VI(X, Y) = VI(Y, X)
\sphinxhyphen{} Non\sphinxhyphen{}negative: VI(X, Y) \textgreater{}= 0
\sphinxhyphen{} Zero iff partitions are identical (up to label permutation)
\sphinxhyphen{} Bounded by 2*log(n) where n is number of elements
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition1}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} First partition, shape (n,) with integer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition2}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{np.ndarray}}) \textendash{} Second partition, shape (n,) with integer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=False}}) \textendash{} If True, normalize by log(n) to get value in {[}0, 2{]}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Variation of information distance

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
float

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{p1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{p2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{vi} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{variation\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}information}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{p1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{p2}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{g+go}{True}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{p3} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Same structure, different labels}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.wilson_score_interval}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.uncertainty.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{wilson\_score\_interval}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{successes}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{n\_trials}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{alpha}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{0.05}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}float\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Wilson score confidence interval for a binomial proportion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Wilson score interval is robust for small sample sizes and probabilities
near 0 or 1. It is preferred over the normal approximation (Wald interval).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{successes}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of successes (e.g., number of times item appeared in selection)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_trials}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Total number of trials (e.g., number of UQ samples)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{default=0.05}}) \textendash{} Significance level (e.g., 0.05 for 95\% CI)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower and upper bounds of the confidence interval

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
tuple of (float, float)

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Based on:
Wilson, E.B. (1927). “Probable inference, the law of succession, and
statistical inference”. Journal of the American Statistical Association.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a CI level of (1\sphinxhyphen{}alpha), we use z = Φ\textasciicircum{}(\sphinxhyphen{}1)(1 \sphinxhyphen{} alpha/2).
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{wilson\PYGZus{}score\PYGZus{}interval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{(0.4..., 0.6...)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{wilson\PYGZus{}score\PYGZus{}interval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{(0.0, 0.036...)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{wilson\PYGZus{}score\PYGZus{}interval}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{(0.963..., 1.0)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxhyphen{} certainty = 1.0

\sphinxhyphen{} mean contains the average across runs
\sphinxhyphen{} std contains the standard deviation

\sphinxAtStartPar
Estimate uncertainty for a network statistic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the main entry point for adding uncertainty to any statistic.
It runs the metric function multiple times with different random seeds
or network perturbations, then computes mean, std, and quantiles.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} The network to analyze.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{metric\_fn}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{callable}}) \textendash{} Function that computes a statistic. Must accept a network and return:
\sphinxhyphen{} dict{[}node, float{]} for per\sphinxhyphen{}node statistics
\sphinxhyphen{} float for scalar statistics
\sphinxhyphen{} np.ndarray for array statistics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_runs}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Number of runs for uncertainty estimation. If None, uses the
default from the current uncertainty config.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resampling}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.ResamplingStrategy}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ResamplingStrategy}}}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Strategy for resampling. If None, uses default from config.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturbation\_params}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Parameters for perturbation strategies. For example:
\{“edge\_drop\_p”: 0.05, “node\_drop\_p”: 0.02\}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}

If metric\_fn returns a dict: StatSeries with uncertainty info
If metric\_fn returns a scalar: float (mean value)
The returned object has mean, std, and quantiles populated.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.StatSeries}]{\sphinxcrossref{StatSeries}}} or float

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Detect communities using the Infomap algorithm.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} \textendash{} Input graph (NetworkX graph or multi\_layer\_network)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{binary}} \textendash{} Path to Infomap binary (default: “./infomap”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edgelist\_file}} \textendash{} Temporary file for edgelist (default: “./tmp/tmpedgelist.txt”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multiplex}} \textendash{} Whether to use multiplex mode (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Whether to show verbose output (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{overlapping}} \textendash{} Whether to detect overlapping communities (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of iterations (default: 200)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{output}} \textendash{} Output format \sphinxhyphen{} “mapping” or “partition” (default: “mapping”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility (default: None)
Note: Requires Infomap binary that supports \textendash{}seed parameter

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dict mapping nodes to community IDs (if output=”mapping”)
or Dict mapping community IDs to lists of nodes (if output=”partition”)

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{FileNotFoundError}} \textendash{} If Infomap binary is not found

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{PermissionError}} \textendash{} If Infomap binary is not executable

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.community_detection.multilayer_modularity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer Modularity Maximization (Mucha et al., 2010)

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements multilayer modularity quality function and optimization
algorithms for community detection in multilayer/multiplex networks.
\subsubsection*{References}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Mucha et al., “Community Structure in Time\sphinxhyphen{}Dependent, Multiscale, and Multiplex
Networks”, Science 328:876\sphinxhyphen{}878 (2010)
