\sphinxAtStartPar
Build the supra\sphinxhyphen{}modularity matrix B for multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The supra\sphinxhyphen{}modularity matrix is:
B\_\{iα,jβ\} = (A\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij \sphinxhyphen{} γ\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]} k\_i\textasciicircum{}α k\_j\textasciicircum{}α / 2m\_α) δ\_αβ + δ\_ij ω\_αβ

\sphinxAtStartPar
This matrix can be used for spectral community detection methods.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple of (modularity\_matrix, node\_layer\_list)
\sphinxhyphen{} modularity\_matrix: Supra\sphinxhyphen{}modularity matrix B (NL × NL)
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_layer\_list: List of (node, layer) tuples corresponding to matrix indices

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Generalized Louvain algorithm for multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implements the multilayer Louvain method as described in Mucha et al. (2010),
which greedily maximizes the multilayer modularity quality function.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Complexity:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} \begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Time: O(n × L × d × k) per iteration, where:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
n = number of nodes per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
L = number of layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
d = average degree

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
k = number of communities

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Typical: O(n × L) iterations until convergence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Worst case: O((n×L)\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) for dense networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Space: O((n×L)\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) for supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (use sparse for large networks)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to community IDs

\end{description}\end{quote}

{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer modularity quality function (Mucha et al., 2010).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The multilayer modularity is defined as:
Q = (1/2μ) Σ\_\{ijαβ\} {[}(A\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij \sphinxhyphen{} γ\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}P\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij)δ\_αβ + δ\_ij ω\_αβ{]} δ(g\_iα, g\_jβ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\sphinxhyphen{} A\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij is the adjacency matrix of layer α
\sphinxhyphen{} P\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij is the null model (e.g., Newman\sphinxhyphen{}Girvan: k\_i\textasciicircum{}α k\_j\textasciicircum{}α / 2m\_α)
\sphinxhyphen{} γ\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]} is the resolution parameter for layer α
\sphinxhyphen{} ω\_αβ is the inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength
\sphinxhyphen{} δ\_αβ = 1 if α=β, else 0 (Kronecker delta)
\sphinxhyphen{} δ\_ij = 1 if i=j, else 0
\sphinxhyphen{} δ(g\_iα, g\_jβ) = 1 if node i in layer α and node j in layer β are in same community
\sphinxhyphen{} μ is the total edge weight in the supra\sphinxhyphen{}network
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{communities}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to community IDs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s). Can be:
\sphinxhyphen{} Single float: same resolution for all layers
\sphinxhyphen{} Dict{[}layer, float{]}: layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific resolution parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength. Can be:
\sphinxhyphen{} Single float: uniform coupling between all layer pairs
\sphinxhyphen{} np.ndarray: layer\sphinxhyphen{}pair specific coupling matrix (L×L)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute (default: “weight”)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modularity value Q ∈ {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the partition of the graph nodes which maximises the modularity
(or try..) using the Louvain heuristices

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the partition of highest modularity, i.e. the highest partition
of the dendrogram generated by the Louvain algorithm.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar

It’s a dictionary where keys are their nodes and values the communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} the key in graph to use as weight. Default to ‘weight’

\sphinxAtStartPar
Find communities in the graph and return the associated dendrogram

\sphinxAtStartPar
A dendrogram is a tree and each level is a partition of the graph nodes.
Level 0 is the first partition, which contains the smallest communities,
and the best is len(dendrogram) \sphinxhyphen{} 1. The higher the level is, the bigger
are the communities
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{networkx.Graph}}) \textendash{} the networkx graph which will be decomposed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{part\_init}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} the algorithm will start using this partition of the nodes. It’s a
dictionary where keys are their nodes and values the communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} the key in graph to use as weight. Default to ‘weight’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resolution}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{double}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Will change the size of the communities, default to 1.
represents the time described in
“Laplacian Dynamics and Multiscale Modular Structure in Networks”,
R. Lambiotte, J.\sphinxhyphen{}C. Delvenne, M. Barahona

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dendrogram} \textendash{} a list of partitions, ie dictionnaries where keys of the i+1 are the
values of the i. and where keys of the first are the nodes of graph

list of dictionaries

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{dendrogram}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{List\DUrole{p}{{[}}Dict\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{level}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Return the partition of the nodes at the given level

\sphinxAtStartPar
A dendrogram is a tree and each level is a partition of the graph nodes.
Level 0 is the first partition, which contains the smallest communities,
and the best is len(dendrogram) \sphinxhyphen{} 1.
The higher the level is, the bigger are the communities
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{dendrogram}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{list}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ of }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}) \textendash{} a list of partitions, ie dictionnaries where keys of the i+1 are the
values of the i.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{level}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} the level which belongs to {[}0..len(dendrogram)\sphinxhyphen{}1{]}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{partition} \textendash{} A dictionary where keys are the nodes and the values are the set it
belongs to

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dictionnary

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{KeyError}} \textendash{} If the dendrogram is not well formed or the level is too high

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{sphinxseealso}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.community_detection.multilayer_benchmark}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer Synthetic Graph Generation for Community Detection Benchmarks

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements synthetic multilayer/multiplex graph generators with
ground\sphinxhyphen{}truth community structure for benchmarking community detection algorithms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Includes:
\sphinxhyphen{} Multilayer LFR (Lancichinetti\sphinxhyphen{}Fortunato\sphinxhyphen{}Radicchi) benchmark
\sphinxhyphen{} Coupled/Interdependent Erdős\sphinxhyphen{}Rényi models
\sphinxhyphen{} Support for overlapping communities across layers
\sphinxhyphen{} Support for partial node presence across layers
\subsubsection*{References}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lancichinetti et al., “Benchmark graphs for testing community detection
algorithms”, Phys. Rev. E 78, 046110 (2008)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Granell et al., “Benchmark model to assess community structure in evolving
networks”, Phys. Rev. E 92, 012805 (2015)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate coupled/interdependent Erdős\sphinxhyphen{}Rényi multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates random Erdős\sphinxhyphen{}Rényi graphs in each layer and couples nodes across
layers with specified coupling strength and probability.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n}} \textendash{} Number of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer names

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Edge probability per layer.
Can be float (same for all layers) or list of floats per layer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength (weight of identity links)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{coupling\_probability}} \textendash{} Probability that a node has inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling.
Range: {[}0, 1{]}
\sphinxhyphen{} 1.0 = all nodes coupled (full multiplex)
\sphinxhyphen{} \textless{}1.0 = partial coupling (interdependent networks)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to generate directed networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\end{description}\end{quote}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate multilayer LFR benchmark networks with controllable community structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This extends the LFR benchmark to multilayer networks, allowing control over:
\sphinxhyphen{} Community persistence across layers (how many nodes keep their community)
\sphinxhyphen{} Node overlap across layers (which nodes appear in which layers)
\sphinxhyphen{} Overlapping communities (nodes belonging to multiple communities)
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n}} \textendash{} Number of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer names

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tau1}} \textendash{} Power\sphinxhyphen{}law exponent for degree distribution (typically 2\sphinxhyphen{}3)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tau2}} \textendash{} Power\sphinxhyphen{}law exponent for community size distribution (typically 1\sphinxhyphen{}2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mu}} \textendash{} Mixing parameter (fraction of edges outside community).
Can be float (same for all layers) or list of floats per layer.
Range: {[}0, 1{]}, where 0 = perfect communities, 1 = random

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{avg\_degree}} \textendash{} Average degree per layer.
Can be float (same for all layers) or list of floats per layer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{min\_community}} \textendash{} Minimum community size

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_community}} \textendash{} Maximum community size (default: n/2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{community\_persistence}} \textendash{} Probability that a node keeps its community from
one layer to the next. Range: {[}0, 1{]}
\sphinxhyphen{} 1.0 = identical communities across all layers
\sphinxhyphen{} 0.0 = completely independent communities per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_overlap}} \textendash{} Fraction of nodes present in all layers. Range: {[}0, 1{]}
\sphinxhyphen{} 1.0 = all nodes in all layers (full multiplex)
\sphinxhyphen{} \textless{}1.0 = some nodes absent from some layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{overlapping\_nodes}} \textendash{} Number of nodes that belong to multiple communities
within each layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{overlapping\_membership}} \textendash{} Number of communities each overlapping node belongs to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to generate directed networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple of (network, ground\_truth\_communities)
\sphinxhyphen{} network: py3plex multi\_layer\_network object
\sphinxhyphen{} ground\_truth\_communities: Dict mapping (node, layer) to Set of community IDs

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate multilayer stochastic block model (SBM) networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates networks where nodes are divided into communities with different
intra\sphinxhyphen{} and inter\sphinxhyphen{}community connection probabilities.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{communities}} \textendash{} List of node sets defining initial communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p\_in}} \textendash{} Intra\sphinxhyphen{}community edge probability per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p\_out}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}community edge probability per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{community\_persistence}} \textendash{} Probability nodes keep their community across layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to generate directed networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple of (network, ground\_truth\_communities)
\sphinxhyphen{} network: py3plex multi\_layer\_network object
\sphinxhyphen{} ground\_truth\_communities: Dict mapping (node, layer) to community ID

\end{description}\end{quote}

\paragraph{Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Network statistics, enrichment tests, and topology utilities.
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer Network Statistics

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements various statistics for multilayer and multiplex networks,
following standard definitions from multilayer network analysis literature.
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kivelä et al. (2014), “Multilayer networks”, J. Complex Networks 2(3), 203\sphinxhyphen{}271

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico et al. (2013), “Mathematical formulation of multilayer networks”, PRX 3, 041022

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mucha et al. (2010), “Community Structure in Time\sphinxhyphen{}Dependent, Multiscale, and Multiplex Networks”, Science 328, 876\sphinxhyphen{}878

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Authors: py3plex contributors
Date: 2025
\index{algebraic\_connectivity() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{algebraic\_connectivity()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.algebraic_connectivity}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{algebraic\_connectivity}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate algebraic connectivity (λ\(\sb{\text{2}}\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: λ\(\sb{\text{2}}\)(ℒ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Second smallest eigenvalue of the supra\sphinxhyphen{}Laplacian (Fiedler value).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Indicates global connectivity and diffusion efficiency of the multilayer system.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
λ\(\sb{\text{0}}\) = 0 always (associated with constant eigenvector)
λ\(\sb{\text{1}}\) \textgreater{} 0 if and only if the multilayer network is connected
Larger λ\(\sb{\text{1}}\) indicates better connectivity and faster diffusion/synchronization

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Second smallest eigenvalue (Fiedler value)

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{alg\PYGZus{}conn} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{algebraic\PYGZus{}connectivity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fiedler (1973), Sole\sphinxhyphen{}Ribalta et al. (2013)

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{community\_participation\_coefficient() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{community\_participation\_coefficient()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.community_participation_coefficient}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{community\_participation\_coefficient}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{communities}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }Any\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }int\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{node}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate participation coefficient for a node across community structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures how evenly a node’s connections are distributed across different
communities, across all layers. A node with connections to many communities
has high participation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Pᵢ = 1 \sphinxhyphen{} Σₛ (kᵢₛ / kᵢ)\(\sp{\text{2}}\)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where kᵢₛ is the number of connections node i has to community s,
and kᵢ is the total degree of node i across all layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{communities}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping (node, layer) to community ID

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node}} \textendash{} Node identifier (not node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuple)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Participation coefficient value between 0 and 1

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{detect\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{pc} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}participation\PYGZus{}coefficient}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Participation: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{pc}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Guimerà \& Amaral (2005), “Functional cartography of complex metabolic networks”

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{community\_participation\_entropy() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{community\_participation\_entropy()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.community_participation_entropy}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{community\_participation\_entropy}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{communities}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }Any\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }int\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{node}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate participation entropy for a node across community structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shannon entropy\sphinxhyphen{}based measure of how evenly a node distributes its
connections across different communities. Higher entropy indicates
more diverse community participation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Hᵢ = \sphinxhyphen{}Σₛ (kᵢₛ / kᵢ) log(kᵢₛ / kᵢ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where kᵢₛ is connections to community s, kᵢ is total degree.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{communities}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping (node, layer) to community ID

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node}} \textendash{} Node identifier (not node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuple)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Entropy value (higher = more diverse participation)

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{entropy} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}participation\PYGZus{}entropy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Participation entropy: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{entropy}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Based on Shannon entropy applied to community structure

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute explicit multislice modularity score.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Direct computation of the modularity quality function for a given
community partition, without running detection algorithms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Q = (1/2μ) Σᵢⱼₐᵦ {[}(Aᵢⱼᵅ \sphinxhyphen{} γ·kᵢᵅkⱼᵅ/(2mₐ))δₐᵦ + ω·δᵢⱼ{]} δ(cᵢᵅ, cⱼᵝ)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{communities}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping (node, layer) to community ID

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter (default: 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength (default: 1.0)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.cross_layer_mutual_information}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{cross\_layer\_mutual\_information}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_i}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_j}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{bins}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{10}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer mutual information (I(Lᵢ; Lⱼ)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: I(Lᵢ; Lⱼ) = H(Lᵢ) + H(Lⱼ) \sphinxhyphen{} H(Lᵢ, Lⱼ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures statistical dependence between degree distributions in two layers;
quantifies how much knowing a node’s degree in one layer tells us about
its degree in another layer.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
H(Lᵢ) = entropy of degree distribution in layer i
H(Lⱼ) = entropy of degree distribution in layer j
H(Lᵢ, Lⱼ) = joint entropy of degree distributions

\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
I = 0 when layers are independent
I \textgreater{} 0 indicates statistical dependence (higher = stronger)
I(Lᵢ; Lⱼ) ≤ min(H(Lᵢ), H(Lⱼ))

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{bins}} \textendash{} Number of bins for discretizing degree distributions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mutual information value in bits

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{mi} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{cross\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}mutual\PYGZus{}information}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{bins}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Mutual information: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{mi}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ bits}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cover \& Thomas (2006), “Elements of Information Theory”
De Domenico et al. (2015), “Structural reducibility”

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{cross\_layer\_redundancy\_entropy() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{cross\_layer\_redundancy\_entropy()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer redundancy entropy (H\_redundancy).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: H\_r = \sphinxhyphen{}Σᵢⱼ rᵢⱼ log\(\sb{\text{2}}\)(rᵢⱼ), where rᵢⱼ is the normalized edge overlap
between layers i and j.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures diversity in structural redundancy across layer pairs; high entropy
indicates varied overlap patterns, low entropy indicates uniform redundancy.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
rᵢⱼ = edge\_overlap(i,j) / Σₐᵦ edge\_overlap(α,β)
Normalized overlap proportion for each layer pair

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Entropy value in bits

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{entropy} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{cross\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}redundancy\PYGZus{}entropy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Cross\PYGZhy{}layer redundancy entropy: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{entropy}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

Bianconi (2018), “Multilayer Networks: Structure and Function”

\index{entropy\_of\_multiplexity() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{entropy\_of\_multiplexity()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.entropy_of_multiplexity}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{entropy\_of\_multiplexity}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate entropy of multiplexity (Hₘ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Hₘ = \sphinxhyphen{}Σₐ pₐ log\(\sb{\text{2}}\)(pₐ), where pₐ = Eₐ / Σᵦ Eᵦ

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shannon entropy of layer contributions; measures layer diversity.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
pₐ = proportion of edges in layer α
Eₐ = number of edges in layer α
log\(\sb{\text{2}}\) gives entropy in bits

\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hₘ = 0 when all edges are in one layer (minimum entropy/diversity)
Hₘ = log\(\sb{\text{2}}\)(L) when edges are uniformly distributed across L layers (maximum entropy)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Entropy value in bits

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{entropy} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{entropy\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}multiplexity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico et al. (2013), Shannon (1948)

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{inter\_layer\_assortativity() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{inter\_layer\_assortativity()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.inter_layer_assortativity}}
\pysigstartsignatures

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_i}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_j}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer assortativity (rᴵ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: r\textasciicircum{}αβ = cov(k\textasciicircum{}α, k\textasciicircum{}β) / (σₐ σᵦ) = corr(k\textasciicircum{}α, k\textasciicircum{}β)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures whether nodes with similar degrees tend to connect across different layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
k\textasciicircum{}α = degree vector in layer α
k\textasciicircum{}β = degree vector in layer β
σₐ, σᵦ = standard deviations of degrees in layers α and β
Equivalent to Pearson correlation of degree vectors

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier (α)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier (β)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assortativity coefficient

\end{description}\end{quote}

Calculate inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength (C\textasciicircum{}αβ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Average weight of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections between corresponding nodes in two layers.
Quantifies cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer connectivity.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
N\_αβ = number of nodes present in both layers α and β
wᵢ\textasciicircum{}αβ = weight of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edge connecting node i in layer α to node i in layer β

\end{description}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier (α)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier (β)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Average coupling strength

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{inter\_layer\_dependence\_entropy() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{inter\_layer\_dependence\_entropy()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer dependence entropy (H\_dep).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: H\_dep = \sphinxhyphen{}Σₙ pₙ log\(\sb{\text{2}}\)(pₙ), where pₙ is the proportion of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer
edges for each node n connecting layers i and j.

Measures heterogeneity in how nodes couple the two layers; high entropy
indicates diverse coupling patterns, low entropy indicates uniform coupling.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}

Total over all nodes connecting the two layers

\end{description}

\item {}

\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Entropy value in bits

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\index{interdependence() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{interdependence()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.interdependence}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{interdependence}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{sample\_size}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate interdependence (λ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: λ = ⟨dᴹᴸ⟩ / ⟨dᵃᵛᵍ⟩

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quantifies how much shortest\sphinxhyphen{}path communication depends on inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dᵢⱼᴹᴸ = shortest path from node i to node j in the full multilayer network
dᵢⱼᵃᵛᵍ = (1/L) Σₐ dᵢⱼᵅ is the average shortest path across individual layers
⟨·⟩ = average over sampled node pairs

\sphinxlineitem{Interpretation:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
λ \textless{} 1: multilayer connectivity reduces path lengths (positive interdependence)
λ ≈ 1: inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections provide little benefit
λ \textgreater{} 1: multilayer structure increases path lengths (rare)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sample\_size}} \textendash{} Number of node pairs to sample for estimation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interdependence ratio

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{interdep} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{interdependence}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Gomez et al. (2013), Buldyrev et al. (2010)

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{interlayer\_degree\_correlation\_matrix() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{interlayer\_degree\_correlation\_matrix()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.interlayer_degree_correlation_matrix}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{interlayer\_degree\_correlation\_matrix}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}ndarray\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }list\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer degree correlation matrix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes Pearson correlation coefficients for node degrees between all
pairs of layers, organized as a symmetric correlation matrix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Matrix{[}α,β{]} = r\textasciicircum{}αβ = corr(k\textasciicircum{}α, k\textasciicircum{}β)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where k\textasciicircum{}α and k\textasciicircum{}β are degree vectors for layers α and β over common nodes.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Diagonal elements are 1.0 (self\sphinxhyphen{}correlation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal elements in {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Symmetric matrix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Positive values indicate positive degree correlation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Negative values indicate negative degree correlation

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
correlation\_matrix: 2D numpy array of shape (num\_layers, num\_layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
layer\_labels: List of layer names corresponding to matrix indices

\end{itemize}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple of (correlation\_matrix, layer\_labels)

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{interlayer\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}correlation\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{seaborn}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{sns}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{sns}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{heatmap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{annot}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{xticklabels}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }            \PYG{n}{yticklabels}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{cmap}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{coolwarm}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{center}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }            \PYG{n}{vmin}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{vmax}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{title}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Inter\PYGZhy{}layer Degree Correlation Matrix}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nicosia \& Latora (2015), “Measuring and modeling correlations in multiplex networks”

\index{layer\_connectivity\_entropy() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{layer\_connectivity\_entropy()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.layer_connectivity_entropy}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_connectivity\_entropy}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate entropy of layer connectivity (H\_connectivity).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: H\_c = \sphinxhyphen{}Σᵢ (kᵢ/Σⱼkⱼ) log\(\sb{\text{2}}\)(kᵢ/Σⱼkⱼ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shannon entropy of degree distribution within a layer; measures
heterogeneity of node connectivity patterns.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
kᵢ = degree of node i in the layer
Σⱼkⱼ = sum of all degrees (2 * edges for undirected)

\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
H\_c = 0 when all nodes have the same degree (uniform distribution)
H\_c is maximized when degree distribution is highly uneven

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer}} \textendash{} Layer identifier

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Entropy value in bits

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{method}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}coupling\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{sample\_size}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate layer influence centrality (Iᵅ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula (coupling): Iᵅ = Σᵦ≠ᵅ C\textasciicircum{}αβ / (L\sphinxhyphen{}1)
Formula (flow): Iᵅ = Σᵦ≠ᵅ F\textasciicircum{}αβ / (L\sphinxhyphen{}1)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quantifies how much a layer influences other layers through inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer
connections (coupling method) or information flow (flow method).
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
C\textasciicircum{}αβ = inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength between layers α and β
F\textasciicircum{}αβ = flow from layer α to layer β (random walk transition probability)
L = total number of layers

\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Higher values indicate layers that strongly influence others
Useful for identifying critical layers in the multilayer structure

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer}} \textendash{} Layer identifier

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} \textendash{} ‘coupling’ for structural influence, ‘flow’ for dynamic influence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sample\_size}} \textendash{} Number of random walk steps for flow simulation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Influence centrality value

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{influence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}influence\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{method}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{coupling}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Layer L1 influence: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{influence}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cozzo et al. (2013), “Mathematical formulation of multilayer networks”
De Domenico et al. (2014), “Identifying modular flows”

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_i}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_j}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate layer redundancy coefficient.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures the proportion of edges in one layer that are redundant
(also present) in another layer. Values close to 1 indicate high
redundancy, while values close to 0 indicate complementary layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Rᵅᵝ = {\color{red}\bfseries{}|Eᵅ ∩ Eᵝ|} / {\color{red}\bfseries{}|Eᵅ|}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where Eᵅ and Eᵝ are edge sets of layers α and β.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Redundancy coefficient between 0 and 1

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{redundancy} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}redundancy\PYGZus{}coefficient}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Redundancy: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{redundancy}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nicosia \& Latora (2015), “Measuring and modeling correlations in multiplex networks”

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_i}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_j}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{method}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}cosine\textquotesingle{}}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate layer similarity (S\textasciicircum{}αβ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: S\textasciicircum{}αβ = ⟨Aₐ, Aᵦ⟩ / (‖Aₐ‖ ‖Aᵦ‖) = Σᵢⱼ AᵢⱼᵅAᵢⱼᵝ / √(Σᵢⱼ(Aᵢⱼᵅ)\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) √(Σᵢⱼ(Aᵢⱼᵝ)\(\sp{\text{2}}\))

\sphinxAtStartPar
Cosine or Jaccard similarity between adjacency matrices of two layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aₐ, Aᵦ = adjacency matrices for layers α and β
⟨·,·⟩ = Frobenius inner product
‖·‖ = Frobenius norm

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier (α)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier (β)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} \textendash{} ‘cosine’ or ‘jaccard’

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarity value between 0 and 1

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{similarity} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}similarity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{method}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{cosine}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer betweenness surface (tensor representation).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes betweenness centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair and organizes
the results as a 2D array (nodes × layers) that can be visualized as
a heatmap or surface plot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Surface{[}i,α{]} = Bᵢᵅ

\sphinxAtStartPar
where Bᵢᵅ is the betweenness centrality of node i in layer α.

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize betweenness values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute name (None for unweighted)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
2D numpy array of shape (num\_nodes, num\_layers) containing betweenness values.
Also returns tuple of (node\_labels, layer\_labels) for axis labeling.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer clustering coefficient (Cᴹ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Cᵢᴹ = Tᵢ / Tᵢᵐᵃˣ

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extends transitivity to account for triangles that span multiple layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tᵢ = number of closed triplets (triangles) involving node i across all layers
Tᵢᵐᵃˣ = maximum possible triplets = Σₐ kᵢᵅ(kᵢᵅ \sphinxhyphen{} 1)/2 for undirected networks
Average over all nodes: Cᴹ = (1/N) Σᵢ Cᵢᴹ

\end{description}

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node}} \textendash{} If specified, compute for single node; otherwise compute for all

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clustering coefficient value or dict of values per node

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer modularity (Qᴹᴸ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a wrapper for the existing multilayer\_modularity implementation
in py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Qᴹᴸ = (1/2μ) Σᵢⱼₐᵦ {[}(Aᵢⱼᵅ \sphinxhyphen{} γₐPᵢⱼᵅ)δₐᵦ + ωₐᵦδᵢⱼ{]} δ(gᵢᵅ, gⱼᵝ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extension of Newman\sphinxhyphen{}Girvan modularity to multiplex networks (Mucha et al., 2010).
Measures community quality across layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
μ = total edge weight in supra\sphinxhyphen{}network
Aᵢⱼᵅ = adjacency matrix element for layer α
Pᵢⱼᵅ = kᵢᵅkⱼᵅ/(2mₐ) is the null model (configuration model)
γₐ = resolution parameter for layer α
ωₐᵦ = inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength
δₐᵦ = Kronecker delta (1 if α=β, 0 otherwise)
δᵢⱼ = Kronecker delta (1 if i=j, 0 otherwise)
δ(gᵢᵅ, gⱼᵝ) = 1 if node i in layer α and node j in layer β are in same community

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{communities}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to community IDs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modularity value Q

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{C}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

Mucha et al. (2010), Science 328(5980), 876\sphinxhyphen{}878

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer motif frequency (fₘ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: fₘ = nₘ / Σₖ nₖ

\sphinxAtStartPar
Frequency of recurring subgraph patterns across layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
nₘ = count of motif type m
Σₖ nₖ = total count of all motifs

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note: This is a simplified implementation counting basic patterns (intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer vs.
inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer triangles). Complete multilayer motif enumeration includes many more
configurations and is computationally expensive.

{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }Any\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multiplex betweenness centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes betweenness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph, accounting for paths
that traverse inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer couplings. This extends the standard betweenness
definition to multiplex networks where paths can cross layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Bᵢᵅ = Σₛ≠ᵢ≠ₜ (σₛₜ(iα) / σₛₜ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where σₛₜ is the total number of shortest paths from s to t, and
σₛₜ(iα) is the number of those paths passing through node i in layer α.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize by the number of node pairs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute name (None for unweighted)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to betweenness centrality values

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{sorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{betweenness}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{key}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico et al. (2015), “Structural reducibility of multilayer networks”

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{multiplex\_closeness\_centrality() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{multiplex\_closeness\_centrality()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.multiplex_closeness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multiplex\_closeness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{weight}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{variant}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}standard\textquotesingle{}}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }Any\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multiplex closeness centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes closeness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph, where shortest paths
can traverse inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges. This captures how quickly a node\sphinxhyphen{}layer
can reach all other node\sphinxhyphen{}layers in the multiplex network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Standard closeness formula: Cᵢᵅ = (N*L \sphinxhyphen{} 1) / Σⱼᵝ≠ᵢᵅ d(iα, jβ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Harmonic closeness formula: HCᵢᵅ = Σⱼᵝ≠ᵢᵅ 1/d(iα, jβ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where d(iα, jβ) is the shortest path distance from node i in layer α
to node j in layer β, and N*L is the total number of node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize by network size

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute name (None for unweighted)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{variant}} \textendash{} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Closeness variant to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘standard’: Classic closeness (reciprocal of sum of distances).
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Can produce biased values for nodes in disconnected components.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’harmonic’: Harmonic closeness (sum of reciprocal distances).
Recommended for disconnected multilayer networks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’auto’: Automatically selects ‘harmonic’ if the network has
multiple connected components, otherwise uses ‘standard’.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default is ‘standard’ for backward compatibility.


\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to closeness centrality values

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{k}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multiplex rich\sphinxhyphen{}club coefficient.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures the tendency of high\sphinxhyphen{}degree nodes to be more densely connected
to each other than expected by chance, accounting for the multiplex structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: φᴹ(k) = Eᴹ(\textgreater{}k) / (Nᴹ(\textgreater{}k) * (Nᴹ(\textgreater{}k)\sphinxhyphen{}1) / 2)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where Eᴹ(\textgreater{}k) is the number of edges among nodes with overlapping degree \textgreater{} k,
and Nᴹ(\textgreater{}k) is the number of such nodes.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{k}} \textendash{} Degree threshold

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize by random expectation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rich\sphinxhyphen{}club coefficient value

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rich\PYGZus{}club} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}rich\PYGZus{}club\PYGZus{}coefficient}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Rich\PYGZhy{}club coefficient: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{rich\PYGZus{}club}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Alstott et al. (2014), “powerlaw: A Python Package for Analysis of Heavy\sphinxhyphen{}Tailed Distributions”
Extended to multiplex networks

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate node activity (aᵢ).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Activity value between 0 and 1

\sphinxlineitem{Contracts:}\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: node must not be None

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: result is in {[}0, 1{]} (fraction of layers)

Postcondition: result is not NaN

\end{itemize}

\index{resilience() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{resilience()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.resilience}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{resilience}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{perturbation\_type}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}layer\_removal\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{perturbation\_param}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate resilience (R).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: R = S’ / S\(\sb{\text{0}}\)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ratio of largest connected component after perturbation to original size.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
S\(\sb{\text{0}}\) = size of largest connected component in original network
S’ = size of largest connected component after perturbation

\sphinxlineitem{Perturbation types:}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer removal: Remove all nodes/edges in a specific layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Coupling removal: Remove a fraction of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
R = 1 indicates full resilience (no impact from perturbation)
R = 0 indicates complete fragmentation
0 \textless{} R \textless{} 1 indicates partial resilience

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturbation\_type}} \textendash{} ‘layer\_removal’ or ‘coupling\_removal’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturbation\_param}} \textendash{} Layer to remove or fraction of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Resilience ratio between 0 and 1

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{r} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{resilience}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer\PYGZus{}removal}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{perturbation\PYGZus{}param}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{r} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{resilience}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{coupling\PYGZus{}removal}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{perturbation\PYGZus{}param}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Buldyrev et al. (2010), Nature 464, 1025\sphinxhyphen{}1028

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{supra\_laplacian\_spectrum() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{supra\_laplacian\_spectrum()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.supra_laplacian_spectrum}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{supra\_laplacian\_spectrum}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{k}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{10}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate supra\sphinxhyphen{}Laplacian spectrum (Λ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: ℒ = 𝒟 \sphinxhyphen{} 𝒜

\sphinxAtStartPar
Eigenvalue spectrum of the supra\sphinxhyphen{}Laplacian matrix; captures diffusion properties.
Uses sparse eigenvalue computation when beneficial.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
𝒜 = supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (NL × NL block matrix containing all layers and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer couplings)
𝒟 = supra\sphinxhyphen{}degree matrix (diagonal matrix with row sums of 𝒜)
ℒ = supra\sphinxhyphen{}Laplacian matrix
Λ = \{λ\(\sb{\text{0}}\), λ\(\sb{\text{1}}\), …, λₙₗ₋\(\sb{\text{1}}\)\} with 0 = λ\(\sb{\text{0}}\) ≤ λ\(\sb{\text{1}}\) ≤ … ≤ λₙₗ₋\(\sb{\text{1}}\)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{k}} \textendash{} Number of smallest eigenvalues to compute

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Array of k smallest eigenvalues

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{spectrum} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}laplacian\PYGZus{}spectrum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico et al. (2013), Gomez et al. (2013)

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses sparse eigsh() for sparse matrices (more efficient)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Falls back to dense computation for small matrices (n \textless{} 100) or when k is large relative to n

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Laplacian is always symmetric for undirected graphs (PSD with smallest eigenvalue = 0)

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate versatility centrality (Vᵢ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Vᵢ = Σₐ wₐ Cᵢᵅ

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weighted combination of node centrality values across layers; measures overall influence.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
wₐ = weight for layer α (typically 1/L for uniform weighting, Σₐ wₐ = 1)
Cᵢᵅ = centrality of node i in layer α (can be degree, betweenness, closeness, etc.)

\end{description}

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Layer weights (default: uniform weights)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping nodes to versatility centrality values

\paragraph{Multilayer Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:multilayer-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Algorithms designed for multilayer graphs, including centrality and entanglement measures.
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer/Multiplex Network Centrality Measures

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements various centrality measures for multilayer and multiplex networks,
following standard definitions from multilayer network analysis literature.


\subparagraph{Weight Handling Notes:}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:weight-handling-notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For path\sphinxhyphen{}based centralities (betweenness, closeness):
\sphinxhyphen{} Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix are converted to distances (inverse of weight)
\sphinxhyphen{} NetworkX algorithms use these distances for shortest path computation
\sphinxhyphen{} betweenness\_centrality: weight parameter specifies the edge attribute for path computation
\sphinxhyphen{} closeness\_centrality: distance parameter specifies the edge attribute for path computation

\sphinxAtStartPar
For disconnected graphs:
\sphinxhyphen{} closeness\_centrality uses wf\_improved parameter (Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust scaling) by default
\sphinxhyphen{} When wf\_improved=True, scores are normalized by reachable nodes only
\sphinxhyphen{} When wf\_improved=False, unreachable nodes contribute infinite distance

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weight Constraints:
\sphinxhyphen{} Weights should be positive (\textgreater{} 0) for shortest path algorithms
\sphinxhyphen{} Zero or negative weights will cause undefined behavior
\sphinxhyphen{} For unweighted analysis, use weighted=False parameters

\sphinxAtStartPar
Authors: py3plex contributors
Date: 2025
