\index{accessibility\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{accessibility\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.accessibility_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{accessibility\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{h}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{2}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute accessibility centrality (entropy\sphinxhyphen{}based reach within h steps).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Accessibility measures the diversity of nodes reachable within h steps
using entropy of the probability distribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Access\_r = exp(H\_r) where H\_r is the entropy of the h\sphinxhyphen{}step distribution
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{h}} \textendash{} Number of steps (default: 2)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): accessibility\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accessibility is measured as the effective number of h\sphinxhyphen{}step destinations,
using the entropy of the random walk distribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Dangling Node Handling: For nodes with no outgoing edges (dangling nodes),
this implementation uses uniform teleportation to all nodes. This differs
from the original Travencolo\sphinxhyphen{}Costa definition which does not include
teleportation. The teleportation ensures a well\sphinxhyphen{}defined random walk
distribution but may affect accessibility values for nodes near dangling
nodes compared to implementations that handle dangling nodes differently.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Travencolo, B. A. N., \& Costa, L. D. F. (2008). Accessibility in complex
networks. Physics Letters A, 373(1), 89\sphinxhyphen{}95.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{bridging\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{bridging\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.bridging_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{bridging\_centrality}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute bridging centrality for nodes in the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bridging centrality combines betweenness with the bridging coefficient,
which measures how much a node connects sparse regions of the network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bridging(u) = B(u) * BCoeff(u)
where BCoeff(u) = (1 / k\_u) * sum\_\{v in N(u)\} {[}1 / k\_v{]}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): bridging\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes with higher bridging centrality act as important bridges
connecting different parts of the network.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute collective influence (CI\_ℓ) for multiplex networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Collective influence identifies influential spreaders by considering
not just immediate neighbors but also nodes at distance ℓ.

\sphinxAtStartPar
CI\_ℓ(u) = (k\_u \sphinxhyphen{} 1) * sum\_\{v in ∂Ball\_ℓ(u)\} (k\_v \sphinxhyphen{} 1)
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{radius}} \textendash{} Radius ℓ for the ball boundary (default: 2)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): collective\_influence\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses overlapping degree across all layers for each physical node.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{communicability\_betweenness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{communicability\_betweenness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.communicability_betweenness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{communicability\_betweenness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute communicability betweenness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This measure quantifies how much a node contributes to the communicability
between other pairs of nodes. It uses the matrix exponential to account
for all walks between nodes.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} If True (default), normalize scores by dividing by the
maximum value (min\sphinxhyphen{}max scaling to {[}0, 1{]} range). Note that
this is simple rescaling, not the theoretical Estrada\sphinxhyphen{}Hatano
normalization from the original literature.

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): communicability\_betweenness\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation uses NetworkX’s communicability\_betweenness\_centrality,
which operates on unweighted graphs. Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency
matrix are used only to determine edge existence (weight \textgreater{} 0), not for
weighted communicability computation. For truly weighted communicability
analysis, a custom implementation using the weighted matrix exponential
would be required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is computationally expensive as it requires computing the matrix
exponential multiple times. For large networks, this may take significant time.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{flow\_betweenness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{flow\_betweenness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.flow_betweenness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{flow\_betweenness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{samples}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute flow betweenness based on maximum flow sampling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Flow betweenness measures how much flow passes through a node when
maximizing flow between randomly sampled source\sphinxhyphen{}target pairs.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{samples}} \textendash{} Number of source\sphinxhyphen{}target pairs to sample (default: 100)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): flow\_betweenness\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a sampling\sphinxhyphen{}based approximation of flow betweenness. The
implementation samples random pairs of supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph nodes and computes
the maximum flow through each intermediate node.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike classical Freeman flow betweenness which uses a normalization
factor based on the number of nodes, this implementation returns the
average flow per sampled pair without additional normalization. For
multilayer networks, the number of supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph nodes (N * L for N
physical nodes and L layers) affects the raw values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks, this sampling approach is more computationally
feasible than computing exact flow betweenness for all pairs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{harmonic\_closeness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{harmonic\_closeness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.harmonic_closeness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{harmonic\_closeness\_centrality}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute harmonic closeness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Harmonic closeness handles disconnected graphs better than standard closeness
by summing the reciprocals of distances instead of taking reciprocal of sum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
HC(u) = sum\_\{v≠u\} (1 / d(u,v)) for finite distances
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): harmonic\_closeness\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This measure naturally handles disconnected components as unreachable
nodes contribute 0 (instead of infinity) to the sum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weight Interpretation: Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix
are interpreted as connection strengths (larger weight = stronger
connection = shorter distance). They are converted to distances via
1/weight for shortest path computation. If your edge weights already
represent distances, do not use this function directly—you would need
to invert them first or use the distance values directly in a custom
computation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{information\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{information\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures

{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{information\_centrality}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Information Centrality (Stephenson\sphinxhyphen{}Zelen style) on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Information centrality measures the importance of a node based on the
information flow through the network. It uses the inverse of a modified
Laplacian matrix.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): information\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation returns values for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair in the
supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph, not aggregated physical node values. To obtain physical
node\sphinxhyphen{}level information centrality, use the aggregate\_to\_node\_level()
method on the returned dictionary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The implementation uses NetworkX’s information\_centrality for computation.
Falls back to harmonic closeness if information centrality computation fails.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Information centrality is defined only for undirected graphs. For directed
networks, the graph is symmetrized with a warning.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stephenson, K., \& Zelen, M. (1989). Rethinking centrality: Methods and
examples. Social Networks, 11(1), 1\sphinxhyphen{}37.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

Compute load centrality (shortest\sphinxhyphen{}path load).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Load centrality measures the fraction of shortest paths that pass
through each node, counting all paths (not just unique pairs).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Load{[}k{]} = sum over all (s,t) pairs of {[}number of shortest paths through k / total shortest paths{]}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): load\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is similar to betweenness but counts all paths rather than
normalizing by the number of node pairs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{local\_efficiency\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{local\_efficiency\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{local\_efficiency\_centrality}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute local efficiency centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Local efficiency measures how efficiently information is exchanged among
a node’s neighbors when the node is removed. It quantifies the fault
tolerance of the network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LE(u) = (1 / ({\color{red}\bfseries{}|N\_u|*(|N\_u|}\sphinxhyphen{}1))) * sum\_\{i≠j in N\_u\} {[}1 / d(i,j){]}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): local\_efficiency\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For nodes with less than 2 neighbors, local efficiency is 0.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{lp\_aggregated\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{lp\_aggregated\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.lp_aggregated_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{lp\_aggregated\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_centralities}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{p}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{2}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{weights}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{exclude\_missing}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Lp\sphinxhyphen{}aggregated per\sphinxhyphen{}layer centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregates per\sphinxhyphen{}layer centrality values using Lp norm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
C\_i = (sum\_\{ℓ in L\_i\} w\_ℓ * {\color{red}\bfseries{}|c\textasciicircum{}ℓ{[}i{]}|\textasciicircum{}p)\textasciicircum{}\{1/p\}  for p \textless{} \(\infty\)
C\_i = max\_\{ℓ in L\_i\} (w\_ℓ * |c\textasciicircum{}ℓ{[}i{]}|})          for p = \(\infty\)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where L\_i is the set of layers where node i exists.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_centralities}} \textendash{} dict of \{layer: \{node: centrality\}\} or
\{(node, layer): centrality\}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Lp norm parameter (default: 2). Use float(‘inf’) for L\sphinxhyphen{}infinity norm.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weights}} \textendash{} dict of \{layer: weight\}. If None, uniform weights are used.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{exclude\_missing}} \textendash{} If True (default), only aggregate over layers where
the node exists (has a centrality value). If False,
treat nodes absent from a layer as having zero centrality,
which may bias scores for nodes with sparse layer
participation.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{node: aggregated\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a framework for aggregating any per\sphinxhyphen{}layer centrality measure.
Input can be degree, PageRank, eigenvector, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sparse Layer Participation: When exclude\_missing=True (default), nodes
that only appear in a subset of layers are aggregated only over those
layers where they exist. This prevents bias against nodes with sparse
layer participation. When exclude\_missing=False, missing layers contribute
zero to the aggregation, which may penalize nodes that don’t appear in
all layers.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{multilayer\_betweenness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{multilayer\_betweenness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_betweenness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{endpoints}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute betweenness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (i,α), computes the fraction of shortest
paths between all pairs of nodes that pass through (i,α).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize the betweenness values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{endpoints}} \textendash{} Whether to include endpoints in path counts.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): betweenness\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is computationally expensive for large networks as it
requires computing shortest paths between all pairs of nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weight handling: Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix are
converted to distances (1/weight) for shortest path computation.
Weights must be positive (\textgreater{} 0). Zero or negative weights will
cause undefined behavior.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{multilayer\_closeness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{multilayer\_closeness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.multilayer_closeness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_closeness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{wf\_improved}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{variant}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}standard\textquotesingle{}}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute closeness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (i,α), computes:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Standard closeness:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
C\_c(i,α) = (n\sphinxhyphen{}1) / Σ\_\{(j,β)\} d((i,α), (j,β))

\sphinxlineitem{Harmonic closeness (recommended for disconnected networks):}
\sphinxAtStartPar
HC(i,α) = Σ\_\{(j,β)≠(i,α)\} 1/d((i,α), (j,β))

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where d((i,α), (j,β)) is the shortest path distance in the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} This parameter is kept for API compatibility but has no effect.
Standard closeness is always normalized by (n\sphinxhyphen{}1) per the
NetworkX implementation. Harmonic closeness returns unnormalized
sums of reciprocal distances by definition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{wf\_improved}} \textendash{} If True, use Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust improved closeness scaling
for disconnected graphs. Default is True. This affects
the magnitude and ordering of scores in graphs with
multiple components (e.g., low interlayer coupling).
See NetworkX documentation for details. Only used when
variant=’standard’.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{variant}} \textendash{} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Closeness variant to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘standard’: Classic closeness (reciprocal of sum of distances).
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For disconnected graphs, uses Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust scaling if
wf\_improved=True. Can produce biased values for nodes in
small or disconnected components.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’harmonic’: Harmonic closeness (sum of reciprocal distances).
Mathematically well\sphinxhyphen{}defined for disconnected networks:
unreachable nodes contribute 0 instead of infinity.
Recommended for disconnected multilayer networks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’auto’: Automatically selects ‘harmonic’ if the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph
has multiple connected components, otherwise uses ‘standard’.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default is ‘standard’ for backward compatibility.


\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): closeness\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation uses NetworkX’s shortest path algorithms on
the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph representation. For large networks, this can be
computationally expensive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For disconnected multilayer graphs (e.g., layers with no inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer
coupling, or networks with isolated components), use variant=’harmonic’
or variant=’auto’ to get mathematically consistent closeness values.
The harmonic variant naturally handles unreachable nodes by summing
1/d for finite distances only (infinite distances contribute 0).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weight Interpretation: Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix
are interpreted as connection strengths (larger weight = stronger
connection). They are converted to distances via 1/weight for
shortest path computation. If your edge weights already represent
distances, use them directly without this function’s weight inversion.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For connected networks, standard closeness works well}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{calc}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{variant}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{standard}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For potentially disconnected networks, use harmonic}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{calc}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{variant}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{harmonic}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Let the algorithm decide based on connectivity}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{calc}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{variant}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{auto}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute PageRank centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses the standard PageRank algorithm on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix
representing the multilayer network. Properly handles dangling nodes
(nodes with no outgoing edges) via teleportation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation preserves sparsity when possible for memory efficiency.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{damping}} \textendash{} Damping parameter (typically 0.85).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for convergence.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): centrality\_value\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Mathematical Invariants:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PageRank values sum to 1.0 (within tol=1e\sphinxhyphen{}6)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All values are non\sphinxhyphen{}negative

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Converges for strongly connected components or with teleportation

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{percolation\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{percolation\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.percolation_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{percolation\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{edge\_activation\_prob}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.5}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{trials}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute percolation centrality using bond percolation Monte Carlo simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation measures the average relative component size that a node
belongs to across multiple bond percolation realizations, providing an estimate
of a node’s importance for network connectivity under random edge failures.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_activation\_prob}} \textendash{} Probability that an edge is active (default: 0.5)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{trials}} \textendash{} Number of Monte Carlo trials (default: 100)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): percolation\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a component\sphinxhyphen{}size\sphinxhyphen{}based percolation measure, not the path\sphinxhyphen{}based
percolation betweenness from the original Piraveenan et al. literature,
which requires recomputing betweenness on each percolated realization.
The original percolation centrality is computationally expensive (O(n\(\sp{\text{3}}\))
per trial), so this implementation provides a more efficient alternative
that captures related connectivity information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Values are normalized to {[}0, 1{]} range where higher values indicate nodes
that tend to belong to larger connected components across percolation
realizations.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Piraveenan, M., Prokopenko, M., \& Hossain, L. (2013). Percolation
centrality: Quantifying graph\sphinxhyphen{}theoretic impact of nodes during
percolation in networks. PloS one, 8(1), e53095.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{spreading\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{spreading\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.spreading_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{spreading\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{beta}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.2}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{mu}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{trials}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{50}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{steps}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute spreading (epidemic) centrality using SIR model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Spreading centrality measures how influential a node is in spreading
information or disease through the network, based on Monte Carlo
simulations of discrete\sphinxhyphen{}time SIR dynamics.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{beta}} \textendash{} Infection rate per edge per time step (default: 0.2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mu}} \textendash{} Recovery rate per time step (default: 0.1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{trials}} \textendash{} Number of simulation trials per node (default: 50)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{steps}} \textendash{} Maximum simulation steps (default: 100)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): spreading\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This measures the average outbreak size (fraction of nodes ever infected)
when seeding the epidemic from each node. Values are normalized by the
total number of nodes, producing scores in the range {[}1/n, 1{]} where n is
the number of supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is an empirical simulation\sphinxhyphen{}based measure, not normalized by
theoretical epidemic threshold or branching factor as in some literature
definitions. The normalization allows comparison of relative spreading
power within the network but may not be directly comparable across
networks of different sizes or structures.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kitsak, M., et al. (2010). Identification of influential spreaders
in complex networks. Nature physics, 6(11), 888\sphinxhyphen{}893.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{communicability\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{supra\_matrix}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{spmatrix}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalize}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{use\_sparse}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{max\_iter}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{100}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tol}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1e\sphinxhyphen{}06}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute communicability centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Communicability centrality measures the weighted sum of all walks between
nodes, with exponentially decaying weights for longer walks. It is computed
as the row sum of the matrix exponential:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_i = sum\_j (exp(A))\_ij
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation uses scipy.sparse.linalg.expm\_multiply for efficient
sparse matrix exponential computation.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{supra\_matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (n x n).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalize}} \textendash{} If True, normalize output to sum to 1.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{use\_sparse}} \textendash{} If True, use sparse matrix operations. Falls back to dense
for matrices smaller than 10000 elements.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations for sparse approximation (currently unused).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for convergence (currently unused).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Communicability centrality scores for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (n,).

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexMatrixError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexMatrixError}}}}} \textendash{} If matrix is invalid (non\sphinxhyphen{}square, empty, etc.).

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{comm} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{communicability\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Communicability centrality computed for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{compute\_all\_centralities() (in module py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality)@\spxentry{compute\_all\_centralities()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.compute_all_centralities}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{compute\_all\_centralities}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{include\_path\_based}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{include\_advanced}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{include\_extended}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{preset}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{wf\_improved}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{closeness\_variant}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}standard\textquotesingle{}}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute all available centrality measures for a multilayer network.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{include\_path\_based}} \textendash{} Whether to include computationally expensive path\sphinxhyphen{}based measures
(betweenness, closeness). Default: False

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{include\_advanced}} \textendash{} Whether to include advanced measures (HITS, current\sphinxhyphen{}flow,
communicability, k\sphinxhyphen{}core). Default: False

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{include\_extended}} \textendash{} Whether to include extended measures (information, accessibility,
percolation, spreading, collective influence, load, flow betweenness,
harmonic, bridging, local efficiency). Default: False

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{preset}} \textendash{} Convenience parameter to set all inclusion flags at once. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘basic’: Only degree and eigenvector\sphinxhyphen{}based measures (default behavior)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘standard’: Includes path\sphinxhyphen{}based measures
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘advanced’: Includes path\sphinxhyphen{}based and advanced measures
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘all’: Includes all measures (path\sphinxhyphen{}based, advanced, and extended)
\sphinxhyphen{} None: Use individual flags (default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{wf\_improved}} \textendash{} If True, use Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust improved scaling for closeness
centrality in disconnected graphs. Default: True. Only used when
closeness\_variant=’standard’.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{closeness\_variant}} \textendash{} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Variant of closeness centrality to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘standard’: Classic closeness (reciprocal of sum of distances).
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust scaling if wf\_improved=True.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’harmonic’: Harmonic closeness (sum of reciprocal distances).
Recommended for disconnected multilayer networks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’auto’: Automatically selects ‘harmonic’ if the network has
disconnected components, otherwise uses ‘standard’.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default: ‘standard’ for backward compatibility.


\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Dictionary containing all computed centrality measures with keys:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Degree\sphinxhyphen{}based: “layer\_degree”, “layer\_strength”, “supra\_degree”,
“supra\_strength”, “overlapping\_degree”, “overlapping\_strength”,
“participation\_coefficient”, “participation\_coefficient\_strength”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Eigenvector\sphinxhyphen{}based: “multiplex\_eigenvector”, “eigenvector\_versatility”,
“katz\_bonacich”, “pagerank”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Path\sphinxhyphen{}based (if include\_path\_based=True): “closeness”, “betweenness”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Advanced (if include\_advanced=True): “hits”, “current\_flow\_closeness”,
“current\_flow\_betweenness”, “subgraph\_centrality”,
“total\_communicability”, “multiplex\_k\_core”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extended (if include\_extended=True): “information”, “communicability\_betweenness”,
“accessibility”, “harmonic\_closeness”, “local\_efficiency”, “edge\_betweenness”,
“bridging”, “percolation”, “spreading”, “collective\_influence”, “load”,
“flow\_betweenness”

\end{itemize}

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Path\sphinxhyphen{}based, advanced, and extended measures are computationally expensive for large
networks. Use flags or presets to control which measures are computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For disconnected multilayer graphs (e.g., networks without inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling,
or with isolated components), use closeness\_variant=’harmonic’ or ‘auto’ to
get mathematically consistent closeness values.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute only basic measures (fast)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{compute\PYGZus{}all\PYGZus{}centralities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use preset for standard analysis}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{compute\PYGZus{}all\PYGZus{}centralities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{preset}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{standard}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\pysigstartsignatures

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{supra\_matrix}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{spmatrix}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{alpha}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{beta}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tol}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1e\sphinxhyphen{}06}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Katz centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Katz centrality measures node influence by accounting for all paths with
exponentially decaying weights. It is computed as:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
x = (I \sphinxhyphen{} alpha * A)\textasciicircum{}\{\sphinxhyphen{}1\} * beta * 1
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where alpha \textless{} 1/lambda\_max(A) to ensure convergence. If alpha is not
provided, it defaults to 0.85 / lambda\_max(A).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{supra\_matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (n x n).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Attenuation parameter. Must be less than 1/spectral\_radius(A).
If None, defaults to 0.85 / lambda\_max(A).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{beta}} \textendash{} Weight of exogenous influence (typically 1.0).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for eigenvalue computation.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Katz centrality scores for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (n,).}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normalized to sum to 1.

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexMatrixError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexMatrixError}}}}} \textendash{} If matrix is invalid or alpha is out of valid range.

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{katz} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Katz centrality computed for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{katz}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} With custom alpha}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}custom} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.centrality_toolkit}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Built\sphinxhyphen{}in multilayer centrality toolkit.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Implements core multilayer variants of centrality measures:
\sphinxhyphen{} Multilayer PageRank
\sphinxhyphen{} Multilayer betweenness centrality
\sphinxhyphen{} Multilayer eigenvector centrality
\sphinxhyphen{} Multiplex degree centrality

\sphinxAtStartPar
These algorithms properly account for the multilayer structure of networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All centrality functions now support first\sphinxhyphen{}class uncertainty estimation via
the \sphinxtitleref{uncertainty} parameter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Authors: py3plex contributors
Date: 2025

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{weight}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute multilayer betweenness centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes betweenness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph, where shortest
paths can traverse multiple layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} Multilayer network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize by number of pairs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge attribute to use as weight (None for unweighted)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to betweenness scores

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Algorithm:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each pair of nodes (s,t), count the fraction of shortest
paths passing through each node v:

\sphinxAtStartPar
BC(v) = Σ\_\{s≠v≠t\} σ\_\{st\}(v) / σ\_\{st\}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where σ\_\{st\} is the number of shortest paths from s to t,
and σ\_\{st\}(v) is the number passing through v.

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico, M., et al. (2015). “Ranking in interconnected
multilayer networks reveals versatile nodes.”
Nature Communications, 6, 6868.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute multilayer eigenvector centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the principal eigenvector of the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix.
Nodes are important if connected to other important nodes across layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} Multilayer network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of power iteration steps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Convergence tolerance

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to eigenvector centrality scores

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Algorithm:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find the principal eigenvector of the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix:

\sphinxAtStartPar
A * x = λ * x

\sphinxAtStartPar
where x is the eigenvector with largest eigenvalue λ.

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Solá, L., et al. (2013). “Eigenvector centrality of nodes in
multiplex networks.” Chaos, 23(3), 033131.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{multilayer\_pagerank() (in module py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit)@\spxentry{multilayer\_pagerank()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_pagerank}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{alpha}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{0.85}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{max\_iter}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{100}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tol}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1e\sphinxhyphen{}06}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{personalization}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Dict\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{uncertainty}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{n\_runs}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{resampling}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.types.ResamplingStrategy}]{\sphinxcrossref{ResamplingStrategy}}}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{random\_seed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.types.StatSeries}]{\sphinxcrossref{StatSeries}}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute multilayer PageRank centrality with optional uncertainty estimation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Implements PageRank on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix, accounting for
random walks across layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} Multilayer network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Damping factor (teleportation probability = 1\sphinxhyphen{}alpha)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Convergence tolerance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{personalization}} \textendash{} Optional personalization vector (node \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} weight)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{uncertainty}} \textendash{} If True, estimate uncertainty via resampling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_runs}} \textendash{} Number of runs for uncertainty estimation (default from config)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resampling}} \textendash{} Resampling strategy (default from config)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
StatSeries with deterministic values (std=None)
If uncertainty=True: StatSeries with mean, std, quantiles

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If uncertainty=False

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Algorithm:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PR = (1\sphinxhyphen{}α)/N + α * A\textasciicircum{}T * PR

\sphinxAtStartPar
where A is the column\sphinxhyphen{}normalized supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Halu, A., et al. (2013). “Multiplex PageRank.”
PLoS ONE, 8(10), e78293.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute multiplex degree centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sums degree across all layers for each node. For multiplex networks
where nodes exist in all layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} Multiplex network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize by maximum possible degree

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{consider\_interlayer}} \textendash{} Whether to count inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to degree centrality scores

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Algorithm:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For node i:
DC(i) = Σ\_α k\_i\textasciicircum{}α

\sphinxAtStartPar
where k\_i\textasciicircum{}α is the degree of node i in layer α.

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Battiston, F., et al. (2014). “Structural measures for
multiplex networks.” Physical Review E, 89(3), 032804.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{versatility\_score() (in module py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit)@\spxentry{versatility\_score()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.centrality_toolkit.versatility_score}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.centrality\_toolkit.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{versatility\_score}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{centrality\_dict}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute versatility score for each node.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures how evenly a node’s centrality is distributed across layers.
High versatility means the node is important in multiple layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{centrality\_dict}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping (node, layer) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} centrality score

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize to {[}0, 1{]}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping node\_id \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} versatility score

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Algorithm:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
V(i) = 1 \sphinxhyphen{} Σ\_α (c\_i\textasciicircum{}α / c\_i\textasciicircum{}total)\textasciicircum{}2

\sphinxAtStartPar
where c\_i\textasciicircum{}α is centrality of node i in layer α.
This is similar to the Herfindahl\sphinxhyphen{}Hirschman index.

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Battiston, F., et al. (2014). “Structural measures for
multiplex networks.” Physical Review E, 89(3), 032804.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.multixrank@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.multixrank}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.multixrank@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.multixrank}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.multixrank}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
MultiXRank: Random Walk with Restart on Universal Multilayer Networks

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements the MultiXRank algorithm described in:
Baptista et al. (2022), “Universal multilayer network exploration by random walk
with restart”, Communications Physics, 5, 170.

\sphinxAtStartPar
MultiXRank performs random walk with restart (RWR) on a supra\sphinxhyphen{}heterogeneous
adjacency matrix built from multiple multiplexes connected by bipartite blocks.
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Paper: \sphinxurl{https://doi.org/10.1038/s42005-022-00937-9}

\item {}

arXiv: \sphinxurl{https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.07869}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Package: \sphinxurl{https://github.com/anthbapt/multixrank}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Docs: \sphinxurl{https://multixrank-doc.readthedocs.io/}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
MultiXRank: Universal multilayer network exploration by random walk with restart.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This class implements the MultiXRank algorithm for node prioritization and
ranking in universal multilayer networks. It builds a supra\sphinxhyphen{}heterogeneous
adjacency matrix from multiple multiplexes and bipartite inter\sphinxhyphen{}multiplex
connections, then performs random walk with restart.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Build the supra\sphinxhyphen{}heterogeneous adjacency matrix S.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This constructs the universal multilayer network matrix by:
1. Placing each multiplex supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency on the block diagonal
2. Adding bipartite blocks for inter\sphinxhyphen{}multiplex connections
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{block\_weights}} \textendash{} Optional dictionary to weight blocks. Keys can be:
\sphinxhyphen{} Multiplex names (to weight within\sphinxhyphen{}multiplex edges)
\sphinxhyphen{} Tuple (multiplex\_from, multiplex\_to) for bipartite blocks

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The supra\sphinxhyphen{}heterogeneous adjacency matrix

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxhyphen{} ‘uniform’: Distribute mass uniformly across all nodes
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘self’: Add self\sphinxhyphen{}loop (mass stays at the node)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘ignore’: Leave as zero (not recommended for RWR)

Column\sphinxhyphen{}stochastic transition matrix

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.supra_matrix_function_centrality}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supra Matrix Function Centralities for Multilayer Networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements centrality measures based on matrix functions of the
supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix, including:
\sphinxhyphen{} Communicability Centrality (Estrada \& Hatano, 2008)
\sphinxhyphen{} Katz Centrality (Katz, 1953)

\sphinxAtStartPar
These measures operate directly on the sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix obtained
from multi\_layer\_network.get\_supra\_adjacency\_matrix().
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Estrada, E., \& Hatano, N. (2008). Communicability in complex networks.
Physical Review E, 77(3), 036111.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Katz, L. (1953). A new status index derived from sociometric analysis.
Psychometrika, 18(1), 39\sphinxhyphen{}43.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Authors: py3plex contributors

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute communicability centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Communicability centrality measures the weighted sum of all walks between
nodes, with exponentially decaying weights for longer walks. It is computed
as the row sum of the matrix exponential:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_i = sum\_j (exp(A))\_ij
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation uses scipy.sparse.linalg.expm\_multiply for efficient
sparse matrix exponential computation.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{supra\_matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (n x n).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalize}} \textendash{} If True, normalize output to sum to 1.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{use\_sparse}} \textendash{} If True, use sparse matrix operations. Falls back to dense
for matrices smaller than 10000 elements.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations for sparse approximation (currently unused).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for convergence (currently unused).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Communicability centrality scores for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (n,).

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexMatrixError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexMatrixError}}}}} \textendash{} If matrix is invalid (non\sphinxhyphen{}square, empty, etc.).

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{comm} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{communicability\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Communicability centrality computed for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{supra\_matrix}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{spmatrix}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{alpha}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{beta}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tol}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1e\sphinxhyphen{}06}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Katz centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Katz centrality measures node influence by accounting for all paths with
exponentially decaying weights. It is computed as:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
x = (I \sphinxhyphen{} alpha * A)\textasciicircum{}\{\sphinxhyphen{}1\} * beta * 1
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where alpha \textless{} 1/lambda\_max(A) to ensure convergence. If alpha is not
provided, it defaults to 0.85 / lambda\_max(A).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{supra\_matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (n x n).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Attenuation parameter. Must be less than 1/spectral\_radius(A).
If None, defaults to 0.85 / lambda\_max(A).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{beta}} \textendash{} Weight of exogenous influence (typically 1.0).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for eigenvalue computation.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Katz centrality scores for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (n,).}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normalized to sum to 1.

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexMatrixError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexMatrixError}}}}} \textendash{} If matrix is invalid or alpha is out of valid range.

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{katz} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Katz centrality computed for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{katz}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} With custom alpha}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}custom} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplex Participation Coefficient (MPC) for multiplex networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements the Multiplex Participation Coefficient metric for
multiplex networks (networks with identical node sets across all layers).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Authors: py3plex contributors
Date: 2025

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality.multiplex_participation_coefficient}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multiplex\_participation\_coefficient}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{multinet}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{check\_multiplex}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the Multiplex Participation Coefficient (MPC) for multiplex networks.
MPC measures how evenly a node participates across layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multinet}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} Multiplex network object (same node set across layers).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Whether to normalize MPC to {[}0,1{]}. Default: True.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{check\_multiplex}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Validate that all layers share the same node set.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node \(\rightarrow\) MPC value mapping.

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{The MPC is computed as:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
MPC(i) = 1 \sphinxhyphen{} sum\_α (k\_i\textasciicircum{}α / k\_i\textasciicircum{}total)\textasciicircum{}2

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Where:
\sphinxhyphen{} k\_i\textasciicircum{}α is the degree of node i in layer α
\sphinxhyphen{} k\_i\textasciicircum{}total is the total degree of node i across all layers

\sphinxAtStartPar
When normalized=True, the result is multiplied by L/(L\sphinxhyphen{}1) to normalize
to {[}0,1{]} range, where L is the number of layers.
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Battiston, F., et al. (2014). “Structural measures for multiplex networks.”
Physical Review E, 89(3), 032804.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico, M., et al. (2015). “Identifying modular flows on multilayer networks
reveals highly overlapping organization in interconnected systems.”
Physical Review X, 5(1), 011027.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Harooni, M., et al. (2025). “Centrality in Multilayer Networks: Accurate
Measurements with MultiNetPy.” The Journal of Supercomputing, 81(1), 92.
DOI: 10.1007/s11227\sphinxhyphen{}025\sphinxhyphen{}07197\sphinxhyphen{}8

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Contracts:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: multinet must not be None

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: normalized and check\_multiplex must be booleans

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: returns a dictionary with numeric values

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\paragraph{General Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:general-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
General\sphinxhyphen{}purpose algorithms such as random walkers and benchmarking helpers.
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk primitives for graph\sphinxhyphen{}based algorithms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides foundation for higher\sphinxhyphen{}level algorithms like Node2Vec,
DeepWalk, and diffusion processes. Implements both basic and second\sphinxhyphen{}order
(biased) random walks with proper edge weight handling and multilayer support.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Key Features:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Basic random walks with weighted edge sampling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Second\sphinxhyphen{}order (Node2Vec\sphinxhyphen{}style) biased random walks with p/q parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple simultaneous walks with deterministic reproducibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Support for directed, weighted, and multilayer networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Efficient sparse adjacency handling

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grover, A., \& Leskovec, J. (2016). node2vec: Scalable feature learning for networks.
KDD ‘16. \sphinxurl{https://doi.org/10.1145/2939672.2939754}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perozzi, B., Al\sphinxhyphen{}Rfou, R., \& Skiena, S. (2014). DeepWalk: Online learning of social
representations. KDD ‘14. \sphinxurl{https://doi.org/10.1145/2623330.2623732}

\end{itemize}

{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{basic\_random\_walk}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{G}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Graph}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{start\_node}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{walk\_length}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{weighted}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{seed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform a basic random walk on a graph with proper edge weight handling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next step is sampled proportionally to the normalized edge weights
of the current node. For unweighted graphs, transitions are uniform.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph (directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start\_node}} \textendash{} Node to start the walk from

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{walk\_length}} \textendash{} Number of steps in the walk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weighted}} \textendash{} Whether to use edge weights (default: True)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility (default: None)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of nodes representing the walk path (includes start\_node)

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If start\_node not in graph or walk\_length \textless{} 1

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
