\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform random walk with layer constraints for multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In a multilayer network represented in py3plex format (where node names
include layer information), this function can constrain walks to specific
layers with occasional inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer transitions.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph (multilayer network in py3plex format)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start\_node}} \textendash{} Node to start walk from (may include layer info)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{walk\_length}} \textendash{} Number of steps in the walk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer}} \textendash{} Target layer to constrain walk to (None = no constraint)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{cross\_layer\_prob}} \textendash{} Probability of crossing to different layer (0\sphinxhyphen{}1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weighted}} \textendash{} Whether to use edge weights

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of nodes representing the walk path

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer network with layer\PYGZhy{}specific walks}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{biological}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... add nodes and edges ...}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{walk} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}specific\PYGZus{}random\PYGZus{}walk}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nodeA\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{cross\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}prob}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{node2vec\_walk}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{G}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Graph}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{start\_node}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{walk\_length}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{p}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{q}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{weighted}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{seed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ List\DUrole{p}{{[}}int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }str\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform a second\sphinxhyphen{}order (biased) random walk following Node2Vec logic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When transitioning from node t \(\rightarrow\) v \(\rightarrow\) x, the probability of choosing x
is biased by parameters p (return) and q (in\sphinxhyphen{}out):
\sphinxhyphen{} If x == t (return to previous): weight / p
\sphinxhyphen{} If x is neighbor of t (stay close): weight / 1
\sphinxhyphen{} If x is not neighbor of t (explore): weight / q
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph (directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start\_node}} \textendash{} Node to start the walk from

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{walk\_length}} \textendash{} Number of steps in the walk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Return parameter (higher p = less likely to return to previous node)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{q}} \textendash{} In\sphinxhyphen{}out parameter (higher q = less likely to explore further)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weighted}} \textendash{} Whether to use edge weights (default: True)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility (default: None)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of nodes representing the walk path (includes start\_node)

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If p \textless{}= 0 or q \textless{}= 0 or start\_node not in graph

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

predictions for each sample, where k is determined by the ground truth
number of labels.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
micro: Micro\sphinxhyphen{}averaged F1 score

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw edges connecting multiple layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws curved or straight edges that connect nodes across different layers
in a multilayer network visualization. Typically used after draw\_multilayer\_default
to add inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network\_list}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs (layers) or dict of layer\_name \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multi\_edge\_tuple}} \textendash{} List of tuples specifying edges to draw, e.g. {[}(node1, node2), …{]}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Type of input (“nodes” or other)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{linepoints}} \textendash{} Line style (e.g., “\sphinxhyphen{}.”, “\textendash{}”, “\sphinxhyphen{}“)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alphachannel}} \textendash{} Transparency level (0.0 to 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{linecolor}} \textendash{} Color of the lines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{curve\_height}} \textendash{} Height of curved edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{style}} \textendash{} Style of edges (“curve2\_bezier”, “line”, “curve3\_bezier”, “curve3\_fit”, “piramidal”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{linewidth}} \textendash{} Width of lines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{invert}} \textendash{} Whether to invert drawing direction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{linmod}} \textendash{} Line modification mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resolution}} \textendash{} Resolution for curve drawing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} \textendash{} Matplotlib Axes to draw on. If None, uses current axes (plt.gca())

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matplotlib Axes object containing the visualization.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Core multilayer drawing method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a diagonal multilayer network visualization where each layer is
offset to create a 3D\sphinxhyphen{}like effect. Nodes within each layer are drawn
with their positions, and background shapes indicate layer boundaries.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network\_list}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs to visualize (or dict of layer\_name \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} graph)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{display}} \textendash{} If True, calls plt.show() after drawing. Default is False
to let the caller control rendering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size}} \textendash{} Base size of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alphalevel}} \textendash{} Transparency level for background shapes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rectanglex}} \textendash{} Width of rectangular backgrounds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rectangley}} \textendash{} Height of rectangular backgrounds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{background\_shape}} \textendash{} Background shape type (“circle” or “rectangle”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{background\_color}} \textendash{} Background color scheme (“default”, “rainbow”, or None)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{networks\_color}} \textendash{} Network color scheme (“rainbow” or “black”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{labels}} \textendash{} Layer labels to display

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{arrowsize}} \textendash{} Size of edge arrows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{label\_position}} \textendash{} Position offset for layer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Whether to log network information

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{remove\_isolated\_nodes}} \textendash{} Whether to remove isolated nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} \textendash{} Matplotlib Axes to draw on. If None, uses current axes (plt.gca())

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_size}} \textendash{} Width of edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_labels}} \textendash{} Whether to display node labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_font\_size}} \textendash{} Font size for node labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{scale\_by\_size}} \textendash{} Whether to scale node size by degree

\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw multilayer network as layered flow visualization (alluvial\sphinxhyphen{}style).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shows each layer as a horizontal band with nodes positioned along the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis.
Intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer activity is encoded as node color/size, and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges are
shown as thick flow ribbons (Bezier curves) where width encodes edge weight.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graphs}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs, one per layer (from multi\_layer\_network.get\_layers())

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multilinks}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping edge\_type \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} list of multi\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{labels}} \textendash{} Optional list of layer labels. If None, uses layer indices

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_activity}} \textendash{} Optional dict mapping node\_id \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} activity value.
If None, computes intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer degree

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} \textendash{} Matplotlib axes to draw on. If None, creates new figure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{display}} \textendash{} If True, calls plt.show() at the end

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_gap}} \textendash{} Vertical distance between layer bands

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size}} \textendash{} Base marker size for nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_cmap}} \textendash{} Matplotlib colormap name for node activity coloring

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{flow\_alpha}} \textendash{} Base transparency for flow ribbons

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{flow\_min\_width}} \textendash{} Minimum line width for flows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{flow\_max\_width}} \textendash{} Maximum line width for flows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{aggregate\_by}} \textendash{} Tuple of keys for aggregating flows (currently not used, for future extension)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Reserved for future extensions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matplotlib axes object

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw a force\sphinxhyphen{}directed “hairball” visualization of a network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates a force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layout visualization where nodes are colored by
type/layer and sized by degree. This is a common visualization for showing
the overall structure of a network.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{g}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph to visualize

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{color\_list}} \textendash{} List of colors for nodes. If None, colors are assigned
based on node types.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{display}} \textendash{} If True, calls plt.show() after drawing. Default is False
to let the caller control rendering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size}} \textendash{} Base size of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{text\_color}} \textendash{} Color for node labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_sizes}} \textendash{} Custom list of node sizes (overrides node\_size and scale\_by\_size)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_parameters}} \textendash{} Parameters for the layout algorithm (e.g., \{“pos”: \{…\}\})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{legend}} \textendash{} If True, display a legend mapping colors to node types

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{scale\_by\_size}} \textendash{} If True, scale node sizes by log(degree)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_algorithm}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} “force”: Force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layout (spring layout)
\sphinxhyphen{} “random”: Random layout
\sphinxhyphen{} “custom\_coordinates”: Use positions from layout\_parameters{[}“pos”{]}
\sphinxhyphen{} “custom\_coordinates\_initial\_force”: Use custom positions as initial layout

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_width}} \textendash{} Width of edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha\_channel}} \textendash{} Transparency level (0.0 to 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{labels}} \textendash{} List of node labels to display (None for no labels)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{draw}} \textendash{} If True, draw the network. If False, only compute layout and return data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{label\_font\_size}} \textendash{} Font size for node labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} \textendash{} Matplotlib Axes to draw on. If None, uses current axes (plt.gca())

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{skip\_layout}} \textendash{} If True, skip all layout computation and visualization, returning immediately.
This is useful for examples that only need to test the API without actually rendering
or when you want to avoid expensive force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layout calculations.
When True, returns None immediately. Default is False.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create an interactive 2.5D diagonal multilayer plot using Plotly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function creates an interactive version of the diagonal multilayer
visualization, mimicking the traditional 2D diagonal layout but in an
interactive 3D environment. Each layer is positioned diagonally with
clear visual separation, similar to the static diagonal visualization.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network\_list}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs (layers) or dict of layer\_name \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_labels}} \textendash{} Optional labels for each layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_algorithm}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm for nodes (“force”, “circular”, “random”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_gap}} \textendash{} Distance between layers in diagonal direction (default: 2.5)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size\_base}} \textendash{} Base size for nodes (default: 8)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_colors}} \textendash{} Optional list of colors for each layer (HTML color names or hex)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{show\_interlayer\_edges}} \textendash{} Whether to show inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{interlayer\_edges}} \textendash{} List of tuples (node1, node2) for inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections

\end{itemize}

False if plotly not available, otherwise plotly figure object

Visualizes the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix of a multilayer network, where the
matrix shows both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections. The matrix is
displayed as a heatmap with configurable colormap.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

to let the caller control rendering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}level function to visualize multilayer networks with multiple visualization modes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function provides a unified interface for various multilayer network visualization
techniques, making it easy to switch between different visual representations.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_network}} \textendash{} A MultiLayerNetwork instance from py3plex.core.multinet

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{visualization\_type}} \textendash{} Type of visualization to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} “diagonal”: Default layer\sphinxhyphen{}centric diagonal layout (existing behavior)
\sphinxhyphen{} “small\_multiples”: One subplot per layer with shared or independent layouts
\sphinxhyphen{} “edge\_colored\_projection”: Aggregate projection with edge colors by layer
\sphinxhyphen{} “supra\_adjacency\_heatmap”: Matrix representation of multilayer structure
\sphinxhyphen{} “radial\_layers”: Concentric circles for layers with radial inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges
\sphinxhyphen{} “ego\_multilayer”: Ego\sphinxhyphen{}centric view focused on a specific node

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional keyword arguments specific to each visualization type.
See individual plot functions for details.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The created figure object

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
matplotlib.figure.Figure

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If visualization\_type is not recognized

\end{description}\end{quote}

This function has the same name as pylab.draw and pyplot.draw
so beware when using

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{o}{*}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
since you might overwrite the pylab.draw function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With pyplot use

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{draw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} networkx draw()}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{draw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pyplot draw()}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

turned off with keyword arrows=False. Be sure to include \sphinxtitleref{node\_size} as a
keyword argument; arrows are drawn considering the size of nodes.

Draw the nodes of the graph G.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This draws only the nodes of the graph G.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{graph}}) \textendash{} A networkx graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{pos}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dictionary}}) \textendash{} A dictionary with nodes as keys and positions as values.
Positions should be sequences of length 2.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{Matplotlib Axes object}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Draw the graph in the specified Matplotlib axes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{nodelist}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{list}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Draw only specified nodes (default G.nodes())

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{scalar}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ or }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{array}}) \textendash{} Size of nodes (default=300).  If an array is specified it must be the
same length as nodelist.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_color}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{color string}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, or }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{array}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ of }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{floats}}) \textendash{} Node color. Can be a single color format string (default=’r’),
or a  sequence of colors with the same length as nodelist.
If numeric values are specified they will be mapped to
colors using the cmap and vmin,vmax parameters.  See
matplotlib.scatter for more details.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_shape}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The shape of the node.  Specification is as matplotlib.scatter
marker, one of ‘so\textasciicircum{}\textgreater{}v\textless{}dph8’ (default=’o’).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ or }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{array}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ of }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{floats}}) \textendash{} The node transparency.  This can be a single alpha value (default=1.0),
in which case it will be applied to all the nodes of color. Otherwise,
if it is an array, the elements of alpha will be applied to the colors
in order (cycling through alpha multiple times if necessary).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{cmap}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{Matplotlib colormap}}) \textendash{} Colormap for mapping intensities of nodes (default=None)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{vmin}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{floats}}) \textendash{} Minimum and maximum for node colormap scaling (default=None)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{vmax}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{floats}}) \textendash{} Minimum and maximum for node colormap scaling (default=None)

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edgecolors}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{{[}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{None}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ | }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{scalar}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ | }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{sequence}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{{]}}}) \textendash{} Colors of node borders (default = node\_color)

Compute force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layout for a graph using ForceAtlas2 or NetworkX spring layout.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{g}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph to layout

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_parameters}} \textendash{} Optional parameters to pass to layout algorithm

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Whether to print progress information

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gravity}} \textendash{} Attraction force towards the center (must be non\sphinxhyphen{}negative)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{strongGravityMode}} \textendash{} Use strong gravity mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{barnesHutTheta}} \textendash{} Barnes\sphinxhyphen{}Hut approximation parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edgeWeightInfluence}} \textendash{} Influence of edge weights on layout

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{scalingRatio}} \textendash{} Scaling factor for the layout (must be positive)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{forceImport}} \textendash{} Whether to use ForceAtlas2 (if available)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility in fallback spring layout

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping nodes to 2D position arrays

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks (\textgreater{}1000 nodes), this may be slow. Consider using
faster layouts (circular, random, spectral) or matrix visualization.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Contracts:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: graph must not be None and be a NetworkX graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: graph must have at least one node

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: gravity must be non\sphinxhyphen{}negative

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: scalingRatio must be positive

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: result is a dictionary

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: result has positions for all nodes

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\subsubsection{Aggregation and Network Operations}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:aggregation-and-network-operations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer aggregation and network\sphinxhyphen{}level transformations.
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.multinet.aggregation@\spxentry{py3plex.multinet.aggregation}}\index{py3plex.multinet.aggregation@\spxentry{py3plex.multinet.aggregation}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.multinet.aggregation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Vectorized multiplex aggregation for multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides optimized implementations for aggregating edges across
multiple layers using vectorized NumPy and SciPy sparse operations, replacing
slower Python loops with efficient matrix operations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Performance targets:
\sphinxhyphen{} ≥3× speedup for 1M edges across 4 layers compared to legacy loop\sphinxhyphen{}based methods
\sphinxhyphen{} Memory\sphinxhyphen{}efficient sparse matrix output by default
\sphinxhyphen{} Float tolerance of 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 for numerical equivalence with legacy methods

\sphinxAtStartPar
Author: py3plex development team
License: MIT

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregate edge weights across multiple layers using vectorized operations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function replaces Python loops with efficient NumPy and SciPy sparse
matrix operations for superior performance on large multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complexity}: O(E) where E is the number of edges
\sphinxstylestrong{Memory}: O(E) for sparse output, O(N\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) for dense output
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edges}} \textendash{} Edge data as ndarray with shape (E, \textgreater{}=3) containing
(layer, src, dst, {[}weight{]}) columns. If no weight column,
assumes weight=1.0 for all edges. Can also accept list of lists.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight\_col}} \textendash{} Column name or index for weights (default “w”).
If edges is ndarray, must be int index (0\sphinxhyphen{}based).
Column 3 is used if it exists, else weights default to 1.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{reducer}} \textendash{} Aggregation method \sphinxhyphen{} one of:
\sphinxhyphen{} “sum”: Sum weights for edges appearing in multiple layers (default)
\sphinxhyphen{} “mean”: Average weights across layers
\sphinxhyphen{} “max”: Take maximum weight across layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{to\_sparse}} \textendash{} If True, return scipy.sparse.csr\_matrix (default, memory\sphinxhyphen{}efficient).
If False, return dense numpy.ndarray.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregated adjacency matrix in requested format (sparse CSR or dense).
Shape is (N, N) where N is the maximum node ID + 1.

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If edges array has wrong shape or reducer is invalid.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{TypeError}} \textendash{} If edges is not ndarray or list\sphinxhyphen{}like.

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Same edge in layer 1}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{mat}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{shape}
\PYG{g+go}{(4, 4)}

\PYG{g+go}{1.5}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} With mean aggregation}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{mat\PYGZus{}mean} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{aggregate\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reducer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{mat\PYGZus{}mean}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Average of 1.0 and 0.5}
\PYG{g+go}{0.75}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node IDs are assumed to be integers starting from 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}loops are supported

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For directed graphs, (i,j) and (j,i) are different edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sparse output recommended for large networks (N \textgreater{} 1000)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Deterministic output for fixed input order

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Performance:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Achieves ≥3× speedup vs loop\sphinxhyphen{}based aggregation on 1M edges:
\sphinxhyphen{} Legacy loop: \textasciitilde{}2.5s for 1M edges, 4 layers
\sphinxhyphen{} Vectorized: \textasciitilde{}0.8s for same dataset (measured on standard hardware)

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\subsubsection{Profiling Utilities}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:profiling-utilities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Timing and profiling utilities for performance analysis.
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.profiling@\spxentry{py3plex.profiling}}\index{py3plex.profiling@\spxentry{py3plex.profiling}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.profiling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Performance profiling utilities for py3plex.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides decorators and utilities for tracking function execution time,
memory usage, and performance metrics. These tools enable performance regression
detection and optimization efforts.
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{profiling}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{profile\PYGZus{}performance}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nd}{@profile\PYGZus{}performance}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{slow\PYGZus{}function}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... computation}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{k}{pass}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{slow\PYGZus{}function}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Logs execution time automatically}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

Benchmark a function with multiple iterations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Runs the function multiple times and collects statistics about execution time.
Includes a warmup phase to allow JIT compilation and caching.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{func}} \textendash{} Function to benchmark

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of iterations to run (default: 100)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{warmup}} \textendash{} Number of warmup iterations (default: 10)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{args}} \textendash{} Positional arguments for the function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{kwargs}} \textendash{} Keyword arguments for the function

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mean: Average execution time (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
median: Median execution time (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
min: Minimum execution time (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max: Maximum execution time (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
std: Standard deviation (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total: Total time for all iterations (seconds)

\end{itemize}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary containing benchmark statistics

\end{description}\end{quote}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decorator to track function execution time and optionally memory usage.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This decorator measures the wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock time taken by a function and logs it.
It can also track memory usage changes if requested. Performance metrics
are stored in the global performance monitor for later analysis.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{func}} \textendash{} Function to decorate (when used without arguments)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{log\_args}} \textendash{} If True, log function arguments (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{track\_memory}} \textendash{} If True, track memory usage (default: False)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decorated function that logs execution time

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Basic usage:
\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} @profile\_performance
… def my\_function(x, y):
…     return x + y

\sphinxAtStartPar
With options:
\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} @profile\_performance(log\_args=True, track\_memory=True)
… def expensive\_function(data):
…     \# … expensive computation
…     return result

\sphinxAtStartPar
Manual wrapping:
\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} def my\_function():
…     pass
\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} profiled\_func = profile\_performance(my\_function)

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Memory tracking requires the tracemalloc module and adds overhead.
Use it only when investigating memory issues.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{heaviside() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests)@\spxentry{heaviside()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests.heaviside}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{heaviside}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{X}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the Heaviside step function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Heaviside function returns 1 for positive values, 0.5 for zero, and 0 for
negative values. This is used in signed\sphinxhyphen{}rank tests for Bayesian comparisons.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{X}} \textendash{} Input array or scalar

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Array with same shape as X containing:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1.0 where X \textgreater{} 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0.5 where X == 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0.0 where X \textless{} 0

\end{itemize}

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{heaviside}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{array([0. , 0.5, 1. , 1. ])}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{hierarchical() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests)@\spxentry{hierarchical()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests.hierarchical}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{hierarchical}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{diff}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{rope}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{rho}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{upperAlpha}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{2}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{lowerAlpha}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{lowerBeta}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.01}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{upperBeta}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{std\_upper\_bound}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{1000}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{verbose}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{names}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{(\textquotesingle{}C1\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}C2\textquotesingle{})}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform hierarchical Bayesian test for comparing algorithms across multiple datasets.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This test accounts for the hierarchical structure of the data (multiple datasets,
each with multiple folds) and correlations due to overlapping training sets.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{diff}} \textendash{} Array of differences between classifier scores

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rope}} \textendash{} Width of the region of practical equivalence (ROPE)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rho}} \textendash{} Correlation between folds (typically around 1/n\_folds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{upperAlpha}} \textendash{} Upper bound for alpha parameter of Gamma prior (default: 2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lowerAlpha}} \textendash{} Lower bound for alpha parameter of Gamma prior (default: 1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lowerBeta}} \textendash{} Lower bound for beta parameter of Gamma prior (default: 0.01)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{upperBeta}} \textendash{} Upper bound for beta parameter of Gamma prior (default: 0.1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{std\_upper\_bound}} \textendash{} Upper bound multiplier for standard deviation prior (default: 1000)
Posterior is insensitive to this if large enough (\textgreater{}100)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Whether to print probability results (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{names}} \textendash{} Tuple of classifier names for verbose output (default: (“C1”, “C2”))

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{(p\_left, p\_rope, p\_right)}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
p\_left: Probability that first classifier is worse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
p\_rope: Probability that classifiers are practically equivalent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
p\_right: Probability that first classifier is better

\end{itemize}

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple{[}float, float, float{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Gamma distribution parameters control the prior on degrees of freedom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The hierarchical structure models between\sphinxhyphen{}dataset and within\sphinxhyphen{}dataset variance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use when comparing algorithms across multiple datasets with cross\sphinxhyphen{}validation

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Benavoli, A., Corani, G., \& Mangili, F. (2016). Should we really use
post\sphinxhyphen{}hoc tests based on mean\sphinxhyphen{}ranks? The Journal of Machine Learning Research.

\end{itemize}


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
hierarchical\_MC: Monte Carlo sampling version
correlated\_ttest: Simpler test for single dataset comparisons


\end{sphinxseealso}


\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{hierarchical\_MC() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests)@\spxentry{hierarchical\_MC()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests.hierarchical_MC}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.bayesiantests.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{hierarchical\_MC}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{diff}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{rope}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{rho}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{upperAlpha}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{2}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{lowerAlpha}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{lowerBeta}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.01}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{upperBeta}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{std\_upper\_bound}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{1000}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{names}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{(\textquotesingle{}C1\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}C2\textquotesingle{})}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Monte Carlo sampling for hierarchical Bayesian test.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Generates Monte Carlo samples from the posterior distribution for hierarchical
comparison of algorithms across multiple datasets with cross\sphinxhyphen{}validation.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{diff}} \textendash{} Array of differences between classifier scores (shape: n\_datasets x n\_folds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rope}} \textendash{} Width of the region of practical equivalence (ROPE)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rho}} \textendash{} Correlation between folds due to overlapping training sets

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{upperAlpha}} \textendash{} Upper bound for alpha parameter of Gamma prior (default: 2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lowerAlpha}} \textendash{} Lower bound for alpha parameter of Gamma prior (default: 1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lowerBeta}} \textendash{} Lower bound for beta parameter of Gamma prior (default: 0.01)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{upperBeta}} \textendash{} Upper bound for beta parameter of Gamma prior (default: 0.1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{std\_upper\_bound}} \textendash{} Upper bound multiplier for standard deviation prior (default: 1000)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{names}} \textendash{} Tuple of classifier names for identification (default: (“C1”, “C2”))

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Monte Carlo samples with shape (n\_samples, 3)}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each row contains {[}p\_left, p\_rope, p\_right{]} for one MC sample

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses PyStan for Bayesian inference with hierarchical model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Data is rescaled by mean standard deviation for numerical stability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hierarchical structure captures both within\sphinxhyphen{}dataset and between\sphinxhyphen{}dataset variance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires pystan package to be installed

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Implementation:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses Stan’s NUTS sampler with 4 chains

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each chain runs 100 iterations (including warmup)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Total posterior samples: \textasciitilde{}200 after warmup

\end{itemize}

\end{description}


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
hierarchical: Main function that processes MC samples
correlated\_ttest\_MC: Simpler MC version for single dataset


\end{sphinxseealso}

\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ImportError}} \textendash{} If pystan is not installed

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\subsubsection{Node Ranking and Classification}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:node-ranking-and-classification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combined node ranking and classification utilities.
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.node\_ranking@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.node\_ranking}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.node\_ranking@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.node\_ranking}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.node_ranking}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node ranking algorithms for multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides various node ranking algorithms including PageRank variants,
HITS (Hubs and Authorities), and personalized PageRank (PPR) for network analysis.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Key Functions:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sparse\_page\_rank: Compute PageRank scores using sparse matrix operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
run\_PPR: Run Personalized PageRank in parallel across multiple cores

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hubs\_and\_authorities: Compute HITS scores for nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stochastic\_normalization: Normalize adjacency matrix to stochastic form

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The PageRank implementations use sparse matrices for memory efficiency and
support parallel computation for large\sphinxhyphen{}scale networks.
\index{authority\_matrix() (in module py3plex.algorithms.node\_ranking)@\spxentry{authority\_matrix()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.node\_ranking}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.node_ranking.authority_matrix}}

{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get the authority matrix representation of a graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the matrix A = A.T @ A where A is the adjacency matrix.
The authority matrix is used in HITS algorithm computation.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Authority matrix (N x N) where N is number of nodes

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For directed graphs: A{[}i,j{]} = number of nodes that point to both i and j

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Used internally by HITS algorithm to compute authority scores

\end{itemize}


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
hub\_matrix: Complementary hub matrix
hubs\_and\_authorities: Compute actual hub/authority scores


\end{sphinxseealso}


\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute HITS (Hubs and Authorities) scores for all nodes in a graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Implements the Hyperlink\sphinxhyphen{}Induced Topic Search (HITS) algorithm to identify
hub nodes (nodes that point to many authorities) and authority nodes (nodes
pointed to by many hubs) in a network.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph (directed or undirected)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}

\sphinxAtStartPar
authority\_scores: Dictionary mapping node \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} authority score

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses scipy\sphinxhyphen{}based implementation from NetworkX (nx.hits\_scipy)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Converges using power iteration method

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run Personalized PageRank (PPR) in parallel for multiple starting nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes personalized PageRank vectors for multiple nodes using parallel processing.
This is useful for creating node embeddings or analyzing node importance from
different perspectives in the network.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} Sparse adjacency matrix (will be automatically normalized to stochastic form)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{cores}} \textendash{} Number of CPU cores to use (default: all available cores)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{jobs}} \textendash{} Custom job batches as list of ranges (default: auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{damping}} \textendash{} Damping factor for PageRank (default: 0.85)
Higher values (0.85\sphinxhyphen{}0.99) emphasize network structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{spread\_step}} \textendash{} Steps to check spread pattern for optimization (default: 10)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{spread\_percent}} \textendash{} Max node fraction for shrinkage optimization (default: 0.3)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{targets}} \textendash{} Specific node indices to compute PPR for (default: all nodes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{parallel}} \textendash{} Enable parallel processing (default: True)
Set to False for debugging or single\sphinxhyphen{}core execution

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Yields}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Union{[}Tuple{[}int, np.ndarray{]}, List{[}Tuple{[}int, np.ndarray{]}{]}{]}} \textendash{}     \sphinxhyphen{} If parallel=True: Lists of (node\_index, pagerank\_vector) tuples (batched)
\sphinxhyphen{} If parallel=False: Individual (node\_index, pagerank\_vector) tuples

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically normalizes input matrix to column\sphinxhyphen{}stochastic form

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses multiprocessing.Pool for parallel execution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Global variables are used to share the graph matrix across processes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Results are yielded incrementally (generator pattern) to save memory

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each pagerank\_vector is L2\sphinxhyphen{}normalized for comparability

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{scipy}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{sparse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{sp}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a small network}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{csr\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute PPR for all nodes in parallel}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{batch} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{run\PYGZus{}PPR}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{adj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{cores}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{parallel}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{pr\PYGZus{}vector} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{batch}\PYG{p}{:}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute PPR for specific nodes without parallelism}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{pr\PYGZus{}vector} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{run\PYGZus{}PPR}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{adj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{targets}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{parallel}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Node }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{pr\PYGZus{}vector}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Performance:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parallel speedup scales with number of cores (up to \textasciitilde{}0.8 * cores efficiency)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Memory usage: O(N * N\_targets) for storing results

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks (\textgreater{}100K nodes), consider processing targets in batches

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute personalized PageRank using sparse matrix operations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Implements an efficient personalized PageRank algorithm with adaptive sparsification
to reduce memory usage and computation time. The algorithm uses a power iteration
method with early stopping based on convergence criteria.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{matrix}} \textendash{} Column\sphinxhyphen{}stochastic sparse adjacency matrix (use stochastic\_normalization first)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start\_nodes}} \textendash{} List or range of starting nodes for personalized PageRank

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{epsilon}} \textendash{} Convergence threshold for L1 norm difference (default: 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_steps}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations (default: 100000)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{damping}} \textendash{} Damping factor / teleportation probability (default: 0.5)
Higher values (e.g., 0.85) favor network structure over random jumps

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{spread\_step}} \textendash{} Number of steps to check for sparsity pattern (default: 10)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{spread\_percent}} \textendash{} Maximum fraction of nodes to consider for shrinkage (default: 0.3)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{try\_shrink}} \textendash{} Enable adaptive shrinkage to reduce computation (default: True)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PageRank scores for all nodes, with start\_nodes set to 0

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assumes matrix is column\sphinxhyphen{}stochastic (use stochastic\_normalization first)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adaptive shrinkage identifies nodes unreachable from start\_nodes and
excludes them from computation for efficiency

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convergence is measured by L1 norm of rank vector difference

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Start nodes are zeroed out in the final result to avoid self\sphinxhyphen{}importance

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Complexity:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Time: O(k * E) where k is iterations and E is edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Space: O(N) for rank vectors, plus matrix storage

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{scipy}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{sparse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{sp}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create and normalize adjacency matrix}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sp}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{csr\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}norm} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{stochastic\PYGZus{}normalization}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{adj}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute PageRank from node 0}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{pr} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sparse\PYGZus{}page\PYGZus{}rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}norm}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{damping}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.85}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{pr}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} PageRank scores (node 0 will be 0)}

{{ $\rightarrow$ spmatrix}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normalize a sparse matrix to stochastic form (column\sphinxhyphen{}stochastic).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Converts an adjacency matrix to a stochastic matrix where each column sums to 1.
This normalization is required for PageRank\sphinxhyphen{}style random walk algorithms.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse adjacency matrix to normalize

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Column\sphinxhyphen{}stochastic sparse matrix where each column sums to 1

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
sp.spmatrix

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Removes self\sphinxhyphen{}loops (sets diagonal to 0) before normalization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Handles zero\sphinxhyphen{}degree nodes by leaving corresponding columns as zeros

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Preserves sparsity structure for memory efficiency

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Hedwig Statistics and Scoring}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:hedwig-statistics-and-scoring}}

\subsubsection{Advanced Visualization}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:advanced-visualization}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specialized visualizations such as hairball and Sankey diagrams.
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.visualization.sankey@\spxentry{py3plex.visualization.sankey}}\index{py3plex.visualization.sankey@\spxentry{py3plex.visualization.sankey}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.visualization.sankey}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sankey diagram visualization for multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer flow visualization to show connection strength
between layers in multilayer networks. The visualization displays flows as arrows
with widths proportional to the number of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note: This uses a simplified flow diagram approach rather than matplotlib’s Sankey
class, as the Sankey class is designed for more complex flow networks and doesn’t
map directly to multilayer network inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections.
\index{draw\_multilayer\_sankey() (in module py3plex.visualization.sankey)@\spxentry{draw\_multilayer\_sankey()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.visualization.sankey}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer flow diagram showing connection strength in multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates a flow visualization where:
\sphinxhyphen{} Each layer is represented in the diagram
\sphinxhyphen{} Flows between layers show the strength (number) of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections
\sphinxhyphen{} Flow width/text indicates the number of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graphs}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs, one per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multilinks}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping edge\_type \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} list of multi\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{labels}} \textendash{} Optional list of layer labels. If None, uses layer indices

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} \textendash{} Matplotlib axes to draw on. If None, creates new figure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{display}} \textendash{} If True, calls plt.show() after drawing. Default is False
to let the caller control rendering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Reserved for future extensions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Matplotlib axes object

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This visualization is most effective for networks with 2\sphinxhyphen{}5 layers.
For networks with many layers, the diagram may become cluttered.
The implementation uses a simplified flow visualization approach.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subsection{Configuration \& Environment}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:configuration-environment}}\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page collects the practical knobs for running py3plex: configuration files, environment variables, supported I/O formats, and common algorithm parameters.


\subsubsection{Configuration Files}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:configuration-files}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex supports configuration files for reproducible workflows. Provide them as YAML or JSON; omit sections you do not need.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network Configuration (YAML):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} network\PYGZus{}config.yaml}
\PYG{n+nt}{network}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{input\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{data/multilayer.edges}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} one of: multiedgelist, edgelist, json, graphml, parquet}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{directed}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{false}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{weighted}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{true}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} field meanings:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} input\PYGZus{}file: path to your dataset}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} input\PYGZus{}type: parser to use (match the file format)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} directed/weighted: toggle graph properties}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load with:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} network.load\PYGZus{}network(**config[\PYGZsq{}network\PYGZsq{}])}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Algorithm Parameters:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} algorithm\PYGZus{}config.yaml}
\PYG{n+nt}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{p}{:}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{42}

\subsubsection{Environment Variables}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:environment-variables}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex respects the following environment variables for customization. Override them in your shell before running scripts or set them in code via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{os.environ}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Directories:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PY3PLEX\_DATA\_DIR}} — Override default data directory location
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}/.py3plex/data}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Used for: Cached datasets, downloaded networks

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PY3PLEX\_CACHE\_DIR}} — Cache directory for computed results
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}/.py3plex/cache}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Used for: Embedding caches, computation results

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance Tuning:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PY3PLEX\_NUM\_WORKERS}} — Suggested number of parallel workers for algorithms
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default recommendation: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{os.cpu\_count()}} when you wire this through to APIs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Effect: only applied by functions/scripts that read the variable

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PY3PLEX\_MEMORY\_LIMIT}} — Optional memory budget for large\sphinxhyphen{}scale operations (in GB)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default: unset (falls back to library defaults)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Effect: honored only by routines that support explicit memory caps

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Setting environment variables:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Linux/macOS}
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PY3PLEX\PYGZus{}DATA\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}/path/to/data\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PY3PLEX\PYGZus{}NUM\PYGZus{}WORKERS}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{8}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Or in Python}
import\PYG{+w}{ }os
os.environ\PYG{o}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}PY3PLEX\PYGZus{}DATA\PYGZus{}DIR\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}/path/to/data\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Debugging and Development:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PY3PLEX\_DEBUG}} — Enable debug mode (verbose output)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Values: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (off), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (on)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PY3PLEX\_PROFILE}} — Enable profiling for performance analysis
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Values: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (off), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (on)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Input Formats}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:input-formats}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supported file formats:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multiedgelist}} — Multilayer edge list format with layer annotations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edgelist}} — Standard edge list (single layer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} — JSON network format produced by py3plex tools

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{graphml}} — GraphML format for interoperability with NetworkX/Gephi

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parquet}} — Apache Parquet for columnar, high\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}} for format details.


\subsubsection{Output Formats}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:output-formats}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Networks can be exported to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pickle (Python serialization)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
JSON

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
CSV/TSV

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
GraphML

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parquet

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/export_serialize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Export and Serialize Networks}}}} for export details.


\subsubsection{Algorithm Configuration}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:algorithm-configuration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Many algorithms accept configuration parameters. The snippets below show common defaults and what each parameter controls.


\paragraph{Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:community-detection}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}louvain}

\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{resolution}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Higher \(\rightarrow\) more, smaller communities}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Inter\PYGZhy{}layer coupling strength}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Node2Vec}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:node2vec}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{wrappers}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{train\PYGZus{}node2vec}

\PYG{n}{embeddings} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{train\PYGZus{}node2vec}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{dimensions}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{128}\PYG{p}{,}      \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Embedding size}
    \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{80}\PYG{p}{,}      \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Steps per walk}
    \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Walks per node}
    \PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}               \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Return parameter (larger discourages backtracking)}
    \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}               \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} In\PYGZhy{}out parameter (smaller explores outward)}
    \PYG{n}{workers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}            \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Parallel workers}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Dynamics}
\label{\detokenize{reference/configuration:dynamics}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}

\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,}            \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Infection probability per contact}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}           \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Recovery probability per step}
    \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Fraction of nodes initially infected (0\textendash{}1)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/algorithm_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Algorithm Roadmap}}}} for complete parameter documentation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Customize visualization; adjust node/edge sizes to match network scale. Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show=False}} for headless rendering:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
