\paragraph{GPU Acceleration (Advanced)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For very large networks with a CUDA\sphinxhyphen{}capable GPU, try GPU acceleration. Keep data sparse to avoid blowing GPU memory and move only the operations that benefit from GPU throughput:

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}
    \PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{cupyx}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{scipy}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{sparse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{csr\PYGZus{}matrix} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{gpu\PYGZus{}csr}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Keep sparse; convert SciPy CSR to CuPy CSR}

    \PYG{n}{gpu\PYGZus{}adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{gpu\PYGZus{}csr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}cpu}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} GPU\PYGZhy{}accelerated sparse matrix operations}

\PYG{k}{except} \PYG{n+ne}{ImportError}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{CuPy not available, using CPU}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Visualization Optimization}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:visualization-optimization}}

\paragraph{Reduce Visual Complexity}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:reduce-visual-complexity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Favor minimal styling for large graphs to avoid overplotting:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For large networks (\PYGZgt{}1000 nodes)}
\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}              \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Tiny nodes}
    \PYG{n}{labels}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{,}             \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} No labels}
    \PYG{n}{edge\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,}            \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Thin edges}
    \PYG{n}{alphalevel}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,}           \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Very transparent}
    \PYG{n}{remove\PYGZus{}isolated\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Remove disconnected}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Save to File Instead of Display}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:save-to-file-instead-of-display}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Don\PYGZsq{}t show interactively (faster)}
\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ax} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subplots}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{figsize}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{8}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Don\PYGZsq{}t show}
    \PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{ax}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save directly to file}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.png}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dpi}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{150}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{bbox\PYGZus{}inches}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{tight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{close}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Free memory}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Use Lower Resolution}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:use-lower-resolution}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{psutil}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{get\PYGZus{}memory\PYGZus{}usage}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Get current memory usage in MB.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{n}{process} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{psutil}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Process}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{getpid}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{process}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{memory\PYGZus{}info}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rss} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1024} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1024}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Memory before loading: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}memory\PYGZus{}usage}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.1f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ MB}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{large\PYGZus{}network.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Memory after loading: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}memory\PYGZus{}usage}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.1f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ MB}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Free Memory When Done}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Delete network when no longer needed}

\paragraph{Use Generators Instead of Lists}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:use-generators-instead-of-lists}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} BAD: Loads all nodes into memory}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} GOOD: Processes nodes one at a time}

    \PYG{n}{process}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{)}

For multiple networks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{gc}

\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}files} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{net1.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{net2.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{net3.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extend with your files}

\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{file} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{enumerate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}files}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Processing }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}files}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}
    \PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute statistics}

    \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Free memory}

    \PYG{n}{gc}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{collect}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save intermediate results every 10 networks}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}results}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{results}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{results\PYGZus{}batch\PYGZus{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.json}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Alternative Tools for Scale}

\paragraph{When py3plex Isn’t Enough}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:when-py3plex-isn-t-enough}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For networks \textgreater{}100k nodes, consider exporting to a faster backend for heavy algorithms and re\sphinxhyphen{}importing results:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{igraph} (C\sphinxhyphen{}based, very fast):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{igraph}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{ig}

\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}multilevel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export back to py3plex if needed}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (via GraphML or edge list)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{graph\sphinxhyphen{}tool} (C++, fastest):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{gt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{minimize\PYGZus{}blockmodel\PYGZus{}dl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}blocks}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Quick Performance Checklist}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:quick-performance-checklist}}

\paragraph{Before Running on Large Network}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:before-running-on-large-network}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
[ ] Enable sparse matrices (automatic for most ops)
[ ] Sample network if \PYGZgt{}10k nodes
[ ] Choose efficient algorithms (degree \PYGZgt{} betweenness)
[ ] Limit visualization detail
[ ] Monitor memory usage
[ ] Use batch processing for multiple networks
[ ] Consider alternative tools if \PYGZgt{}100k nodes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Optimization Order}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:optimization-order}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use sparse matrices} (biggest impact, usually automatic)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Sample network} (if \textgreater{}10k nodes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choose efficient algorithms} (avoid O(n\textasciicircum{}3) operations)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Parallelize} (if multi\sphinxhyphen{}core available)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{GPU acceleration} (only if CUDA GPU available)

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

│                     Nginx (Port 8080)                        │

└───────┬────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
        │                        │
        ▼                        ▼
┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────────────┐
│   Frontend   │         │      FastAPI         │
│ React + Vite │         │  (Port 8000)         │

└──────────────┘         └──────────┬───────────┘
                                    │
                    ┌───────────────┴────────────────┐
                    ▼                                ▼
            ┌──────────────┐                ┌──────────────┐
            │    Redis     │                │    Celery    │
            │  (Port 6379) │◄──────────────│    Worker    │
            │    Broker    │                │  + Flower    │
            └──────────────┘                └──────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼
            ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
            │  Shared Volume: /data            │

            └──────────────────────────────────┘

\paragraph{Local Development Against py3plex}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:local-development-against-py3plex}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex repository root is bind\sphinxhyphen{}mounted read\sphinxhyphen{}only into containers at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/workspace}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} In Dockerfile.api}
\PYG{k}{ARG}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PY3PLEX\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}/workspace
\PYG{k}{RUN}\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{PY3PLEX\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Benefits:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes to py3plex core reflect immediately (no rebuild)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Editable install for development

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Isolated GUI code under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gui/}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Note:} The mount is read\sphinxhyphen{}only to prevent accidental writes from containers.

\subsubsection{Data Formats}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:data-formats}}

\paragraph{Accepted Input Formats}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:accepted-input-formats}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. Edge List (.edgelist, .txt)}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer format: node1 node2 layer weight}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{1} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2} \PYG{n}{social} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{1} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3} \PYG{n}{work} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{2} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3} \PYG{n}{hobby} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Simple format: node1 node2}
\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{n}{B}
\PYG{n}{B} \PYG{n}{C}
\PYG{n}{C} \PYG{n}{D}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use whitespace\sphinxhyphen{}separated columns. Include the layer column for multilayer graphs; omit it for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer files. Weights are optional and default to 1.0 if absent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{2. GML (.gml)}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Graph Modeling Language

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Preserves attributes and metadata

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{3. NetworkX Pickle (.gpickle)}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Native NetworkX serialization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fastest for large graphs

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Production Deployment}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:production-deployment}}

\paragraph{Static Build (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:static-build-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For production, serve pre\sphinxhyphen{}built frontend assets instead of the Vite dev server:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} Modify Dockerfile.frontend to use multi\PYGZhy{}stage build}
\PYG{k}{FROM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{node:20\PYGZhy{}alpine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{AS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{builder}
\PYG{k}{WORKDIR}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/app}
\PYG{k}{COPY}\PYG{+w}{ }frontend/\PYG{+w}{ }.
\PYG{k}{RUN}\PYG{+w}{ }npm\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }npm\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }build

\PYG{k}{FROM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{nginx:alpine}
\PYG{k}{COPY}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{o}{=}builder\PYG{+w}{ }/app/dist\PYG{+w}{ }/usr/share/nginx/html
\PYG{k}{COPY}\PYG{+w}{ }nginx/nginx.conf\PYG{+w}{ }/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Update \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docker\sphinxhyphen{}compose.yml}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nt}{frontend}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{build}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{context}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{.}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{dockerfile}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{Dockerfile.frontend.prod}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Remove dev server volume mounts}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Security Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:security-considerations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CORS allow\_origins}} to specific domains (not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add authentication/authorization middleware

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use HTTPS (add TLS termination in Nginx)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validate file uploads strictly

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set resource limits per user/job

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable Celery task rate limiting

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Current Status}: Development mode \sphinxhyphen{} suitable for local use only. Do not expose to the public internet without proper security hardening.

\subsection{Development Guide}
\label{\detokenize{dev/development_guide:development-guide}}\label{\detokenize{dev/development_guide::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide covers \sphinxstylestrong{development workflows}, \sphinxstylestrong{Makefile commands}, \sphinxstylestrong{testing}, and \sphinxstylestrong{contributing} to py3plex. Keep it handy as your single reference while coding, testing, and writing docs.


\subsubsection{Getting Started}
\label{\detokenize{dev/development_guide:getting-started}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clone the repository and install in development mode. Requirements: Python 3.8+ and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}} is recommended for the shortcuts below. Keep your virtual environment active so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}} uses the same interpreter every time.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Setup development environment (creates .venv)}
make\PYG{+w}{ }setup

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install package in editable mode with dev dependencies}
make\PYG{+w}{ }dev\PYGZhy{}install
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you prefer manual setup, create and activate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.venv}} yourself, then run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip install \sphinxhyphen{}e .{[}dev{]}}} from the repository root. Whichever path you choose, activate the environment before running any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}} target so the same interpreter is used consistently.


\subsubsection{Makefile Commands}
\label{\detokenize{dev/development_guide:makefile-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Makefile provides a streamlined development workflow. Run targets from the repository root with your virtual environment active:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} View all available commands}
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{help}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Environment setup}
make\PYG{+w}{ }setup\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create virtual environment}
make\PYG{+w}{ }dev\PYGZhy{}install\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install in editable mode}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Code quality}
make\PYG{+w}{ }format\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Auto\PYGZhy{}format code}
make\PYG{+w}{ }lint\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run linters}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Testing}
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{test}\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run tests with coverage}
make\PYG{+w}{ }coverage\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Open coverage report}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Documentation}
make\PYG{+w}{ }docs\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build Sphinx documentation}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build \PYGZam{} publish}
make\PYG{+w}{ }clean\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Remove build artifacts}
make\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build distributions}
make\PYG{+w}{ }publish\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Publish to PyPI}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} CI}
make\PYG{+w}{ }ci\PYG{+w}{             }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run full CI checks (format + lint + tests)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Makefile highlights:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.venv/bin/}} tools when available, otherwise falls back to global tools

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Colorized output with clear \sphinxstylestrong{success/warning/error} messages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Works on \sphinxstylestrong{Linux} and \sphinxstylestrong{macOS}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make ci}} is the superset; use it before pushing. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make format}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make lint}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make test}} for quicker local loops during development.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Testing}
\label{\detokenize{dev/development_guide:testing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Start with the Makefile target, then drill down with pytest as needed. Favor deterministic seeds for generators so results are reproducible. Use narrow targets while iterating, then run the full suite.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Recommended: run all tests with coverage}
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{test}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Equivalent pytest invocations}
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pytest\PYG{+w}{ }tests/\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}v
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pytest\PYG{+w}{ }tests/\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}cov\PYG{o}{=}py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}cov\PYGZhy{}report\PYG{o}{=}html

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run a specific test module or node}
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pytest\PYG{+w}{ }tests/test\PYGZus{}core.py\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}k\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}degree\PYGZdq{}}
python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }pytest\PYG{+w}{ }tests/test\PYGZus{}core.py::test\PYGZus{}degree\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} single test}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The coverage HTML report is written to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{htmlcov/index.html}}.

\paragraph{Documentation Style Guide}
\label{\detokenize{dev/development_guide:documentation-style-guide}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When contributing to documentation, follow these conventions for consistency:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Naming Conventions:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use “Quickstart” (one word) instead of “Quick Start” or “Quickstart Guide”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use “multilayer” (no hyphen) consistently, not “multi\sphinxhyphen{}layer” or “multi layer”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use short, direct section titles without boilerplate

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tone and Structure:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Write first paragraphs that directly explain why the reader is on this page

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Avoid boilerplate like “This chapter will introduce…” or “In this section, you will learn…”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Start with concrete examples rather than abstract explanations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When relevant, point readers to clear paths for different audiences (new users, experienced users, advanced users) so they can skip to what they need

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Code Examples:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All code examples must include:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Imports} — Always show required imports

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network creation} — Build a tiny example network from scratch or via helper

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Core operation} — Run one focused operation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output} — Show what the user should see

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example structure:}

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}statistics} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mls}

\subsection{Architecture and Design}
\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture:architecture-and-design}}\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This document describes the \sphinxstylestrong{system architecture}, \sphinxstylestrong{design patterns}, and \sphinxstylestrong{extension points} of py3plex. It explains how the layers fit together, what each layer owns, and where to plug in new capabilities without leaking responsibilities across layers.


\subsubsection{System Overview}
\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture:system-overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex uses a \sphinxstylestrong{modular, layered architecture} with explicit boundaries. Higher layers depend on lower ones, never the reverse; data flows downward for computation and back upward for presentation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│          High\PYGZhy{}Level Interfaces (Wrappers)           │
│  node2vec\PYGZus{}embedding, benchmark\PYGZus{}nodes                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Algorithms Layer                        │
│  ┌──────────────┬───────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Community   │  Statistics   │  Multilayer     │ │
│  │  Detection   │               │  Algorithms     │ │
│  └──────────────┴───────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            Visualization Layer                       │
│  ┌──────────────┬───────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Multilayer  │  Drawing      │  Layout         │ │
│  │  Plots       │  Machinery    │  Algorithms     │ │
│  └──────────────┴───────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                Core Layer                            │
│  ┌──────────────┬───────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  multinet    │  Parsers      │  Converters     │ │
│  │  (MultiLayer │               │                 │ │
│  │   Network)   │               │                 │ │
│  └──────────────┴───────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           NetworkX Foundation                        │
│  MultiDiGraph, MultiGraph, Algorithms                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reading the diagram:} NetworkX primitives sit at the base. The core layer wraps them in a multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}aware data model. Algorithms, visualization, and wrappers build on that model and never mutate it implicitly; wrappers orchestrate complete tasks while delegating computation to the lower layers.


\subsubsection{Architectural Layers}
\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture:architectural-layers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each layer has a narrow contract: the core encodes data, algorithms consume that encoding, visualization renders results, and wrappers orchestrate complete tasks. When extending py3plex, start from the lowest layer you need and only depend upward.

\begin{itemize}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{core\_network}} \sphinxhyphen{} Underlying NetworkX graph

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Encoding Scheme and Invariants:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are represented as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer)}} tuples in Python.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When serialized to flat text (files, labels), tuples are joined with the delimiter: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{node\_id\}\{delimiter\}\{layer\}"}}. Avoid using the delimiter inside raw IDs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer names are mapped to integers in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_name\_map}} for stable ordering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{core\_network}} stays a NetworkX \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiGraph}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiDiGraph}}; avoid injecting derived attributes that are not part of the graph definition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{coupling\_weight}} unless explicitly weighted; modifying coupling should clear related caches.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any mutation (adding/removing nodes, relabeling layers) should invalidate cached matrices or embeddings.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Data Flow}
\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture:data-flow}}

\paragraph{Typical Workflow}
\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture:typical-workflow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex workflows follow a predictable sequence: load \(\rightarrow\) compute \(\rightarrow\) analyze \(\rightarrow\) visualize \(\rightarrow\) export. Each step uses the layer beneath it and should avoid mutating lower layers unless explicitly intended.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input:} Load or create network, keeping encoding consistent

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.graphml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{graphml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Processing:} Apply algorithms against the core graph without re\sphinxhyphen{}encoding

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{best\PYGZus{}partition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{centrality} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{calc}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Extension Points}
\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture:extension-points}}

\paragraph{Custom Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture:custom-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add new algorithms by following existing patterns (pure functions returning dictionaries or NetworkX objects). Keep inputs typed as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} to reuse encoding and caching, and avoid mutating the passed network unless the function is explicitly transformative. Document input assumptions (directed vs. undirected, weighted vs. unweighted) and expose new callables in the relevant package \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_init\_\_}} when you want them importable by name.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Custom centrality measure.}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Parameters}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    network : multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}

\PYG{l+s+sd}{    Returns}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    dict}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{        Node centrality scores}
\PYG{l+s+sd}{    \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}
    \PYG{n}{centrality} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use sparse representations for large networks; the threshold is configurable in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config.py}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{sparse} \PYG{o+ow}{or} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{SPARSE\PYGZus{}THRESHOLD}\PYG{p}{:}
